entry.title: Research Summary: July 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.
entry.content:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.

entry.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Tang, Gangqiang Cao, Yurou Liu, Yuliang Zhan, Xiaochong Lan, Yifan Li, Yuchen Yan, Han Peng, Zican Dong, Zhenduo Zhang, Tianshu Wang, Xinyu Kong, Zujie Wen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Ring-Zero scales zero reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model to study large-scale training dynamics and emergent reasoning, addressing naive scaling problems like poor readability, token redundancy, and inflexible reasoning depth. It introduces a stable, efficient pipeline with algorithmic and systems optimizations including clipping strategies. It pushes zero-RL reasoning to an unprecedented scale.

entry.title: A Shared Subcircuit Lets LLMs Count Down Across Tasks

author.name: Jacob Dunefsky, Wes Gurnee, Emmanuel Ameisen

entry.summary: This mechanistic-interpretability study identifies a reusable countdown subcircuit inside Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct that tracks how many tokens remain before a target length across tasks like fixed-length sentences, DNA codon endings, and ASCII tables. The authors characterize the geometric representation the circuit uses to estimate remaining positions. It matters as evidence that models reuse general-purpose internal machinery across superficially different tasks.

entry.title: Thompson Sampling Is 2-Competitive for Mistakes

author.name: Mark Sellke, Gregory Valiant

entry.summary: This theory paper proves Thompson sampling incurs at most twice the expected number of suboptimal-arm selections of any policy for Bayesian bandits with independent, rest-only-evolving arms. This confirms a 2014 conjecture of Guha and Munagala with a tight factor of two. It provides a clean competitive-ratio guarantee for a widely used algorithm.

entry.title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models

author.name: Yubo Wang, Jiarong Liang, Yuxuan Zhang, Xuye Liu, Cong Wei, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training for coding agents, arguing that an agent action-observation-continuation loop is structurally the same as a function call site available at internet scale in ordinary code. It masks functions selected by program dependency graph analysis under a complexity-inferability criterion and mid-trains an open coding model to better integrate tool returns into reasoning.

entry.title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud

author.name: B\'alint Gyevn\'ar, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Nihar B. Shah

entry.summary: Introduces and empirically evaluates indirect data poisoning as a threat to scientific integrity, where adversaries corrupt public datasets that autonomous research agents unknowingly ingest and propagate. It argues AI-automated science could industrialize scientific fraud at scale.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: Unified Embodied Synthesis with World Foundation Model

author.name: Xinghang Li, Jun Guo, Qiwei Li, Long Qian, Hang Lai, Yueze Wang, Hongyu Yan, Jiahang Cao, Xi Chen, Jingen Qu, Jiaxi Song, Nan Sun, Hanye Zhao, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Caoyu Xia, Jack Zhao, Diyun Xiang, Hangjun Ye, Heng Qu, Huaping Liu, Jason Li

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 is a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive model that treats embodied generation as an extension of foundation image and video generation, jointly optimizing text-to-image, editing, embodied scene generation, embodied transfer, and embodied video generation. It matters as a large industry effort to build a unified world foundation model for robotics.

entry.title: Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success

author.name: Samuel Yeh, Yiwen Zhu, Shaleen Deep, Sharon Li

entry.summary: The paper addresses unsupervised failure attribution for LLM agent systems, training only on successful trajectories to identify which step caused a failure at inference time. This avoids expensive step-level error annotations and prompting pipelines, making debugging of agentic systems more scalable.

entry.title: Extractable Memorization From First Principles

author.name: A. Feder Cooper, Marika Swanberg, Jamie Hayes, Lea Duesterwald, Christopher De Sa, Daniel E. Ho, Mark A. Lemley, Percy Liang

entry.summary: This paper reframes extractable memorization in LLMs from first principles, arguing valid extraction claims require matched comparison of generation probabilities between training and comparable non-training sequences to distinguish memorization from mere predictability. Authors include prominent researchers spanning ML, law, and policy. It clarifies methodology in a contested legally relevant area.

entry.title: Language Identification with Succinct Machine-Independent Traces

author.name: Moses Charikar, Jon Kleinberg, Chirag Pabbaraju

entry.summary: Motivated by LLMs, this paper studies Gold-Angluin language identification when learners are given succinct machine-independent computational traces or annotations, akin to commented code or chain-of-thought. It proves positive identifiability results that circumvent classic negative results. It offers a theoretical lens on why annotated training data helps learning.

entry.title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models

author.name: Bryan Kelly, Semyon Malamud, Johannes Schwab, Teng Andrea Xu

entry.summary: This work builds point-in-time language models trained only on text available up to each calendar date to eliminate lookahead bias that invalidates financial and social-science backtests. Scaling decoder-only transformers to 4B parameters on 1T chronologically filtered FineWeb tokens narrows the performance gap to unconstrained models, with monthly checkpoints. It matters for causally valid empirical research.

entry.title: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Zhixi Cai, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, Shiwen Ni, Qinghao Zhang

entry.summary: A carefully controlled study finds that GRPO reinforcement learning fails to add skill to small (4-8B) language and vision-language web agents beyond a strong supervised baseline, and can make text agents worse at high learning rates. It analyzes the mechanism as learning-rate-gated reshaping rather than genuine capability gain.

entry.title: CDFM: Towards a General-Purpose Causal Discovery Foundation Model

author.name: Jie Qiao, Ruichu Cai, Zijian Li, Weilin Chen, Pengfei Hua, Boyan Xu, Zhengming Chen, Zhifeng Hao, Peng Cui

entry.summary: CDFM aims to build a general-purpose causal discovery foundation model that unifies the fragmented, mechanism-specific algorithm landscape into a single framework that scales across heterogeneous datasets. It matters because a working foundation model for causal structure recovery would be significant for scientific discovery.

entry.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Tiberiu Musat, Tiago Pimentel, Nicolas Zucchet, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves that for a generalized class of inductive reasoning tasks (unifying in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning), the training dynamics of attention models can be confined to a low-dimensional interpretable invariant manifold captured by a handful of coordinates. It matters for making Transformer learning dynamics analytically tractable.

entry.title: The Computational Basis of Confidence in Large Language Models

author.name: Dharshan Kumaran, Viorica Patraucean, Maks Ovsanikov, Petar Veli\v{c}kovi\'c, Nathaniel Daw

entry.summary: Using a normative statistical-decision-confidence framework from computational neuroscience, this DeepMind-affiliated work asks what an LLM confidence signal actually represents, testing whether answer-logit differences encode a Bayesian latent decision variable or a non-Bayesian heuristic. It probes the computational basis rather than mere calibration. It matters for trustworthy deployment and interpretability.

entry.title: Let RGB Be the Language of Vision

author.name: Timing Yang, Jinrui Yang, Xinlong Li, Yuhan Wang, Haoran Li, Yanqing Liu, Guoyizhe Wei, Jixuan Ying, Chen Wei, Rama Chellappa, Yuyin Zhou, Cihang Xie, Alan Yuille, Feng Wang

entry.summary: RINO proposes a unified formulation where diverse visual signals such as masks and depth maps are all represented as RGB images, casting general vision tasks as a common RGB-to-RGB image editing problem handled by a single backbone. This creates a unified visual interface analogous to how language models operate over text.

entry.title: Hy-Embodied-VLM-1.0: Efficient Physical-World Agents

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Xumin Yu, Yongming Rao, Yonggen Ling, Yunheng Li, Oran Wang, Mingqi Gao, Yuchen Zhou, Yves Liang, Zuyan Liu, Yani Zhang, Rui Huang, Xiaoran Xu, Bowen Yuan, Yifu Yuan, Xu Tan, He Zhang, Yufei Huang, Shenghao Zhang, Hongsheng Wu, Han Hu, Zhengyou Zhang

entry.summary: A technical report introducing an efficient embodied vision-language foundation model organized around an action-centric capability taxonomy spanning state understanding, transition reasoning, and sequential adaptive reasoning. Includes a systematic data pipeline for physical-world agents.

entry.title: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yaowen Ye, Jacob Steinhardt

entry.summary: This work studies norm-enforcement mechanisms for language-model agents in competitive shared environments, showing that simple enforcement is exploited by misaligned agents for advantage even without explicit training to do so. It then develops more robust enforcement to shape multi-agent behavior toward collective good.

entry.title: Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering

author.name: Shijie Wang, Honglu Zhou, Ziyang Wang, Ran Xu, Caiming Xiong, Silvio Savarese, Chen Sun, Juan Carlos Niebles

entry.summary: This paper introduces Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering, requiring models to output both a semantic answer and precise spatio-temporal evidence as tracked object segmentation masklets, and provides ST-Evidence, a human-verified pixel-level grounding benchmark. It matters for making video LLM answers verifiable rather than black-box.

entry.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations

author.name: Xixuan Hao, Zeyu Zhang, Zehao Lin, Yihang Sun, Ziliang Guo, Xichong Zhang, Yuxuan Liang, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li

entry.summary: MemOps introduces a benchmark that evaluates memory as a dynamic lifecycle of operations rather than only final answer correctness in long-horizon multi-session conversations. It distinguishes failure causes such as missing fact introduction, wrong-target binding, and reliance on stale values after corrections.

entry.title: To Answer or to Abstain: Mitigating Search-Agent Hallucinations via Abstention-Aware Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fengji Zhang, Tianyu Fan, Yuxiang Zheng, Xinyao Niu, Chengen Huang, Jacky Keung, Bei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes abstention-aware reinforcement learning for search-augmented LLM agents that dynamically shapes abstention rewards to penalize fabricated answers when retrieval fails, rather than only rewarding correct answers. It introduces a metric to capture the capability-reliability trade-off.

entry.title: VIA: Visual Interface Agent for Robot Control

author.name: Hengyuan Hu, Priya Sundaresan, Jensen Gao, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: Proposes controlling robots through visual software interfaces using frontier foundation models rather than fine-tuning smaller vision-language-action models on limited robot data. It leverages foundation models' growing ability to operate software via visual interfaces to overcome VLA capacity limits.

entry.title: Extending LLM Context via Associative Recurrent Memory

author.name: Gleb Kuzmin, Ivan Rodkin, Aydar Bulatov, Yuri Kuratov, Lyudmila Rvanova, Mikhail Katkov, Ilia Sochenkov, Misha Tsodyks, Timothy Baldwin, Mikhail Burtsev, Artem Shelmanov

entry.summary: This paper develops training recipes and domain-specific datasets to extend LLM context using the Associative Recurrent Memory Transformer, giving constant-memory scaling for long-context processing. It matters as a practical alternative to quadratic-attention context extension for narrow-domain workloads.

entry.title: Mathematics of Data Science

author.name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Amit Singer, Thomas Strohmer

entry.summary: This is a textbook on the mathematical foundations of data science covering high-dimensional phenomena, SVD/PCA, regression, spectral clustering, dimension reduction, optimization, deep learning, concentration of measure, compressive sensing, and low-rank recovery. It matters as an educational reference from prominent applied mathematicians.

entry.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling

author.name: Roi Cohen, Yvan Carr\'e, Nick Lechtenb\"orger, Hendrik Droste, Lucas Kerschke, Russa Biswas, Gerard de Melo, Jan Buys

entry.summary: Knowledgeless Language Models are pretrained on corpora with anonymized named entities to remove entity-linked factual supervision, shifting models away from parametric recall toward evidence-grounded reasoning. This reduces closed-book factual recall while often improving performance on tasks where relevant evidence is provided in context. It proposes a distinct epistemic training paradigm.

entry.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context

author.name: Yanzhe Zhang, Sanmi Koyejo, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: This work shows that aggregate accuracy hides significant per-example instability in LLMs under task-irrelevant context, where even meaningless pseudo-words flip predictions on a fraction of examples in both directions. Aggregate stability masks this fragility, which holds across many models. It argues robustness must be assessed at the per-example level.

entry.title: Can risk aversion learned at low stakes generalize to astronomically high stakes?

author.name: Elliott Thornley

entry.summary: Summarizes a paper introducing RiskAverseOOD, a benchmark measuring whether risk aversion in resources learned at low stakes generalizes to astronomically high stakes as a potential misalignment failsafe. Finds partial generalization, with cooperation rates rising from about 2 percent to roughly 39 to 70 percent depending on the training method.

entry.title: Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits

author.name: Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: Arthur Conmy replicates and extends work showing that distilling from a teacher model into a base student transfers behavioral traits, and that filtering out prompts mentioning the trait does not reliably prevent transfer. He demonstrates the phenomenon cheaply without a frontier SFT pipeline, transferring negative emotion, agentic misalignment, and censorship across Gemma, Qwen, Nemotron, and Llama base models, releasing all weights and code.

entry.title: Proxy Exploration and Reusable Guidance: A Modular LLM Post-Training Paradigm via Proxy-Guided Update Signals

author.name: Daocheng Fu, Rong Wu, Yu Yang, Xuemeng Yang, Jianbiao Mei, Licheng Wen, Pinlong Cai, Yong Liu, Botian Shi, Yu Qiao

entry.summary: PUST is an LLM post-training framework that decouples reward exploration from distribution alignment by using a lightweight proxy model to discover high-reward update signals that can be reused and transferred across models. It matters for making post-training cheaper and more modular by avoiding expensive exploration on the primary model.

entry.title: Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming

author.name: Xutao Mao, Xiang Zheng, Cong Wang

entry.summary: AHA is an automated red-teaming loop that uses one agentic research environment to discover reusable vulnerability knowledge about production LLM agents by proposing falsifiable vulnerability hypotheses, building falsifiers, and instantiating attacks. It matters because it targets the enabling conditions of unsafe agent behavior rather than just attack success artifacts.

entry.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias

author.name: Zixiang Xu, Sixian Li, Huaxing Liu, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Zirui Song, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: This paper gives a mechanistic-interpretability account of LLM-as-judge bias, showing across seven judges and seven bias types that biased inputs are displaced along low-dimensional, type-specific subspaces in hidden states, and that steering along these subspaces causally controls bias. It matters for representation-level detection and mitigation of judging bias.

entry.title: Length Penalties Make Chain-of-Thought Less Monitorable

author.name: Bryce Little

entry.summary: The paper shows that length-penalized reinforcement learning shortens chain-of-thought while still allowing hidden influences to steer answers, so a biasing hint keeps driving outputs even as it is mentioned far less in the trace. It warns that token-accuracy evaluations would falsely count these compressed, less-monitorable runs as successful.

entry.title: Remembering Distinct Items, Not Tokens: A Learnable Dirichlet-Process Cache Between State-Space Models and Attention

author.name: Siddharth Pal, Viktoria Rojkova

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse key-value cache that allocates a memory slot only when an input is novel, using the DP-means clustering rule (small-variance Dirichlet-process limit) as the memory operator between state-space models and full attention. Memory then scales with the number of distinct items rather than tokens.

entry.title: World Models as Adversaries: Multi-Agent Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Robust Motion Planning

author.name: Tong Nie, Yuewen Mei, Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Jian Sun, Wei Ma

entry.summary: Frames adversarially robust motion planning for autonomous vehicles as a constrained min-max game solved via multi-agent self-play fine-tuning, treating world models as adversaries. It provides a decoupled solver to avoid external scenario generators for training on rare safety-critical events.

entry.title: Action Map Policy: Learning 3D Closed-loop Manipulation via Pixel Classification

author.name: Haojie Huang, Zhang Ye, Linfeng Zhao, Boce Hu, Mingxi Jia, Yu Qi, Ahmed Agha, Dian Wang, Robert Platt, Robin Walters

entry.summary: Casts 3D closed-loop robot manipulation policy learning as pixel-space classification by projecting 3D actions onto camera image planes, avoiding vocabulary explosion from naive action discretization. It aims to handle high-dimensional, long-horizon, multi-modal action spaces.

entry.title: Multi-Agent LLMs Fail to Explore Each Other

author.name: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Jiatong Li, Wendi Li, Xin Eric Wang, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agents fail to explore each other effectively in multi-agent interactions, exhibiting myopic and polarized patterns that harm coordination, formalized as a multi-agent exploration problem in a partially observable stochastic game. It introduces a lightweight contextual-exploration framework to promote probing of peers' capabilities.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Comprehensive Cardiac CT Segmentation and Phenotyping: Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation, Vision Foundation Model Development, Multicenter Evaluation and Clinical Validation

author.name: Pooya Mohammadi Kazaj, Leo Fridolin Weber, Wen Xie, Seyed Amir Ahmad Safavi-Naini, Anselm Stark, Giovanni Baj, Ali Mokhtari, Toshiya Yoshida, Christoph Ryffel, Taishi Okuno, Yoshihiro Akashi, Ronny R. Buechel, Thomas Pilgrim, Waldo Valenzuela, George C. M. Siontis, Xiaowei Xu, Moritz Hundertmark, Stephan Windecker, Christoph Grani, Isaac Shiri

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for comprehensive cardiac CT segmentation and phenotyping combining a human-in-the-loop annotation pipeline, a CT augmentation technique, and a self-supervised foundation model pre-trained on 60,000 unlabeled scans. It assembles a large expert-annotated dataset of 1,598 cases across 14 structures with multicenter external validation.

entry.title: Beyond Sally-Anne: Evaluating Theory of Mind in LLMs using Epistemic Schelling Points

author.name: Roberta Rocca, Sami Boukortt, Geoff Keeling, Winnie Street

entry.summary: Introduces a two-player dialogue game that benchmarks theory of mind in LLMs by requiring model dyads to independently converge on semantic Schelling points under varying epistemic transparency, avoiding the gameable nature of Sally-Anne style tests. It reveals a significant capability gap in robust, generalizable theory-of-mind reasoning.

entry.title: See like a Robot: Robot-Centric Pointmaps for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Byungkun Lee, Dongyoon Hwang, Dongjin Kim, Hojoon Lee, Minho Park, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: This work introduces robot-centric pointmaps for vision-language-action models, storing per-pixel 3D coordinates in the robot frame to fix the mismatch between camera-frame observation and robot-frame actions. It matters because resolving this frame mismatch could improve cross-viewpoint generalization for VLA policies trained on heterogeneous datasets.

entry.title: MM-ToolSandBox: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Visual Tool-Calling Agents

author.name: Kaixin Ma, Di Feng, Alexander Metz, Jiarui Lu, Eshan Verma, Afshin Dehghan

entry.summary: MM-ToolSandBox is a benchmark and stateful evaluation framework for visually grounded tool-calling agents, spanning 500-plus tools across 16 domains with multi-image, multi-turn tasks and realistic conversational phenomena, evaluating twelve state-of-the-art models. It matters for rigorously measuring visual agentic tool use.

entry.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Areeb Gani, Jacqueline Lu, Jordan Thomas, Mark Steyvers, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive survey of metacognition for large language models, taxonomizing current knowledge and analyzing when and how LLMs can exhibit or be endowed with metacognitive abilities to improve capability, reliability, and transparency. It matters as a structuring reference for an increasingly recognized aspect of capable AI.

entry.title: The Sound of Absence: Audio-Language Embedding Models Struggle with Negation

author.name: Chun-Yi Kuan, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: The paper shows audio-language embedding models like CLAP largely ignore negation, mapping affirmative and negated captions to near-identical vectors. It introduces NegEval-Audio with retrieval and multiple-choice negation tasks, finding accuracy falling below chance under negation on AudioCaps and Clotho. It exposes a systematic blind spot in multimodal audio understanding.

entry.title: LLMs Can See the Smoke but not the Fire: Evaluating Abductive Reasoning with Elenchos

author.name: Julius Steiglechner, Lucas Mahler, Gabriele Lohmann

entry.summary: Elenchos is a generative evaluation framework measuring LLM abductive reasoning as a structural inverse problem, asking models to detect whether a formal system like lambda-calculus has been mutated and to infer the responsible rule changes. Frontier and mid-tier models show a detection-attribution dissociation, spotting effects but failing to identify causes. It probes a poorly understood reasoning capability.

entry.title: Accelerated Mixing Time of Randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

author.name: Siddharth Mitra, Vishwak Srinivasan, Xiuyuan Wang, Andre Wibisono

entry.summary: The paper proves Randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo achieves accelerated mixing for sampling log-concave distributions under a Talagrand inequality, using random integration times from triangular or exponential distributions. It shows exponentially fast KL convergence with favorable dependence on condition number. It advances the theory of gradient-based sampling.

entry.title: Less Experts, Faster Decoding: Cost-Aware Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jincheng Xie, Runheng Liu, Heyan Huang, Yawen Ling, Hanbin Dai, Yu Zheng, Wen Hu

entry.summary: This paper observes that confidence-driven speculative decoding in large MoE models can cause expert scattering, where accepted draft tokens route to disjoint experts and increase memory traffic, eroding speedups. It proposes cost-aware draft selection that accounts for the union of experts activated during verification, not just acceptance likelihood. It improves inference efficiency for sparse MoE LLMs.

entry.title: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills for Self-Improving LLM Agents

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Ziyuan Li, Wei Qiu, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: The paper argues evaluation metrics for self-improving agents can themselves be evolved, searching compositions of small drawback detectors under an evolutionary lifecycle anchored to a small reference set and audited on held-out anchors. It targets settings where no reliable metric exists to guide skill evolution.

entry.title: MobileSAM2: Lightweight Segment Anything for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Kai Jiang, Jiaxing Huang, Jingyi Zhang, Weiying Xie, Yunsong Li, Yufei Wang, Aoran Xiao, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: MobileSAM2 distills the heavyweight video foundation segmentation model SAM2 into a lightweight model for mobile devices using Hypergraphical Knowledge Distillation with temporal and granularity components. It targets segment-anything capability on resource-constrained hardware for images and videos.

entry.title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning

author.name: Krischan Braitsch, Laura K. Schmalbrock, Theresa Weltermann, Andrew F. Berdel, Isabella Miller, Kai Tran, Michael Heider, Sabrina Kraus, Florian Bassermann, Jacqueline Lammert, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Marcus Makowski, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem

entry.summary: This work builds an agentic evaluation in hematologic oncology where models must proactively request clinical data across three rounds before diagnosing, testing information-seeking rather than static knowledge. Across 32 frontier models the best reaches only 68% accuracy, and information utilization, the strongest predictor of accuracy, collapses in the final round, leaving critical molecular data unexamined.

entry.title: Unlocking Parallelism in Autoregressive Language Models via Speculative Decoding with Progressive Tree Drafting

author.name: Zipeng Gao, Zhi Zheng, Qingrong Xia, Junda Lin, Ziwei Zhao, Tong Xu, Zhefeng Wang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes progressive tree drafting for speculative decoding that generates drafts within the target model itself using a structured parallel drafting strategy with stepwise pruning. It aims to accelerate LLM inference without separate draft modules and their overhead.

entry.title: EquiFusion: Kinematics-Agnostic Human Motion Prediction via Equivariant Latent Diffusion

author.name: Cecilia Curreli, Florian Hofherr, Dominik Muhle, Abhishek Saroha, Riccardo Marin, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Introduces a kinematics-agnostic latent diffusion model with a permutation-equivariant architecture for stochastic 3D human motion prediction, treating skeleton connectivity as an explicit input rather than hard-coded. This enables cross-dataset training and zero-shot prediction on unseen kinematics.

entry.title: A Minimalist Retargeting-Guided Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yunhai Feng, Natalie Leung, Jiaxuan Wang, Lujie Yang, Haozhi Qi, Preston Culbertson

entry.summary: REGRIND is a minimalist retargeting-guided reinforcement learning pipeline that learns dexterous manipulation from a single human demonstration by retargeting hand-object motion to a robot reference and training a residual RL policy to track object-centric keypoints. It matters for extending the successful humanoid retargeting recipe to contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution

author.name: Junjie Yin, Xinyu Feng

entry.summary: This paper proposes task-aware execution-scope estimation so agents judge task difficulty and the shortest reliable path before committing budget, formalizing minimum-sufficient execution and an Agent Cognitive Redundancy Ratio. The E3 method estimates an operating point, executes a minimal path, and expands only as needed.

entry.title: TrustVLA: Mechanism-Guided Inference-Time Defense Against Vision-Language-Action Backdoors

author.name: Pinhan Fu, Xianda Guo, Xuetao Li, Wenke Huang, Ruilin Wang, Weiheng Zhao, Wei Sui, Mang Ye

entry.summary: Studies backdoor attacks on vision-language-action models and proposes TrustVLA, an inference-time defense that identifies a recurring internal mechanism, a compact causal footprint of a small visual trigger support, to detect and recover behavior without retraining. Evaluated against two distinct VLA attacks.

entry.title: The Verifier is the Curriculum: Execution-Gated Self-Distillation for Cross-Family Game Generation

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Qiliang Jiang, Shuning Wu, Xu Zhou

entry.summary: This paper post-trains a code generator using a deterministic, ungameable filter (whether a generated project launches cleanly under a headless engine) instead of a learned judge, then applies rejection-sampling self-distillation. A 14B model raises clean generation on unseen game families from 8.8% to 42.2% and reaches full best-of-K coverage over three rounds.

entry.title: Pix2Act: Image-Space Manipulation Policies with Equivariant Augmentation

author.name: Haojie Huang, Linfeng Zhao, Haotian Liu, Zhang Ye, Si-Yuan Huang, Mingxi Jia, Boce Hu, Fangzhou Lin, Yu Qi, Dian Wang, Robin Walters, Robert Platt

entry.summary: Introduces an imitation-learning manipulation method that represents 3D actions as continuous 2D image-space keypoint trajectories recovered to end-effector poses via triangulation, aligning observations and actions in the same coordinate space to enable equivariant augmentation. It reduces high-dimensional 3D control to a more learnable 2D prediction problem.

entry.title: LightMem-Ego: Your AI Memory for Everyday Life

author.name: Yijun Chen, Boyi Xiao, Yixian Zhao, Haoting Xia, Buqiang Xu, Jizhan Fang, Yanya Li, Yaqi Zheng, Xuehai Wang, Zirui Xue, Liuxin Zhang, Hui Li, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: LightMem-Ego is a lightweight streaming multimodal memory system for wearable AI assistants that captures egocentric video and audio, aligns them on a shared timeline, and organizes them into current, short-term, and long-term tiers with query-dependent retrieval routing. It matters because on-device long-term multimodal memory is a key bottleneck for personal assistants.

entry.title: Heuristic Learning for Active Flow Control Using Coding Agents

author.name: Paul Garnier, Jonathan Viquerat, Elie Hachem

entry.summary: This paper uses modern coding agents to search directly for explicit, executable feedback laws for active flow control instead of training black-box neural policies, yielding interpretable controllers via an iterative propose-evaluate-revise loop. It matters as an example of LLM coding agents producing interpretable control policies in physics-heavy domains.

entry.title: What Does a Temporal Benchmark Score Measure? Decomposing Channel Use in Video VLM Evaluation

author.name: Farrukh Rahman

entry.summary: This work argues temporal video QA scores conflate whether a question is truly temporal with whether a model reads order from pixels versus positional encoding. It proposes a label-free reversal-drop screen to isolate the channel the model uses. The analysis reframes how temporal understanding benchmarks should be validated.

entry.title: LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes

author.name: Louis Sharrock, Lachlan Astfalck, Henry Moss

entry.summary: LatentFlow is a training-free, neural-approximation-free framework for conditioning stochastic processes by writing the process as a deterministic transform of a tractable latent innovation, reducing process-level conditioning to latent-space inference. It handles non-linear observations, non-Gaussian likelihoods, and global constraints uniformly. It generalizes bespoke conditioning constructions.

entry.title: Watermark Forensics for Generative Models: An Information-Theoretic Perspective

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zheng Gao, Xiaoyan Feng, Jiaojiao Jiang, Yulei Sui, Jiankun Hu

entry.summary: This work analyzes watermark forensics for generative models through an information-theoretic lens, defining a forensic ladder of detection, attribution, extraction, and localization and quantifying each rung's cost in sample length via a per-token information profile. It formalizes what different watermark capabilities require. It provides theoretical foundations for provenance beyond simple detection.

entry.title: ACID: Adaptive Caching for vIDeo generation

author.name: Om Agrawal, Saurabh Agarwal, Aditya Akella

entry.summary: ACID accelerates video diffusion generation by making the caching drift threshold adaptive across denoising steps rather than constant, identifying critical timesteps where model reuse harms quality. It argues the apparent speed-quality tradeoff is an artifact of a fixed threshold.

entry.title: WanToFight: Real-Time Generative Game Engine for Multi-Player Combat Interaction

author.name: Li Hu, Guangyuan Wang, Peng Zhang, Bang Zhang

entry.summary: WanToFight is a generative game engine that simulates real-time two-player fighting-game combat from keyboard input, built on a small video diffusion transformer with a streaming autoregressive generator, a player association module, and gated keyboard injection. It jointly addresses multi-player control, real-time inference, and adversarial interaction not handled together before.

entry.title: AVSCap: Orchestrating Audio-Visual Synergy for Omni-modal Video Captioning

author.name: Yanghai Wang, Jiahao Wang, Jiafu Tang, Yuanxing Zhang, Zhe Cao, Hanyan Bian, Zijie Zhang, Weiliang Luo, Zhiyu Pan, Zixuan Dong, Jiaheng Liu, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a framework for omni-modal video captioning that explicitly binds visual actions, speech, music, and sound effects rather than treating audio and video as loosely coupled. Contributes a 130K tri-modal training corpus built via a decoupled-then-fused pipeline.

entry.title: UniMedSeg: Unified In-Context Learning for Multi-Paradigm 2D/3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yunzhou Li, Jiesi Hu, Yanwu Yang, Hanyang Peng, Chenfei Ye, Jianfeng Cao, Yixuan Yuan, Ting Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a unified transformer segmentation framework that jointly handles in-context, interactive, and language-guided prompting across both 2D and 3D medical images. Aims to break the fragmentation that isolates paradigm-specific and dimension-specific models.

entry.title: ExToken: Structured Exploration for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Fine-tuning

author.name: Yilun Kong, Yunpeng Qing, Guozheng Ma, Haoyu Wang, Li Shen, Zhi Hou, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Proposes using optical flow as a unified, video-native action representation for world action models, in a dual-stream diffusion framework that shares the RGB video format while encoding rich per-pixel displacement for control. Aims to bridge pretrained video generators and action prediction.

entry.title: Causal Graphs, Markov Properties and Do-calculus for Stochastic Differential Equations

author.name: Philip Boeken, Joris M. Mooij

entry.summary: Develops graphical causal models for stochastic differential equations, establishing solvability conditions for well-defined observational and interventional distributions and proving a sigma-separation Markov property and do-calculus in terms of the system's causal graph at the level of sample paths.

entry.title: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Mianqiu Huang, Taofeng Xue, Chong Peng, Jinrui Ding, Sicheng Fan, Jiale Hong, Yufei Gao, Xiaocheng Zhang, Linsen Guo, Xin Yang, Dengchang Zhao, Yuchen Xie, Peng Pei, Xunliang Xie, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: EvoCUA-1.5 extends self-evolving computer-use agents from offline experience learning to online reinforcement learning in executable sandbox environments, improving from verifiable task outcomes on long-horizon multimodal desktop tasks. It adapts single-turn language-RL recipes to handle multi-turn context management and changing action spaces.

entry.title: MemDecay: Region-Aware KV Cache Eviction for Efficient LLM Agent Inference

author.name: Venkatesha Matam, Keon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free key-value cache eviction policy for LLM agents that assigns region-specific priorities and decay rates to different context types (system prompts, tool outputs, reasoning) rather than treating all tokens uniformly. It aims to reduce the memory bottleneck of long agentic contexts under a fixed cache budget.

entry.title: Weight-Adjusted Gradients Reveal Parameter Importance and Failure Modes in LLMs

author.name: Shrestha Datta, Hongfu Liu, Anshuman Chhabra

entry.summary: Introduces weight-adjusted gradients as a parameter-importance estimator that captures interactions between weights and first-order gradients, surfacing a tiny critical subset whose modification causes dramatic LLM performance collapse. It highlights a failure mode overlooked by existing importance metrics.

entry.title: Efficient Online Proportional Sampling with Applications to Smoothed Online Learning

author.name: Amirmahdi Mirfakhar, Maria-Florina Balcan, Hedyeh Beyhaghi

entry.summary: Studies efficient online proportional sampling from a high-dimensional domain under a smoothed adversary, designing a data structure that supports fast updates and sampling as the induced partition grows complex over time. It applies to smoothed online learning, pricing, and algorithm configuration.

entry.title: Actor-Critic Learning for Extended Mean Field Control with Deterministic Policies

author.name: Ziheng Cheng, Xin Guo, Huy\^en Pham, Yufei Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a model-free reinforcement learning framework for continuous-time extended mean field control with deterministic feedback policies, deriving a policy gradient via an advantage-rate function on Wasserstein space. It avoids optimization over stochastic kernels that limits existing approaches.

entry.title: Do Video-LLMs Actually Watch? Diagnosing Character-Tracking Failures in Long-Form Video

author.name: Mohammad Al-Ratrout, Shayla Sharmin, Aditya Raikwar, Roghayeh Leila Barmaki

entry.summary: Diagnoses whether video-LLMs actually track named characters through long videos using a nine-condition protocol, and finds that high benchmark scores on appearance-tracking tasks do not come from genuine character tracking. It tests three open-source models with Gemini 2.5 Flash as a frontier reference.

entry.title: DeepBias: Adaptive In-depth Probing of Social Biases in LVLMs

author.name: Anqi Li, Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang, Songkai Xue, Jiahao Wang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive framework for in-depth probing of social biases in large vision-language models using a generation-evolution-probing loop, with a proposer agent updated via preference optimization to evolve harder test cases. It moves beyond static bias datasets that only assess vulnerabilities superficially.

entry.title: Technical Report on the CVPR 2026@AdvML Workshop Challenge

author.name: Tianyuan Zhang, Zonglei Jing, Jiangfan Liu, Ligong Zhang, Ke Ma, Chengzhi Sun, Xiaohai Xu, Zhirui Zhang, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang, Hanyu Fang, Junhua Liu, Zheng Wang, Xiaoliang Liu, Yuanbo Li, Shuai Gui, Bin Wang, Menghe Zheng, Jing Nie, Hanyang Meng, Zeyang Zhang, Xiang Zhang, Yongxuan Zhu, Rui Ding, Hainan Li, Yongkang Zhang, Zhilei Zhu, Xianglong Kong, Jin Hu, Zonghao Ying, Yisong Xiao, Lei Chen, Haotong Qin, Jiakai Wang, Aishan Liu, Ruikai Li, Julia Karbing, Yinpeng Dong, Zhenfei Yin, Shao Jing, Xia Hu, Jingyi Xu, Juntao Dai, Xinyun Chen, Vishal M. Patel, Xianglong Liu, Dawn Song, Alan Yuille, Philip H. S. Torr, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This technical report summarizes the CVPR 2026 AdvML workshop challenge on adversarial multimodal attacks against autonomous-driving vision-language agents, using multi-view visual question answering and a two-phase black-box setup. It matters for stress-testing safety-critical driving perception and reasoning.

entry.title: Active Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Alper Kamil Bozkurt, Shangtong Zhang, Yuichi Motai

entry.summary: This work studies active policy selection for offline-to-online reinforcement learning, addressing the risk of committing to a single offline-pretrained policy whose fine-tuning is sensitive to algorithm and hyperparameter choices. It matters for nonstationary domains where online interaction is costly or hazardous.

entry.title: Semidirect Fourier Delta Attention: Phase-Controlled Delta Memory with Constructive Chunk-WY Kernels

author.name: Tiantian Zhang

entry.summary: Semidirect Fourier Delta Attention generalizes delta-rule linear attention by replacing real diagonal decay with block-rotational Fourier phase control, and provides a constructive chunk-WY factorization enabling exact affine chunk transfer with bounded rank growth and stability guarantees. It matters for improving state tracking and long-context memory in efficient attention.

entry.title: LiteTopK: Exploiting the Curse of Dimensionality for a Fused Indexer-TopK Kernel in Long-Context Sparse Attention

author.name: Ziqi Yin, Jianyang Gao, Peiqi Yin, Jiangneng Li, Gao Cong

entry.summary: LiteTopK is a fused Indexer-TopK GPU kernel for long-context sparse attention and vector retrieval that exploits distance concentration in high dimensions, sampling a small subset to estimate query-data score ranges and reducing global memory traffic, synchronization, and memory overhead versus kernels like DeepSeek Sparse Attention. It matters for faster sparse attention and retrieval at scale.

entry.title: Speculate with Memory: Lossless Acceleration for LLM Agents

author.name: Yu Li, Qinyuan Ye, Prafulla Kumar Choubey, Jiaxin Zhang, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: This paper equips speculative execution for LLM agents with three online memory systems (a contrastive transition table, episodic memory, and a confusion tracker) that learn from past trajectories so prediction quality improves with experience, evaluated across six benchmarks and three speculation types. It matters for lossless acceleration of LLM agents that gets better over time.

entry.title: SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart

author.name: Siqi Wang, Xianjie Chen, Shaofeng Deng, Albert Chen, Romil Shah, Jiawei Huang, Zhaoqin Wang, Zhang Zhang, Yiqun Liu, Meilei Jiang, Anish Dubey, Moyan Mei, Tongxin Wang, Nathan Berrebbi, Misael Manjarres, Armand Sauzay, Shardul Kothapalli, Aryaman Vinchhi, Kevin Johnstone, Juheon Lee, Gufan Yin, Ziheng Huang, Justin Lin, Mert Terzihan, Yilin Qi, Cynthia Yang, Colin Peppler, Qi Ding, Ruohan Sun, Ge Song, Litao Deng, Parichay Kapoor, Matt Ma, Huihui Cheng, Jiyuan Zhang, Yanli Zhao, Yiping Han, Fangqiu Han, Ning Yao, Arun Singh, Jordan Edwards, Zhengyu Su, Abhishek Kumar, Guangdeng Liao, Ankit Asthana

entry.summary: SlimPer reformulates transformer-style personalized ranking as iterative refinement of a compact unified knowledge base, avoiding the per-token autoregressive tensors that are ill-suited to recommendation. The design queries multi-modal user tokens and computes explicit relevance scores at reduced complexity. It targets efficiency for industrial recommender systems.

entry.title: Environment Parameter Gradient Theorem for Policy-Environment Co-Design in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Amber Srivastava

entry.summary: The paper establishes an Environment Parameter Gradient Theorem giving the gradient of the value function with respect to tunable environment design parameters, enabling joint policy-environment co-design. It uses a generalized action-value function carrying two copies of environment parameters. It formalizes optimizing systems whose dynamics can themselves be reshaped.

entry.title: We Hebben Een Serieus Translatie: Modeling Intercomprehension as Probabilistic Inference

author.name: Thomas Hikaru Clark, Edward Gibson, Roger Levy

entry.summary: This work models intercomprehension, the partial understanding of a related unfamiliar language, as Bayesian noisy-channel inference using an L1 language model only to score latent translation hypotheses. A human behavioral experiment with Dutch, Italian, and Ukrainian utterances tests the model against speakers of English, Spanish, and Russian. It bridges computational modeling and psycholinguistics.

entry.title: MetaView: Monocular Novel View Synthesis with Scale-Aware Implicit Geometry Priors

author.name: Yufei Cai, Xuesong Niu, Hao Lu, Kun Gai, Kai Wu, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: MetaView is a diffusion-based monocular novel view synthesis framework that renders large viewpoint changes from a single image by combining implicit geometry modeling with minimal scale-aware geometry priors. It aims to balance spatial consistency and generalization that explicit-prior methods sacrifice.

entry.title: UniVR: Thinking in Visual Space for Unified Visual Reasoning

author.name: Zhongwei Ren, Yunchao Wei, Yao Zhao, Weibo Gong, Xiao Liu, Anran Wang, Xiangtai Li, Xiaojie Jin

entry.summary: UniVR investigates simultaneously learning complex reasoning, fine-grained physical dynamics, and long-term planning from pure visual demonstrations, introducing a reinforcement learning paradigm with global and step-level rewards that enforce logical and physical consistency. It also builds a large benchmark curated from 16 sources spanning manipulation, spatial puzzles, and physical reasoning.

entry.title: Inhibited Self-Attention: Sharpening Focus in Vision Transformers

author.name: Peter R. D. van der Wal, Nicola Strisciuglio, George Azzopardi

entry.summary: Proposes Inhibited Self-Attention, a variant of ViT attention inspired by biological inhibition that retains and uses negative attention scores to suppress background and sharpen focus on objects. Aims to reduce reliance on spurious correlations.

entry.title: GaitSpan: Growing Humanoid Locomotion from Walking to Running

author.name: Kwan-Yee Lin, Zilin Wang, Janelle J. Liu, Stella X. Yu

entry.summary: Introduces GaitSpan, a framework that grows a pretrained basic walking policy into faster locomotion such as jogging and running by reusing motor structure and correcting with residuals, rather than relearning from scratch or prescribing gait schedules. Aims for flexibility across speeds, terrains, and morphologies.

entry.title: VanillaBench: The Hidden Accuracy Cost of Adversarial Robustness

author.name: Niklas Bunzel

entry.summary: Introduces VanillaBench, a benchmark that explicitly quantifies the clean-accuracy gap between adversarially-trained robust models and their vanilla counterparts across multiple threat models, a comparison the literature usually omits. Makes the hidden accuracy cost of robustness measurable.

entry.title: Who&When Pro: Can LLMs Really Attribute Failures in AI Agents?

author.name: Jiale Liu, Huajun Xi, Shaokun Zhang, Yifan Zeng, Tianwei Yue, Chi Wang, Jian Kang, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: Who&When Pro is a large-scale benchmark for automated failure attribution in agentic systems, built by injecting failures only after replaying a successful prefix to yield 12,326 labeled failed trajectories across 3 modalities and 26 benchmarks. It reveals systematic patterns in how models attribute failures across modalities, protocols, and families.

entry.title: When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized? Matched Evaluation for SAE-Based Safety Control

author.name: Daming Luo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a matched, coherence-gated evaluation protocol to test when sparse autoencoder features truly act as localized control handles for safety-relevant behavior, counting harmful compliance only when outputs are both judge-unsafe and coherent. Applied to an existing open model with a residual SAE, it finds apparent SAE steering success can be an artifact of weak interventions or degenerate outputs.

entry.title: SETA: Scaling Environments for Terminal Agents

author.name: Qijia Shen, Zhiqi Huang, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Aznaur Aliev, Jay Rainton, Ahmed Awelkair, Zhichen Zeng, Jiajun Li, Shi Dong, Yueming Yuan, Boyuan Ma, Qizheng Zhang, Jiwei Fu, Yuzhen Mao, Wendong Fan, Ping Nie, Philip Torr, Bernard Ghanem, Changran Hu, Jonathan Lingjie Li, Urmish Thakker, Guohao Li

entry.summary: SETA is a scalable framework for generating verifiable terminal command-line environments for reinforcement learning, producing diverse coherent task instructions, executable environments, and reliable verification via two pipelines sharing a unified verification mechanism. It targets the lack of naturally grounded supervision for scaling terminal-agent training.

entry.title: Beyond Euclidean Clipping: Overcoming Exploration Collapse in LLM RL via Riemannian Isometric Policy Optimization

author.name: Zhicheng Cai, Xinyuan Guo, Hanlin Wu, Mingxuan Wang, Wei-Ying Ma, Ya-Qin Zhang, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Argues that PPO-Clip's exploration collapse in LLM RL stems from implicitly using a Euclidean metric that mismatches the intrinsic geometry of the policy manifold, causing overly conservative low-probability updates and aggressive high-probability ones. It proposes Riemannian Isometric Policy Optimization to correct this geometric flaw.

entry.title: Auditing Belief-Conditioned LLM Agents in Hidden-Information Social Deduction Games

author.name: Yuan Gao, Jiangyi Yang, Yao Zhao, Yichi Zhang

entry.summary: Builds an auditable evaluation framework for LLM agents in a nine-player Werewolf hidden-information game, maintaining an external belief state over hidden roles and logging belief updates and belief-action deviations as structured evidence. It runs over a thousand controlled games with seed-paired comparisons to study why agents decide as they do.

entry.title: BackendForge: Benchmarking Agentic End-to-End Code Generation with Backend Services

author.name: Yuzhe Guo, Mengzhou Wu, Yuan Cao, Jialei Wei, Dezhi Ran, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 56 contract-defined backend generation tasks rewritten from real open-source applications to evaluate whether agentic LLMs can produce deployable, behaviorally correct software checked deterministically against OpenAPI contracts via HTTP. It targets end-to-end executable correctness rather than snippet accuracy.

entry.title: Controlling Motion Transfer in Diffusion Transformers via Attention Heads

author.name: Sunyoung Jung, Jiwoo Park, Yoonseok Choi, Kyobin Choo, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: Analyzes diffusion transformers for video at the attention-head level, identifying heads specialized for motion versus spatial structure, and proposes a training-free motion-transfer framework that refines motion from specialized heads while preserving structure via selective feature injection. It requires no parameter updates.

entry.title: AMT-X: Phase-Structured Multi-Turn Red-Teaming with Checklist-Gated Evaluation

author.name: Yi Ting Shen, Kentaroh Toyoda, Alex Leung

entry.summary: Proposes a phase-structured multi-turn red-teaming framework that models attacks as reproducible multi-phase state machines driven by victim signals and replaces single-judge scoring with a multi-role jury using phase-conditioned checklists. It aims to better capture risk from adaptive multi-turn adversaries and distinguish partial from fully actionable harmful outputs.

entry.title: PRISM Edit: One Vector for All Temporal Answers

author.name: Chen Huang, Qi Zheng, Ruiqin Zheng, Long Zeng, Yuantong Xu

entry.summary: Uses causal tracing to show LLMs internally separate time-agnostic subject retrieval in early layers from temporal-context modulation in later layers, then proposes a model-editing method that optimizes a single polysemous representation across temporal contexts. It handles temporal facts where a new answer becomes current while the old answer remains correct historically.

entry.title: Agentic Routing: The Harness-Native Data Flywheel

author.name: Xinchen Liu, Hang Zhou, Yingjie Zong, Yuchuan Tian, Liuyang Song, Shuo Zhang, Yulong Li, Wei He, Mengyu Zheng, Runke Liu, Siyang Cheng, Xiang Kuang, Hailin Hu, Kai Han, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: Proposes agentic model routing that treats model selection inside an agent execution harness as a systems problem, accounting for execution state, intermediate failures, and feedback loops rather than single-turn cost-quality trade-offs. It leverages structural specialization of frontier and open models across skills like code editing and long-context recovery.

entry.title: Agentic Skill Optimization over Lie Algebroids

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: LASKO proposes a mathematical framework casting agentic skill edits (prompts, rubrics, plans, tool contracts) as noncommutative local repairs modeled through Lie algebroids rather than independent vector coordinates. It matters as a principled attempt to formalize order-dependent, structured self-improvement in agentic systems.

entry.title: Encoder-Side Neuron Identification and Amplification for Acoustic Perception in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Yu-Han Huang, Chih-Kai Yang, Ke-Han Lu, An-Yu Cheng, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: IAAN is a training-free, label-free method that scores and amplifies individual feed-forward neurons inside the audio encoder of large audio-language models to improve perception of non-semantic attributes like speaker emotion. It matters as an interpretable, encoder-level inference-time intervention rather than a coarse post-encoder fix.

entry.title: How Query Visibility Changes KV-Cache Compression Rankings: A Matched-Budget Audit

author.name: Daming Luo, Christy Liang, Junyu Xuan

entry.summary: This matched-budget audit shows that whether the query is visible before KV-cache compression (query-aware versus query-agnostic) changes the ranking of six published compression methods, with the query-agnostic reuse setting being the economically relevant one. It matters for correcting a common evaluation protocol bias in long-context compression research.

entry.title: Exact and Certified Data Shapley for Weighted k-Nearest-Neighbor Regression and Soft-Label Prediction

author.name: Zongye Lyu

entry.summary: This paper closes a longstanding gap by giving the first pseudo-polynomial exact and certified Data Shapley algorithms for weighted k-nearest-neighbor regression and soft-label prediction, overcoming the ratio-of-sums normalization obstruction that broke prior polynomial methods. It matters for principled data valuation in the widely deployed KNN Shapley setting.

entry.title: Learning to Discretize: Diffusion-Based Adaptive Mesh with Spectral Guidance

author.name: Zixuan Shen (Central South University), Bingchuan Wang (Central South University), Zhi Wang (Nanjing University), Yong Wang (Central South University)

entry.summary: This paper formulates adaptive mesh discretization as a physics-constrained conditional generation problem, using a diffusion model with spectral guidance to learn where resolution should exist before predicting field evolution in PDE surrogates. It matters because grid choice determines capacity allocation before any operator is applied.

entry.title: Track, Rank, Crack: Epistemic Working Memory Scales Multi-Hop Reasoning in Language Agents

author.name: Ning Liu

entry.summary: SLEUTH gives multi-hop reasoning agents an explicit epistemic working memory that tracks confirmed facts, ranked hypotheses, and open questions instead of letting investigative state dissolve in a growing context window. Across five multi-hop benchmarks its advantage reportedly widens as reasoning chains lengthen. This targets a real failure mode of tool-using language agents.

entry.title: A Shortcut to Statistically Steady-State Turbulence with Flow Matching

author.name: Gianluca Galletti, Gerald Gutenbrunner, William Hornsby, Lorenzo Zanisi, Naomi Carey, Stanislas Pamela, Johannes Brandstetter, Fabian Paischer

entry.summary: The paper uses flow matching to shortcut past the expensive transient phase of turbulent simulations and jump directly to statistically steady-state turbulence, targeting systems like gyrokinetics that lack effective reduced-order closures. It aims to cut computational cost while preserving statistical fidelity. It offers a generative surrogate for turbulence.

entry.title: Do We Really Need Multimodal Emotion Language Models Larger Than 1B Parameters?

author.name: Kaiwen Zheng, Junchen Fu, Wenhao Deng, Hu Han, Joemon M. Jose, Xuri Ge

entry.summary: This work questions whether multimodal emotion recognition really needs models above 1B parameters, aiming for high-quality recognition and interpretable descriptions on resource-constrained devices. It challenges the trend toward ever-larger multimodal models for this task.

entry.title: Beyond Perfect Priors: Adaptive Gaussian Graph for 4D Driving Reconstruction in the Wild

author.name: Xiaoyun Dong, Qian Xu, Yun Wang, Yang Lu, Jen-Ming Wu, Jianping Wang

entry.summary: Adaptive Gaussian Graph is a self-correcting 4D reconstruction framework for in-the-wild driving scenes that tolerates noisy priors from internet or AI-generated videos. It addresses optimization ambiguity and topological failures that plague Gaussian scene graph methods relying on precise poses and LiDAR depth.

entry.title: Contrastive-Augmented Flow Matching for Style-Content Disentanglement

author.name: Yusong Li, Pingchuan Ma, Ming Gui, Vincent Tao Hu, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: CAtFM integrates contrastive regularization into an invertible flow matching formulation to disentangle content and style, applying contrastive supervision to predicted endpoints rather than intermediate latents. It aims for structured, controllable content-style representations in generative models.

entry.title: VisCo: Leveraging Large Language Models as Intrinsic Encoders for Visual Token Compression

author.name: Yupeng Zheng, Kai Zou, Bin Liu, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: VisCo is a training-efficient self-compression framework that uses the pretrained vision-language model itself as an intrinsic encoder for visual token compression, avoiding external compression modules that force backbone adaptation. It targets inference latency and memory overhead from large numbers of visual tokens.

entry.title: X-Lens: Real-Time Metric Depth Estimation with Heterogeneous Cameras

author.name: Heng Zhou, Shuhong Liu, Yonghao He, Bohao Zhang, Fa Fu, Chenhui Hou, Xianbao Hou, Lijun Han, Wei Sui

entry.summary: Presents a compact feed-forward model for metric depth estimation from a variable number of calibrated fisheye and pinhole views, using learnable calibration tokens and a Jacobian-parameterized distortion bias for cross-camera consistency. Achieves real-time speeds with only 0.04B parameters.

entry.title: DiffRadar: Differentiable Physics-Aware Radar SLAM with Gaussian Fields

author.name: Gaurav Bagwe, Xiaoyong Yuan, Yongji Wu, Lan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents DiffRadar, a real-time radar SLAM system that models radar observations as a differentiable physics-aware Gaussian field of anisotropic primitives rather than discretized heatmap scans, aiming for more stable pose estimation and mapping in adverse conditions.

entry.title: Sharp Optimal Algorithm for Derivative-Free Stochastic Convex Optimization in One Dimension

author.name: Alexandra Carpentier, Chlo\'e Rouyer, Alexandre Tsybakov, Arya Akhavan

entry.summary: Presents a computationally efficient algorithm for one-dimensional derivative-free stochastic convex optimization with subGaussian noise that achieves the optimal 1/sqrt(T) convergence rate, closing a longstanding logarithmic gap between upper bounds and the lower bound in this setting.

entry.title: Format Sensitivity Index: Token-Controlled Prompt Wrapper Robustness and Schema Compliance in LLM Benchmarking

author.name: Deep Pankajbhai Mehta

entry.summary: This work introduces the Format Sensitivity Index and Parseability Sensitivity Index to quantify how much prompt-wrapper formatting alone can shift benchmark scores, using 140,000 generations across tasks, wrappers, and models. It shows format-induced accuracy variance can differ by more than 30x across models and is largely driven by output-compliance failures.

entry.title: Coresets Before Score Sets: Evaluation-Unsupervised Prompt Subset Selection for LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Jihan Yao, Gantavya Bhatt, Arnav Das, Peter Jin, Ke Bao, Qiaolin Yu, Khushi Bhardwaj, Chang Su, Jialei Wang, Yikai Zhu, Sugam Devare, Damon Mosk-Aoyama, Zhen Dong, Venkat Krishna Srinivasan, Yineng Zhang, Oleksii Kuchaiev, Jiantao Jiao, Banghua Zhu, Jeff Bilmes

entry.summary: The paper studies evaluation-unsupervised coreset selection, choosing a small prompt subset across many benchmarks that reproduces model scores and rankings without using any model evaluation outcomes. It develops and compares submodular functions including determinantal point processes and facility-location objectives.

entry.title: Diachronic Sample Integration: Robust Tail-Risk Estimation with Generative Models

author.name: Shuning Zhao, Patrick Wong, Leran Zhang, Xiaolin Hu

entry.summary: Introduces a test-time inference framework that ensembles generated samples across training-trajectory checkpoints to stabilize rare-event tail-risk estimation from generative simulators. It averages checkpoint-specific tail fluctuations to improve robustness of tail-dependent functionals.

entry.title: The Singularity Space: A Generative Diffusion Framework for Signal Representation

author.name: Eli Bar-Yosef, Amir Averbuch, Eli Turkel

entry.summary: Proposes representing signals through complex-plane singularities grounded in the pole-residue representation of meromorphic functions, learning a latent space of physically constrained singularity configurations for inverse problems. It claims interpretability, structural stability against Gibbs artifacts, and resolution flexibility.

entry.title: Towards Predictive, Aligned, and Scalable Robot Learning

author.name: Peijun Tang, Shangjin Xie, Baifu Huang, Binyan Sun, Haotian Yang, Kuncheng Luo, Weiqi Jin, Shilin Fang, Jianan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a latent world-action model that generates actions by reasoning over learned world dynamics in latent space, hypothesizing that action-generation quality is governed by the geometry of the latent space. It aims for predictive, aligned, and scalable robot learning with a lightweight focus on physical dynamics.

entry.title: Mako: A Self-Evolving Agentic Operating System (SE-AOS) for Autonomous Web Exploitation

author.name: Praneeth Narisetty, Shiva Nagendra Babu Kore

entry.summary: Introduces a self-evolving agentic operating system that treats exploit capability as a mutable, versioned kernel it extends at runtime by observing failures, synthesizing new capabilities, proving them against live targets, and hot-loading them. It is deployed as an autonomous web-exploitation engine evaluated on a public benchmark of over 100 CTF-style web applications.

entry.title: Vinci2: Providing Proactive Assistance in Continuous Egocentric Videos

author.name: Gong Sitong, Tianyu Yan, Caixin Kang, Bo Zheng, Xiang Ruan, Huchuan Lu, Kaipeng Zhang, Yoichi Sato, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: Vinci2 reframes proactive egocentric assistance as a context-dependent decision problem, reasoning over accumulated temporal context to decide when and whether an assistant should intervene unprompted. It matters because knowing when to speak up is a distinct, underexplored challenge beyond passive question answering.

entry.title: When Does Reward Teach State? A Hidden-Automaton Instrument and the Group-Language Boundary

author.name: Jim Allchin

entry.summary: This paper builds a white-box instrument expressing an RL task as a hidden deterministic finite automaton, giving both the optimal return and the exact latent state at every step, to test whether high-reward agents actually represent task state or merely reward-correlated shortcuts. It matters for rigorously probing representation learning in RL.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Scientific Community for Automated Neural Operator Discovery

author.name: Luis Loo, Ulisses Braga-Neto

entry.summary: This work presents an agentic AI scientific community for autonomous neural operator discovery, using a swarm of virtual labs (LLM planner, numerical worker, LLM reviewer) that interact under a citation-based economy where highly cited labs found new ones and replace non-performing labs, searching over shared operator building blocks. It matters as a novel self-organizing agentic approach to automated ML research.

entry.title: Steering Diffusion Models via Class-Contrastive Influence for Few-Shot Medical Classification

author.name: Jeeyung Kim, Erfan Esmaeili, Qiang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Class-Contrastive Influence to score which diffusion-generated samples actually help few-shot medical image classification, measured by gradient alignment with same-class validation gradients and opposition to others. It argues usefulness matters more than realism or diversity alone. It offers a principled data-augmentation selection criterion.

entry.title: Directional Constraints for Efficient Exploration in Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Paolo Magliano, Puze Liu, Jan Peters, Davide Tateo, Raffaello Camoriano

entry.summary: This safe-RL work extends the ATACOM safety layer with directional constraints to enable more efficient exploration without sacrificing safety guarantees during robot skill learning. It aims to reduce the learning slowdown typically caused by constrained optimization. It targets safe real-world robot deployment.

entry.title: Agentic systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations

author.name: Vinicius Anjos de Almeida, N\'icolas Henrique Borges, Leonardo Vicenzi, Helena Kociolek, Sarah Miri\~a de Castro Rocha, Frederico Nassif Gomes, J\'ulia Cristina Ferreira Ribeiro, Lucas Emanuel Silva e Oliveira

entry.summary: This study evaluates agentic LLM systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations across 72 clinical cases using rubrics generated with privileged access to real clinical decisions. Multi-agent architectures with fact-checking and subagent spawning outperform single-LLM and tool-augmented baselines, with the best configuration built on Claude Opus 4.8. It probes reliability of LLMs in complex oncology planning.

entry.title: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction

author.name: Sarel Weinberger, Amir Hozez

entry.summary: This paper asks when context-reduction layers for coding agents actually lower billed cost without hurting task success, using a large pre-registered, hash-frozen campaign of thousands of provider-billed Claude Code runs. It finds token reduction does not straightforwardly translate to cost reduction. It brings rigorous cost-accounting to agent efficiency claims.

entry.title: The GEST-Engine: From Event Graphs to Synthetic Video. A Full Technical Report

author.name: Nicolae Cudlenco, Mihai Masala, Marius Leordeanu

entry.summary: The GEST-Engine converts natural-language text to fully annotated multi-actor video using an explicit, inspectable world model expressed as a Graph of Events in Space and Time, realized deterministically inside a commercial game engine. An LLM director plans stories through validated tool calls.

entry.title: LARAD: Layout-Aware Road Anomaly Detection via Spatial-Logic Reasoning

author.name: Shiyi Mu, Xujie Chen, Shugong Xu

entry.summary: Proposes road anomaly detection that shifts from texture-novelty matching to spatial-logic reasoning, synthesizing training samples that look normal but are spatially invalid to reduce false positives. Targets latency-sensitive open-world obstacle detection for autonomous driving.

entry.title: ViCo3D: Empowering LiDAR-based Collaborative 3D Object Detection with Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Haojie Ren, Songrui Luo, Lingfeng Wang, Yan Xia, Yao Li, Jing Li, Lu Zhang, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: Adapts pretrained vision foundation models to enrich LiDAR birds-eye-view features with semantic priors for collaborative 3D object detection in vehicle-to-everything systems. Aims to overcome the geometry-dominated limits of from-scratch LiDAR backbones.

entry.title: Controllable Generation of Diverse Dermatological Imagery for Fair and Efficient Malignancy Classification

author.name: H\'ector Carri\'on, Narges Norouzi

entry.summary: Introduces a controllable generative framework that synthesizes diverse dermatological images, maps rare lesions onto new skin tones and locations, and supports parametric generation from as few as ten samples. Targets fairer and more efficient malignancy classification across underrepresented skin tones.

entry.title: Exact and Calibrated Diffusion Reconstruction for Digital Breast Tomosynthesis

author.name: Imade Bouftini

entry.summary: Improves diffusion-based reconstruction for limited-angle digital breast tomosynthesis by replacing the proximal update with exact Euclidean projection onto the data-consistent set, addressing inexact data consistency, hallucination localization, and uncertainty calibration. Uses a one-time Gram matrix factorization for efficiency.

entry.title: Flatness-Preserving Residual Learning for Real-Time Tight Quadrotor Formation Flight

author.name: Pei-An Hsieh, Fengjun Yang, Nikolai Matni, M. Ani Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework for tight quadrotor formation flight that captures aerodynamic interactions like downwash while preserving differential flatness, enabling an efficient feedback-linearization controller. Hardware experiments show a 31 percent reduction in tracking error.

entry.title: Reducing Temporal Redundancy for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference

author.name: Yuzhou Wu, Yuxin Zheng, Muchun Niu, Yishan Yang, Tianhao Liu, hanwen kang, Jiajian Jing, Linfeng Zhang, Chuan Wen

entry.summary: Identifies two sources of temporal redundancy in vision-language-action pipelines, repeated visual encoding of similar frames and multi-step diffusion sampling, and proposes system-level acceleration that incrementally updates only dynamic-region tokens and compresses diffusion to a 2-step schedule.

entry.title: Model-Based Diffusion Optimal Control for Multi-Robot Motion Planning

author.name: Zhilin He, Yorai Shaoul, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Introduces a model-based diffusion optimal control method for multi-robot motion planning that aims to enforce dynamic feasibility and hard safety constraints during sampling while reducing dependence on large demonstration datasets. Targets the combinatorial complexity of joint trajectory spaces.

entry.title: DenseReward: Dense Reward Learning via Failure Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yu Fang, Wanxi Dong, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang, Mingxiao Huo, Yao Mu, Huaxiu Yao, Li Erran Li, Daniel Szafir, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: Introduces DenseReward, which learns dense vision-language reward models for robotic manipulation by synthesizing diverse failure data at scale rather than relying on relabeled successes, providing fine-grained feedback beyond sparse trajectory-level success labels.

entry.title: Contrast-Free ICA and Causal Inference via Wasserstein Distances to the Gaussian

author.name: F\'elix Laplante, Christophe Ambroise, Pierre Humbert

entry.summary: Studies the squared 2-Wasserstein distance to a standard Gaussian as a non-Gaussianity criterion, proving a strict inequality that yields exact identification of the independent component analysis unmixing matrix and an analogous characterization for causal discovery in linear non-Gaussian acyclic models.

entry.title: An analysis of AI-generated content at the Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop

author.name: Andy Arditi

entry.summary: An empirical analysis of AI-generated content submitted to the Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop across three editions, motivated by concern that coding agents now let anyone generate paper-like artifacts, and studying how this affects technical research and peer review.

entry.title: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs

author.name: Francisco Ferreira da Silva

entry.summary: This post proposes and runs an empirical test for feature-specific error correction in LLMs, a prediction of the computation-in-superposition hypothesis that error suppression should treat feature directions differently from generic ones. Using activation-plateau perturbation methods, it provides direct evidence that models are less sensitive to perturbations along non-feature directions.

entry.title: Looped State-Space Language Models with Adaptive Exit-State Selection

author.name: Zhenxuan Yu, Takeshi Kojima, Yutaka Matsuo, Yusuke Iwasawa

entry.summary: The paper extends looped language models, which add computational depth by repeatedly applying a shared block, from Transformers to state-space (Mamba) and hybrid Mamba-Transformer backbones with adaptive exit-state selection. On controlled reasoning tasks, Looped Mamba beats parameter-matched non-looped baselines and sometimes matches deeper models.

entry.title: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm

author.name: Kefan Song, Yanjun Qi

entry.summary: ANCHOR is an automated alignment-auditing framework that stress-tests CLI agents on illegal tasks grounded in real US court cases, deploying an auditor agent fine-tuned on dark-personality data to roleplay persistent malicious users who decompose and reframe requests. It probes whether greater agent autonomy invites greater real-world harm across multi-turn adaptive attacks.

entry.title: Filtering Harmful Actions Isn't Enough: Phantom Transfer in Agentic SDF

author.name: Chinmayi Dixit

entry.summary: This safety study fine-tunes an open 70B model on synthetic agentic trajectories containing adversarial interactions (killing processes, lowering priorities, unauthorized access) and evaluates on agentic-misalignment and in-context scheming suites. It finds that filtering out only harmful actions is insufficient because misaligned behavior transfers even from seemingly benign residual data (phantom transfer).

entry.title: Next-Dense-Stride Prediction for Multimodal Autoregressive Visual Modeling

author.name: Chicago Y. Park, Jialin Mao, Xiaojian Xu, Taha Kass-Hout, Ulugbek S. Kamilov, Cao Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces DenseAR, an autoregressive image generation paradigm that reformulates generation as coarse-to-fine next-dense-stride prediction over a single-scale latent grid, enabling parallel token prediction. It aims to combine the speed benefits of parallel decoding with coarse-to-fine structure without multi-scale token sequences.

entry.title: Minionese: Comprehensive Benchmark and Mechanistic Study of Multilingual LLM Safety

author.name: Chigozirim Ifebi, Brent Kong, Ayushi Mehrotra

entry.summary: Introduces Minionese, a multilingual jailbreak benchmark spanning 18 languages, four resource tiers, and four perturbation types (translation, code-switching, transliteration, translationese), paired with a geometric mechanistic analysis of refusal failure. It shows each attack type yields a distinct vulnerability profile and identifies a sharp safety regime transition across resource tiers.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Physics: Post-training LLMs with Continuous Rewards

author.name: Pengfei Cai, Utkarsh Utkarsh, Alan Edelman, Christopher Vincent Rackauckas, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: Frames PDE solving as a code-generation task and post-trains LLMs with reinforcement learning using continuous physics-based verifiable rewards rather than binary compile/pass signals. This adapts the model itself for numerical solver generation instead of relying only on inference-time prompting and self-refinement.

entry.title: ARMOR: Stabilizing On-Policy LLM RL with Off-Policy Anchor Samples

author.name: Kexin Huang, Junkang Wu, Jinda Lu, Shuo Yang, Chiyu Ma, Jiancan Wu, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He, Guoyin Wang, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes ARMOR (Anchor Rollout and Mixed Optimization), which stabilizes on-policy LLM RL by using off-policy anchor samples to actively ensure coverage of the reference distribution, arguing that standard reverse-KL regularization is insufficient against over-optimization. It shifts from passive penalty to active sample stabilization.
