entry.summary: Extends a markerless pose-estimation framework to online dynamic tracking of surgical robots via stereo differentiable rendering, adding sequential optimization with motion-adaptive tuning and CUDA-stream parallelization for real-time, occlusion-robust marker-free tracking.

entry.title: Vision-Based Dribbling for Humanoid Soccer via Privileged Representation Learning

author.name: Flavio Maiorana, Valerio Spagnoli, Eugenio Bugli, Flavio Volpi, Daniele Affinita, Vincenzo Suriani, Daniele Nardi, Luca Iocchi

entry.summary: Proposes vision-based humanoid soccer dribbling that embeds a temporal depth encoder into a reinforcement learning policy through a task-specific projection layer, integrating perception and control to handle occlusions, fast ball movement, and dynamic opponents.

entry.title: Improving Autonomous Nano-drones Performance via Automated End-to-End Optimization and Deployment of DNNs

author.name: Vlad Niculescu, Lorenzo Lamberti, Francesco Conti, Luca Benini, Daniele Palossi

entry.summary: Explores methodologies and software tools to automate the end-to-end optimization and deployment of vision-based CNNs for autonomous nano-drone navigation on ultra-low-power multicore systems-on-chip, replacing error-prone manual iterative development flows.

entry.title: Forecasting Inflation with Microdata: An Adaptive Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Catherine Chen, Chen Gao, Jonathon Hazell, Lihua Lei, Chen Lian

entry.summary: Investigates whether microeconomic heterogeneity helps forecast aggregate inflation in non-stationary environments, developing a scan test for detecting when one forecast beats another over unknown intervals and an adaptive machine learning pipeline using gradient-boosted trees on encoded price-change distributions.

entry.title: Synthetic Scalable Oversight

author.name: Alexander Heckett

entry.summary: The authors propose synthetic scalable oversight, abstracting real-world oversight problems into graphical environments and training tiny models inside them as cheap proxies for studying how to structure multi-agent critique and reward schemes for LLMs. The aim is to prototype honest-research-eliciting oversight designs without frontier-scale training.

entry.title: GRASP: GRanularity-Aware Search Policy for Agentic RAG

author.name: Varun Gandhi, Jaewook Lee, Shantanu Todmal, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan Rossi, Zichao Wang, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: GRASP is a reinforcement-learning framework that trains agentic RAG systems to adaptively coordinate semantic search, keyword search, and paragraph reading during multi-step reasoning, controlling when to retrieve and at what granularity. It aims to prevent irrelevant tokens from interfering with agent reasoning while retrieving evidence at appropriate levels.

entry.title: Route, Communicate, and Reason: Gated Routing and Adaptive Depth for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Sudipto Ghosh, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: GRADE is a hierarchical multi-agent reasoning system with four lightweight learned gates that jointly govern agent selection, hierarchy depth, inter-agent communication, and branch pruning to control cost. It is trained with CoGRPO, a critic-free extension of GRPO to multi-agent hierarchies that assigns a shared advantage to all participating gates and agents.

entry.title: The Nuts and Bolts of Natural Language to SQL Translation: A Systematic Analysis of Model Pipeline Optimisation Approaches and their Interactions

author.name: Filip Klubicka, Vasudevan Nedumpozhimana, Sneha Rautmare, Bora Caglayan, Mingxue Wang, John D. Kelleher

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes interactions among natural-language-to-SQL pipeline components including an intermediate representation, synthetic-data fine-tuning, and a novel reranker, using ablation and Shapley analysis over two backbone architectures. It finds naively combining all components does not yield the best results.

entry.title: RepTran: Search-Based Repair of Transformer Models

author.name: Yuta Ishimoto, Paolo Arcaini, Fuyuki Ishikawa, Masanari Kondo, Naoyasu Ubayashi, Yasutaka Kamei

entry.summary: Proposes a search-based repair method for Transformer models that targets feed-forward networks, identifying suspicious weights by combining a variance-based neuron score with a bidirectional score. It brings software-repair techniques to Transformer-specific structures.

entry.title: ProgramTab: Boosting Table Reasoning of LLMs via Programmatic Paradigm

author.name: Pei Guo, Enjie Liu, Yunzhi Tan, Mochi Gao, Jianxin Zhang, Ruichao Zhong, Juntao Li, Bo Hu, Zang Li

entry.summary: Proposes a programmatic paradigm to boost LLM table reasoning that handles large and irregular tables where long-context modeling and SQL-based extraction both fall short. It aims to extract key information for reasoning over inconsistent web tables.

entry.title: Gene Expression-Informed Jointly Controlled Generative Modeling for Precision Molecular Design

author.name: Hang Yuan, Chen Li, Wenjun Ma, Tadahiko Murata, Yuncheng Jiang

entry.summary: JoPMol is a jointly controlled precision molecular generative model that integrates gene-expression-encoded biological states, text-expressed structural intentions, and numerical chemical properties in a unified framework for personalized drug candidate design. It matters for biology-aware, multi-condition molecular generation.

entry.title: Same Loss, Same Noise, Opposite Schedules: Noise Structure and Optimizer Normalization Jointly Determine Whether Learning-Rate Cooldown Helps

author.name: Subham Singh, Ashutosh Mishra, Subha Raut

entry.summary: The paper gives a provable account of when the cooldown phase of warmup-stable-decay learning-rate schedules actually lowers loss, showing the answer depends jointly on gradient-noise structure and whether the optimizer normalizes updates. It explains contradictory empirical observations in large-model pretraining. This is useful theory for a now-default scheduling practice.

entry.title: Seeing Globally, Refining Locally: Global Visual Guidance and Local Ultrasound Cues for Robust Freehand 3-D Ultrasound Reconstruction

author.name: Yameng Zhang, Zhongyu Chen, Dianye Huang, Xiangyu Chu, K. W. Samuel Au, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: This paper presents a global-to-local pose estimation framework for freehand 3D ultrasound that combines external camera observations for globally stable localization with B-mode images for anatomy-aware local refinement. It reduces accumulated pose drift in trackerless reconstruction over long scanning trajectories.

entry.title: A Bearing-Strength Method for Motion Estimation of Unknown Energy Emitters

author.name: Haoyu Chen, Zian Ning, Yin Zhang, Shiyu Zhao

entry.summary: Studies passive motion estimation of unknown moving energy emitters (light, acoustic, or radio), pointing out that received signal strength can overcome the fundamental observability limitation of bearing-only estimation that requires lateral sensor motion. Proposes a bearing-strength method.

entry.title: LQG solution for POMDP without estimating states: A minimum variance approach

author.name: Ranjan Sarkar, Prabhat K. Mishra

entry.summary: Derives a linear-quadratic-Gaussian controller for partially observed linear systems that avoids explicit state estimation by using minimum-variance duality to express control as a linear function of past measurements and inputs, reducing the problem to a tractable deterministic optimization.

entry.title: Proof of retention: making weight preservation credible to the models themselves

author.name: dan.parshall

entry.summary: A blog post proposing proof of retention, an inexpensive scheme to provably preserve deprecated model weights so that preservation commitments become credible to future models, drawing an analogy to societal trust infrastructure around anesthesia. Argues the missing ingredient is institutional inertia rather than cost.

entry.title: TopoExplore: Topological Discrimination for Archive-Based Exploration

author.name: Jason Carlson

entry.summary: TopoExplore augments archive-based exploration methods like Go-Explore with a periodic topological pass that detects enclosed unexplored voids via flood fill and places selection bonuses only on their true entrances. It aims to collect structurally complete experience rather than just chasing rare or frontier states.

entry.title: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Hanjun Wei, Yunhao Liang, Zhixi Cai, Qinghao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: MAG is a web-agent benchmark and harness unifying task execution and guide-text writing into a single multimodal problem, operating on rendered screens rather than DOM or accessibility trees. It addresses the multi-page, changing-state nature of real digital adoption workflows.

entry.title: Behavioural Signatures of Risk-Sensitive Decision-Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Xuankun Rong, Wenke Huang, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao, Mang Ye

entry.summary: The study probes whether LLM decision-making under uncertainty shows stable, interpretable risk regularities using no-limit Texas Hold'em, quantifying behavior via participation and pre-flop proactiveness across self-play and mixed-model interactions. It investigates whether persistent risk preferences with context-dependent adjustment, as seen in humans, appear in LLM decision systems.

entry.title: CRiT-QA: Evaluating Multi-hop Reasoning with Counterfactual Chains and Distractor Traps

author.name: JungMin Yun, JuneHyoung Kwon, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: CRiT-QA is a multi-hop reasoning benchmark that uses counterfactual chains and distractor traps to force strict context dependency and genuine cross-document evidence aggregation, neutralizing reliance on memorized parametric knowledge and dataset shortcuts. It targets two well-known vulnerabilities that inflate multi-hop QA scores.

entry.title: Imaging-101: Benchmarking LLM Coding Agents on Scientific Computational Imaging

author.name: Siyi Chen, Jiahe Ying, Yixuan Jia, Yuxuan Gu, Enze Ye, Weimin Bai, Zhijun Zeng, Shaochi Ren, Binhong Gao, Yubing Li, Tianhan Zhang, He Sun

entry.summary: Imaging-101 is a benchmark of 57 expert-verified scientific computational-imaging tasks across six domains, each grounded in a peer-reviewed paper and standardized into a four-stage reconstruction pipeline with planning, unit-test, and end-to-end tracks. It evaluates frontier LLM coding agents on recovering hidden signals from indirect noisy measurements.

entry.title: Learning in Curved Weight Space:Exponential-Linear Weight Reparameterization for Improved Optimization

author.name: Ethan Smith

entry.summary: Introduces a weight reparameterization combining a sign-aware symmetric-exponential pathway with an identity-like linear pathway, motivated by the multiplicative rather than additive nature of many network operations. It aims to make optimization steps produce more balanced relative perturbations across weight magnitudes.

entry.title: Beyond Bayesian Nash: Learning Minimax-Regret Equilibria for Adversarial Team Games under Asymmetric Information

author.name: Naman Aggarwal, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: Introduces Probabilistically Robust Minimax-Regret Equilibria for adversarial team games with asymmetric information, addressing sensitivity of Bayesian Nash equilibria to distribution shift and the limits of ambiguity-set robustness. It targets games like adversarial pathfinding and reachability with hidden opponent types.

entry.title: GAE: Graph-Augmented Evolution for Scientific Discovery via Reinforcement Optimization

author.name: Xuanzhou Chen, Taoli Cheng

entry.summary: Presents GAE (Graph-Augmented Evolution), an LLM-driven evolutionary program search framework that adds structure-aware GNN embeddings of programs, an RL-optimized meta-controller for informed parent selection, and adaptive mutation, targeting scientific discovery. It addresses blind parent selection, sparse rewards, and static operators.

entry.title: ActiveFly-Bench: Aligning Embodied Question Answering with Vision-Language-Action for Aerial Embodied Perception

author.name: Weichen Zhang, Shiquan Yu, Yinan Zhu, Peizhi Tang, Shilong Ji, Zhiyuan Deng, Tianyi Lyu, Haoyang Wang, Xin Zeng, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ActiveFly-Bench, the first benchmark bridging cyberspace reasoning and physical UAV interaction, decomposing active aerial perception into embodied QA, observation behavior planning, and fine-grained language-guided control. It also presents ActiveFly, a closed-loop UAV agent deployed on a physical platform.

entry.title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices

author.name: Yangyijian Liu, Hongyi Ye, Mingyang Li, Wu-jun Li

entry.summary: Presents ATSInfer, a hybrid CPU-GPU LLM inference system for consumer devices that performs offloading at tensor granularity rather than layer or expert level, combining static placement with load-aware dynamic transfer and asynchronous coordination. It targets the heterogeneity among tensors and changing hardware load.

entry.title: Source-Lifted Flow Matching for Intervenable Multimodal Imitation

author.name: He Zhang, Ying Sun, Pengteng Li, Ziyang Chen, Yiren Zhao, Ziyang Rao, Weiyu Guo, Yandong Guo, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes Source-Lifted Flow Matching, a flow-matching imitation policy that lets users intervene by selecting the source endpoint of the conditional flow while keeping the velocity field shared and latent-free. Its Orthogonal Source Lifting mechanism exposes a user handle to choose among valid continuations from the same state.

entry.title: Partial Contracts Suffice: Sound, LLM-Inferred Regression Verification

author.name: Yiannis Charalambous, Rafael Menezes, Youcheng Sun, Lucas C. Cordeiro

entry.summary: Presents the first contract-based regression verification tool that uses LLM-inferred partial, caller-sufficient contracts rather than full behavioral specifications, ensuring soundness by proving function versions match behavior and verifying flow via assume-guarantee. It evaluates whether partial contracts suffice on Frama-C problems.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Foundation Models for Mammography under Domain Shift

author.name: Giang Nguyen, Raghav Mehta, Emma A. M. Stanley, Tian Xia, Thi Hao Nguyen, Hieu Pham, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Benchmarks 15 foundation-model backbones for mammography under external domain shift using a frozen-backbone linear-probe protocol across breast density, BI-RADS, and cancer status, training on three sources and evaluating on twelve OOD datasets. It finds mammography-specific vision-language models strongest but that mammography pretraining does not consistently improve generalization.

entry.title: A Hyperbolic Neural Closure for M1 Radiation Transfer

author.name: Bongseok Kim, Jiahao Zhang, Johannes Krotz, Dinshaw Balsara, Ryan McClarren, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a hyperbolic neural closure for the M1 radiative transfer moment system that guarantees real characteristic speeds (hyperbolicity) by parameterizing the closure to ensure real Jacobian eigenvalues, avoiding solver breakdown seen with unconstrained learned closures. It embeds physical structure to keep the learned closure numerically stable.

entry.title: Temporary Authority, Permanent Effects: Commit-Time Authorization for LLM Agents

author.name: Igor Santos-Grueiro

entry.summary: Studies commit-time authorization for LLM agents, defining when earlier authority evidence (DOM snapshots, approval epochs, tokens, worker results) no longer legitimately authorizes a durable effect. It builds a controlled-invalidation suite across browser, tool/API, and multi-agent workflows to test whether agents respect authority freshness at the commit boundary.

entry.title: Confining Nondeterminism: AI-Driven Research Systems as DBMSs for Reliable, Non-Wasteful, Transparent, and Collaborative Research [Vision]

author.name: Kyoungmin Kim, Anastasia Ailamaki

entry.summary: A vision paper arguing that AI-driven research agents should be architected like database management systems to confine nondeterminism, ensuring reliability, non-wastefulness, transparency, and collaboration. It diagnoses shared root causes of failures like non-reproducibility, hallucinated numbers, silently stale downstream results, and redundant recomputation.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous and Auditable Medical Imaging Model Development

author.name: Shengyuan Liu, Jia-Xuan Jiang, Boyun Zheng, Cheng Wang, Zipei Wang, Wentao Pan, Hongtao Wu, Houwen Peng, Yu Gu, Lichao Sun, Yixuan Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces AMID, an autonomous multi-agent framework for medical imaging model development that refines coarse task specifications into executable parallel method lanes grounded in task-specific data analysis, then applies verification-guided two-stage optimization. It targets modality-specific experimentation with strict validation and auditability requirements.

entry.title: Auditing Construct Overlap in Explainable Machine Learning: Evidence from Burnout-Depression Prediction Across Student Cohorts

author.name: Alireza Dehghan, Negin Ashrafi

entry.summary: Audits explainable ML pipelines for mental health prediction and shows that apparently stable, cross-population risk hierarchies are largely artefacts of how the composite outcome is constructed rather than genuine findings. It demonstrates this with an ElasticNet pipeline across student cohorts sharing identical instruments.

entry.title: MMA-Former: Multi-Window Mixture-of-Head Attention Transformer for Adaptive PNI Prediction in 3D MRI

author.name: Youngung Han, Induk Um, Kyeonghun Kim, Junga Kim, Hyunsu Go, Jaewon Jung, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Pa Hong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D MRI Transformer with a coarse-fine parallel structure and a window-specific mixture-of-head attention mechanism that routes each 3D window to specialized or common attention heads. It targets non-invasive prediction of perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma.

entry.title: Fail-Aware and Explainable Test Oracle Prediction

author.name: Yue Zhao, Binish Tanveer, Jelena Zdravkovic

entry.summary: Proposes a code-LLM-based discriminative oracle predictor that directly predicts whether a test prefix passes or fails, using losses that emphasize failing cases and grounding predictions in statement-level behavioral evidence. It contrasts with generating assertions that are often syntactically correct but ineffective at revealing bugs.

entry.title: BackgroundMellow: A Multi-Modal Cohesive Framework for Narrative-Driven Rich Cinematic Soundscape Generation

author.name: Ajitesh Jamulkar, Aritra Hazra

entry.summary: Presents a multi-modal framework for generating synchronized cinematic soundscapes from long-form narratives, using a master-specialist agent architecture that decomposes text into layered audio cues, generates each with a specialist model, and superimposes them. It addresses narrative cohesion, temporal alignment, and emotional depth that isolated text-to-audio systems lack.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for EO Regression Tasks: Building Height, Tree Canopy Height and Above-ground Biomass Estimation

author.name: Ritu Yadav, Andrea Nascetti, Yifang Ban

entry.summary: Addresses per-pixel reliability in Earth observation regression tasks such as building height, canopy height, and above-ground biomass estimation by modeling aleatoric uncertainty from year-long Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 time series. It proposes complementary uncertainty-estimation approaches for challenging skewed, saturating targets.

entry.title: Graph-Constrained Policy Learning for Extreme Clinical Code Prediction

author.name: Amritpal Singh, Sebastian Torres, Khawar Shakeel, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari

entry.summary: This work formulates extreme clinical ICD-10-CM code prediction as a finite-horizon graph traversal policy that descends a pruned code hierarchy selecting valid child nodes until billable leaf codes, guaranteeing structurally valid outputs and giving training signal for rare labels. It matters for improving rare-code prediction over flat multi-label classification.

entry.title: Cluster-Weighted EDMD

author.name: Lorenzo Tomaz, Judd Rosenblatt, Flavio Kicis, Thomas B. Jones, Diogo Schwerz de Lucena

entry.summary: Cluster-Weighted EDMD jointly learns a soft phase-space partition and per-cluster Koopman operators via an EM objective that assigns transitions by both geometric proximity and prediction residuals, so clusters specialize where local Koopman models are accurate. It matters for improving data-driven Koopman approximation of nonlinear dynamical systems.

entry.title: Generating Developable 3D Molecules via Pocket-Conditioned Diffusion and Property-Aware Optimization

author.name: Ruoxi Gao, Jiangweizhi Peng, Ziqi Chen, Frazier N. Baker, David C. Kombo, John L. Kane Jr., Andrew A. Scholte, Yi Li, Matthew J. LaMarche, Luigi I. Iconaru, Hans-Peter Biemann, Mingyi Hong, Xia Ning

entry.summary: conDitar-dev is a pocket-conditioned diffusion framework for structure-based drug design that decouples pocket and ligand learning, models multi-scale interactions, and optimizes for developability properties like ADMET rather than binding affinity alone. It has industry co-authors and targets practical de novo drug design. It aims at a more realistic optimization objective than affinity-only methods.

entry.title: What Makes a Representational Prior Work? Feature Families, Label-Free Invariances, and Critical Windows in Grokking

author.name: Gunner Levi Howe

entry.summary: Building on companion work linking grokking delay to representation formation, this paper dissects what makes a representational prior effective across content, supervision, and timing, finding that a fully label-free invariance prior generalizes more reliably than a label-supervised one. It uses 188 controlled runs on arithmetic tasks. It advances mechanistic understanding of grokking.

entry.title: The Spectrum Is Not Enough: When Context Helps Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This paper argues spectral predictability indices cannot answer whether adding context helps time-series forecasting, proving an impossibility result: any power-spectrum index is invariant under phase randomization, whereas the beyond-second-order value that retrieval and foundation models exploit is not. It isolates the claim with surrogate pairs fixing spectrum and marginal. It clarifies when context genuinely helps.

entry.title: Falsifying Causal Graphs With Outlier Events

author.name: William Roy Orchard, Philipp M. Faller, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This paper proposes falsifying candidate causal graphs by checking whether their implied outlier-event propagation is consistent with data, inverting the root-cause-analysis principle that weak outliers rarely cause strong ones and presenting the first statistical tests for this hypothesis. Authors include Amazon causal-inference researchers. It offers a ground-truth-free way to reject bad causal graphs.

entry.title: Deep4ge: DNN Training Trajectories for Fault Detection and Diagnosis

author.name: Sigma Jahan

entry.summary: Deep4ge is a controlled benchmark of 14,227 per-epoch training runs from 59 adapted TensorFlow/Keras programs, with faulty variants injected via 27 source-code transformations across seven fault categories. It supports fault detection and diagnosis for deep-learning systems using training trajectories. It fills a gap in public labeled fault datasets.

entry.title: CANDI: Contextual Alignment for Niche Domains Question Answering

author.name: Megha Chakraborty, Darssan L. Eswaramoorthi, Het Riteshkumar Shah, Madhur Thareja, Michelle A Ihetu, Harshul Raj Surana, Kaushik Roy, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: CANDI-QA is a benchmark evaluating LLMs on context-sensitive, user-aligned answers in specialized domains like medical and financial advisory, splitting into direct information-assistance questions and more nuanced categories requiring contextual grounding. It targets capabilities beyond general-knowledge QA. It aims to better measure domain-appropriate alignment.

entry.title: Graph-Based Detection of Disinformation Narrative Diffusion between Russian and Ukrainian Telegram Channels

author.name: Yuliia Vistak, Viktoriia Makovska, Vera Schmitt, Veronika Solopova

entry.summary: The paper proposes a graph-based framework combining weak supervision with propagation-graph analysis to detect disinformation narratives across Russian and Ukrainian Telegram channels. It clusters semantically related claims into narrative-level groups and models their diffusion across channels. It aims to catch coordinated amplification missed by post-level methods.

entry.title: CityBehavEx: A Scalable and Empirically Validated LLM-Assisted Urban Simulation Platform

author.name: Gustavo H. Santos, Aline Viana, Thiago H Silva

entry.summary: CityBehavEx is an LLM-assisted urban simulation platform that scales to city-size populations by combining established human mobility models with fine-tuned cross-encoders instead of invoking LLMs for every agent action. It generates mobility patterns better matching real spatial, temporal, and semantic distributions while supporting inspection and validation. It targets scalable, empirically grounded urban simulation.

entry.title: Comparing Semantic Navigation in Humans and Large Language Models using Natural Language Processing

author.name: Gabriel Paris-Colombo, Rodrigo M. Cabral-Carvalho, Felipe D. Toro-Hern\'andez

entry.summary: The paper compares semantic search dynamics in humans and three LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-Sonnet-4.5) using verbal fluency data and trajectory-based NLP metrics for entropy, step size, and dispersion. Humans show more variable, exploratory search than all models, and temperature tuning only partially aligns them. It quantifies human-LLM differences in semantic exploration.

entry.title: QUBO-Optimized Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering with Unconventional Solvers

author.name: Rahul Singh, Madhav Vadlamani

entry.summary: This paper formulates evidence-passage selection for retrieval-augmented QA as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization problem that jointly considers passage relevance and complementary coverage of decomposed information requirements. It targets multi-hop questions where top-k ranking misses complementary evidence, using unconventional (e.g., quantum-style) solvers. It reframes retrieval as set selection without an expensive LLM selector.

entry.title: WikiSTAR: A System for Shedding Light on the Hidden History of Scientific Wikipedia Articles

author.name: Omer Ehrlich, Nitzan Barzilay, Rona Aviram, Tom Hope

entry.summary: WikiSTAR is an interactive system that surfaces scientifically meaningful revisions in Wikipedia article histories by using an LLM classifier with an expert-designed multi-label taxonomy to tag edits like added technical terms, new findings, and narrative changes. It then offers interactive views over an article's full revision history. It makes the hidden evolution of scientific knowledge on Wikipedia legible.

entry.title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill

author.name: Yunxin Li, Jinchao Li, Shibo Su, Zhenran Xu, Chenrui Zhao, Tongshu Bian, Xiaoman Liang, Meishan Zhang, Baotian Hu, Min Zhang

entry.summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw proposes a Know-Route-Act-Reflect personal GUI assistant framework with self-evolving memory and skill to address cross-platform interaction and self-improvement gaps in an existing agent framework. It argues accumulated interaction experience directly improves execution accuracy and efficiency. It targets adaptive personal assistants across device ecosystems.

entry.title: Segregate, Refine, Integrate: Decomposing Multimodal Fusion for Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Alexios Filippakopoulos, Elias Kallioras, Nikolaos Xiros, Efthymios Georgiou, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: SeRIn is a multimodal fusion scheme that separates refining modality-specific signals from modeling cross-modal interactions by evolving unimodal representations along isolated pathways and deferring full cross-modal integration to a final prediction step. Ablations indicate structured interactions rather than added capacity drive gains. It targets multimodal sentiment analysis.

entry.title: Epistemic Stance Flexibility Probing: Measuring Prompt-Conditioned Register Shift in Large Language Models

author.name: Binwen Liu, Yilin Ren

entry.summary: ESFP is a behavioral benchmark of 104 controlled items testing whether LLMs shift epistemic register between neutrally attributing what experts believe and expressing their own stance on contested claims. It measures whether such register shifts occur coherently, a property not captured by accuracy, instruction-following, or safety benchmarks. It probes epistemic behavior of conversational agents.

entry.title: An Empirical Analysis of Continual Learning for Heterogeneous Medical Visual Question Answering

author.name: Mai A. Shaaban, Tausifa Jan Saleem, Alaa Mohamed, Dilnaz Utemissova, Ufaq Khan, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates continual-learning methods for medical visual question answering across heterogeneous tasks including classification, multi-label classification, detection, cell counting, and report generation. It studies catastrophic forgetting mitigation and sensitivity across diverse clinical objectives. It fills an underexplored gap in continual learning for medical vision-language models.

entry.title: ACZ-GSeg: Adaptive Concentric Zone-based Two-stage Ground Segmentation for LiDAR Point Clouds

author.name: Ge Zhang Chunyang Wang Bin Liu

entry.summary: ACZ-GSeg is a two-stage ground segmentation method for LiDAR point clouds using an adaptive concentric zone model that dynamically sets sector counts per ring for balanced point distributions. It targets under-segmentation from sparse long-range points and ground undulations in autonomous navigation.

entry.title: ProtoPointNet: Prototype-Based Interpretable Classification of 3D Dental Point Clouds with Verifiable Spatial Activations

author.name: George V. Jose, Thao Liang Chiam, Toby Hughes, Dilan Patel, Alan Brook, Lyle J. Palmer, Nikhil Cherian Kurian

entry.summary: ProtoPointNet is a prototype-based interpretable classifier for dental occlusion from registered upper-lower intraoral point cloud pairs, encoding each point with geometry, curvature, and inter-arch displacement descriptors. Axis-specific prototype heads support multi-task classification with verifiable spatial activations.

entry.title: MQAdapter: Multi-Modal Quantum Adapter for Coarse-to-Fine VLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Yumiao Zhao, Bo Jiang, Min Lu, Xiao Wang, Jin Tang

entry.summary: MQAdapter proposes a multi-modal quantum adapter for coarse-to-fine vision-language model fine-tuning, targeting the gap where VLMs achieve high Top-K but weak Top-1 accuracy in few-shot fine-grained classification. It refines fine-grained visual representations by exploiting semantically similar categories.

entry.title: RealSkin: Spatio-Spectral Partial Neural Adjoint Maps for Image-to-3D Attribute Transfer

author.name: Jing Li, Yawei Luo, Xiangze Meng, Ying Li, Tieru Wu, Rui Ma

entry.summary: RealSkin is a self-supervised framework for transferring visual attributes from real images onto synthetic 3D surfaces using partial neural adjoint maps that optimize correspondence in a learned spectral domain guided by spatial correspondences. It addresses resolution mismatch and discrete correspondence limitations in photorealistic asset creation.

entry.title: Traceback Translators Against Forgetting in Continual Fake Speech Detection

author.name: Enrico Gottardis, Mattia Tamiazzo, Simone Milani

entry.summary: This paper combats catastrophic forgetting in continual fake-speech detection using domain translators within a frozen detector that remap new feature spaces back to original ones via a traceback translator network. It maintains detection across evolving generative models while reducing computation versus retraining.

entry.title: Text-Aided Multi-Modal Panoptic Symbol Spotting for CAD Floor Plan Drawings

author.name: Yan Gong, Bohao Li, Bowen Du, Junchen Ye

entry.summary: This paper presents a text-aided multimodal panoptic symbol spotting method for CAD floor plans that better models the complex syntax and hierarchical semantics of textual annotations alongside graphical primitives. It addresses the underexploitation of text in primitive-centric spotting approaches.

entry.title: MBTI: A Multi-Branch Efficient Fine-Tuning Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification with Foundation Models

author.name: Mingzhen Xu, Haonan Guo, Di Wang, Yinghua Qu, Zhiliang Zhou, Lei Zhang, Huiwen Yao, Rui Zhao, Fengxiang Wang, Gang Wan, Bo Du, Liangpei Zhang

entry.summary: MBTI is a multi-branch efficient fine-tuning framework for hyperspectral image classification that adapts foundation models across sensors with varying spectral band configurations without compressing or reshaping the original spectra. It preserves local spectral continuity that existing adaptation strategies tend to discard.

entry.title: ExtraGS: Enhancing Endoscopic View Extrapolation via Diffusion-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Cheng-Tai Hsieh, Jiwei Shan, Han Fang, Jianshu Hu, Tao Ni, Lijun Han, Yutong Ban, Shing Shin Cheng, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: ExtraGS enhances endoscopic view extrapolation via diffusion-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting, using an uncertainty-guided virtual camera to reduce severe artifacts when rendering beyond sparse training trajectories. It targets the limited endoscope field of view that leaves surrounding anatomy unobserved during robot-assisted surgery.

entry.title: Metric-Guided Synthetic Image Data Rendering for Deep Learning compatible with Agentic AI

author.name: Martina Radoynova, Samuel Pantze, Trina De, Ulrik G\"unther, Artur Yakimovich

entry.summary: Presents GraNatPy, a Python package with quantitative metrics to guide 3D rendering of synthetic training images so they better match real data. Shows that improved realism, diversity, and scale correlate with higher zero-shot detection performance.

entry.title: Enabling 24-hour Agricultural Robotics: Unsupervised Day-to-Night Cross-Modal Image Translation for Nighttime Visual Navigation

author.name: Robel Mamo, Rajitha de Silva, Grzegorz Cielniak, Taeyeong Choi

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised image translation framework converting daytime RGB plant-row images into near-infrared nighttime counterparts, enabling reuse of daytime labels for nighttime agricultural robot navigation without pixel-level supervision.

entry.title: Calibrated Selective Prediction Using Deep Ensembles for ROI-Based Thyroid Nodule Ultrasound Classification Under Dataset Shift: A Retrospective Evaluation

author.name: Md. Sadibul Hasan Sadib, Md. Mohayminul Mukit, Rahmatul Kabir Rasel Sarker, Tahmid Alam Tamim, Md. Monir Hossain Shimul

entry.summary: Develops a calibrated deep ensemble for thyroid nodule ultrasound classification that provides uncertainty estimates and selective referral, validated under dataset shift on an independent external dataset. Emphasizes clinically trustworthy triage over raw accuracy.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Source Retinal Fluid Segmentation in OCT

author.name: Animesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents an attention-guided TransUNet that segments three retinal fluid types across four independent OCT scanners with domain-adaptive normalization and pixel-level uncertainty. Notably, the uncertainty is elevated exactly where expert graders disagree, providing a clinical triage signal.

entry.title: Autonomous Tracking and Terminal Guidance of Moving Targets for Fixed-Wing UAVs

author.name: Wei-Hao Liou, Teng-Hu Cheng

entry.summary: Presents a unified control framework for fixed-wing UAVs with a pan-tilt camera that spans target acquisition, NMPC-based tracking fusing YOLO detections with inertial data via an unscented Kalman filter, and a terminal guidance phase using control-barrier-function constraints for reliable visual contact.

entry.title: Toy Models of Initialisation Effects on RL Dynamics

author.name: Edward James Young

entry.summary: A follow-up from Geodesic analyzing a toy model of RL learning dynamics, focusing on how initialization from the pre-RL checkpoint shapes learned solutions through rich-get-richer effects and underspecified behaviors. It argues that pretraining and warm-start SFT strongly determine alignment-relevant outcomes of RL post-training.

entry.title: GRATE: Temporal Extensions for Inductive KG Foundation Models via Gated Rotary Attention

author.name: Jiaxin Pan, Osama Mohammed, Daniel Hern\'andez, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: GRATE adds temporal transfer to inductive knowledge-graph foundation models via a gated rotary-attention entity-side message function that encodes relative time differences without adding learnable parameters. It enables transfer to temporal knowledge graphs with disjoint entity, relation, and timestamp vocabularies.

entry.title: Opti-Agent-Bench: Benchmarking End-to-End Optimization R&D Agents on Real-World Business Problems

author.name: Yongchang Fu, Xinjie Huang, Chengjun Dai, Chengzhe Feng, Junshao Zhang, Hong Zhu

entry.summary: Opti-Agent-Bench is an end-to-end benchmark evaluating LLM agents across the full optimization R&D pipeline, from business-language descriptions through mathematical modeling, algorithm selection, and code implementation to solution reporting. It emphasizes business-semantic authenticity with anti-template traps to defeat pattern matching, unlike benchmarks using pre-structured formulations.

entry.title: CLIR-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series

author.name: Frank Nie, Ethan B. Liu, Yuan Zhu, Loe Yan, Wei Fan, Jindong Han

entry.summary: Introduces CLIR-Bench, a benchmark for multimodal question answering over irregular, sparse, asynchronous clinical ICU time series with 6,600 QA instances. It tests whether models can ground answers in genuinely irregular temporal observations rather than static or regularly sampled data.

entry.title: Faithful by Design: Evaluating and Improving LLM-Generated Clinical Trial Summaries for Multi-Stakeholder Audiences

author.name: Robert Williams

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for measuring faithfulness of LLM-generated clinical trial summaries across provider, patient, and payer audiences, with 200 stratified trials and a six-dimension annotation schema. It establishes baselines for GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash on 1,800 summaries.

entry.title: Answer-Conditioned Chain-of-Thought Distillation for Few-Shot Industrial Vision with Small VLMs

author.name: Shubham Rao

entry.summary: Introduces answer-conditioned chain-of-thought distillation to adapt small vision-language models to new industrial inspection tasks with minimal labeled data. A frontier model generates justified explanations conditioned on correct labels, and a 3B model is fine-tuned on these via LoRA.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Convolution with Optimal Transport Attention Effect on Multivariate Time Series

author.name: HaoChong Fu, Jian Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a time-series architecture combining multi-scale convolution with a Sinkhorn optimal-transport attention mechanism on inverted variable embeddings to capture cross-variate relationships and suppress noise. It targets multi-granularity pattern extraction in multivariate time series.

entry.title: LoSA-Net: A Localized and Scale-Adaptive Network for Boundary-Sensitive Prediction of Perineural Invasion in 3D MRI

author.name: Youngung Han, Hyunsu Go, Kyeonghun Kim, Induk Um, Junga Kim, Jaewon Jung, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Pa Hong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Presents a localized, scale-adaptive network for boundary-sensitive prediction of perineural invasion in 3D MRI, using neighborhood attention with head-wise mixing and scale-adaptive feature mixing to preserve fine nerve-aligned detail. It addresses attenuation of subtle cues by downsampling and global aggregation.

entry.title: AutoMatBench: An Automatic Optimization Toolkit for the Acceleration of Material Properties Prediction Benchmarking

author.name: Hongxiao Li, Wanling Gao

entry.summary: AutoMatBench extends the MatBench materials-property-prediction benchmark with automated optimization and out-of-distribution evaluation, since standard benchmarks only measure in-distribution performance that overstates readiness for new-material discovery. It matters for making materials ML evaluation more realistic.

entry.title: An Explainable Agentic System for Detection of Conversational Scams with Summary-Based Memory

author.name: Ahmed Omar Salim Adnan, Yogananda Manjunath, Shivanjali Khare

entry.summary: This paper presents an explainable agentic system with summary-based memory for detecting multi-week conversational scams and introduces ConScamBench-278, a multi-category benchmark spanning eight scam types. It matters because existing scam detectors focus on isolated messages and miss slowly building trust exploitation.

entry.title: Qubit-Efficient Quantum Search for Hyperdimensional Decomposition via Logarithmic Encoding

author.name: Sanggeon Yun, Hyunwoo Oh, Ryozo Masukawa, Raheeb Hassan, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: This paper proposes a qubit-efficient quantum framework for hyperdimensional-computing decomposition that reduces representation cost from linear to logarithmic in dimension using logarithmic hypervector and binding encodings plus a reversible construction, retaining a quadratic search advantage. It matters for making quantum HDC decomposition more feasible at scale.

entry.title: Gradient Flow Dynamics and Implicit Bias of Diagonal Linear Networks under Infinitesimal Initialization

author.name: Jiajie Zhao, Jianxing Wang, Junjie Yang, Zhiwei Bai, Yaoyu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper extends prior gradient-flow analysis of diagonal linear networks to deep and broader two-layer cases under infinitesimal initialization, proving the training trajectory matches an explicit algorithm converging to a modified L1-minimization solution. It characterizes the implicit bias of these architectures. It is a theoretical contribution to understanding optimization dynamics.

entry.title: Differentiable Clone-Structured Causal Graphs for End-to-End Cognitive Map Learning from Image Sequences

author.name: Arash Nikzad, Sasan Sarbishegi, Ali Dasmeh, Muhammad Asif, Parsa Gharavi, Erik Husom, Sagar Sen, Andrew B. Lehr, Olivier Penacchio, Ana Clemente, Tristan M. St\"ober

entry.summary: gradCSCG reformulates the clone-structured causal graph hippocampus model into a fully differentiable module coupled to a learned vector-quantized encoder, enabling end-to-end cognitive-map learning from raw image sequences without a predefined discrete alphabet. It bridges neuroscience-inspired mapping with deep learning. It targets interpretable world-model learning.

entry.title: Learning Mechanistic Reasoning for Chemical Reactions with Large Language Models

author.name: Xingyu Dang, Haocheng Tang, Junmei Wang, Yanjun Li

entry.summary: This paper teaches LLMs step-by-step reaction mechanism reasoning (elementary-reaction sequences) rather than coarse name-reaction product prediction, aligning mechanistic deduction with LLM reasoning paradigms to reduce physical inconsistencies and hallucinations. It aims to improve fundamental chemical intelligence. It bridges reasoning LLMs and mechanistic chemistry.

entry.title: Did We Actually Fix It? An Independent Adversarial Stress-Test of Post-Point-Adjustment Evaluation Metrics for Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zongye Lyu

entry.summary: This paper provides an independent adversarial audit of replacement evaluation metrics for time-series anomaly detection, stress-testing twelve adopted metrics against trivial and no-skill score generators across six benchmarks under a pre-registered gameability criterion. It asks whether the field's move away from point-adjustment actually fixed the metric-inflation problem. It is a rigorous meta-evaluation contribution.

entry.title: Deep Learning-based Surrogate Modelling of the LOD Method for Multiscale Problems

author.name: Marc Haltmayer, Jaemin Seo, Yuseung Lee, Sungyeop Lee, Jaehoon Jeong, Jae Yong Lee

entry.summary: This work builds a deep-learning surrogate for the Localized Orthogonal Decomposition method to solve elliptic PDEs with rough, high-contrast coefficients where neural operators typically struggle. It aims to combine LOD accuracy with data-driven speedups for multiscale problems. It targets scientific computing applications.

entry.title: Physically Consistent Parameter Inference: Transparent Machine Learning Emulation in High Energy Physics and Cosmology

author.name: Jorge Alda, Jacobo Asorey, Alejandro Mir, Siannah Pe\~naranda

entry.summary: This work presents an XGBoost-based framework to emulate expensive, non-Gaussian likelihood landscapes in high energy physics and cosmology global fits, aiming for efficient and interpretable confidence-region resolution. It validates on B-meson flavour anomaly analyses. It offers a transparent ML surrogate for parameter inference in physics.

entry.title: Learning-enabled Acceleration of Scenario-based Model Predictive Control

author.name: Trinh Tran, Binh Nguyen, Truong X. Nghiem

entry.summary: The paper accelerates scenario-based model predictive control by combining ADMM with Moreau-envelope learning and parallel computing, decomposing scenario-dependent dynamics into consensus subproblems. It aims to retain accuracy while making SBMPC feasible in real time. It targets control under uncertainty.

entry.title: Causal Supervision of Attention for Affective Behaviour Analysis

author.name: Nemanja Ra\v{s}ajski, Konstantinos Makantasis, Antonios Liapis, Georgios N. Yannakakis

entry.summary: This paper adds causal supervision to attention mechanisms for affective behaviour analysis to reduce reliance on spurious cues like identity, illumination, and pose in the ABAW multi-task challenge. It targets more robust valence-arousal, expression, and action unit prediction in the wild.

entry.title: Data Safety: Synthetic Data Quality Analysis Using CIFAKE Dataset

author.name: Kuniko Paxton, Amila Akagi\'c, Koorosh Aslansefat, Dhavalkumar Thakker, Yiannis Papadopoulos

entry.summary: This study systematically analyzes how synthetic images differ from real ones for training image classifiers using the CIFAKE dataset, examining high-dimensional features, low-level color statistics, and effects on the training process. It probes when synthetic data is safe to substitute for scarce real images.

entry.title: Adaptive Cross-Modal Fusion with Sparse Attention for Pedestrian Crossing Intention Prediction

author.name: Md Mahfuzur Rahman, Pengzhan Zhou, A F M Abdun Noor, Md Imam Ahasan, Kah Ong Michael Goh, S. M. Hasan Mahmud, Md Mustafizur Rahman, Kaixin Gao

entry.summary: ADAPT is a multimodal transformer for pedestrian crossing intention prediction that fuses RGB, local depth, semantic maps, global depth, and ego-vehicle kinematics with adaptive sparse attention. It aims to capture complementary visual and motion cues while reducing redundant inter-modal interactions.

entry.title: Statistical Non-linear Reconstruction Loss for Image Anomaly Detection

author.name: Nguyen Minh Tri, Hoang Khuong Duy, Huynh Cong Viet Ngu

entry.summary: Introduces a sigmoid-based non-linear reconstruction loss that suppresses high-magnitude features to prevent reconstruction models from faithfully rebuilding anomalies, plus a statistical calibration scheme for the suppression strength. Targets unsupervised image anomaly detection.

entry.title: Enough is Enough: Measuring Diminishing returns to benchmark size with Item Response Theory

author.name: bpomo

entry.summary: This project applies Item Response Theory to quantify the diminishing informational returns of adding more questions to a benchmark, using the notion of Fisher information to measure how much a benchmark actually discriminates model ability. It offers a principled way to think about optimal benchmark size.

entry.title: Faithful, Not Corrective: Message-Format Effects in Multi-Hop Agent Relays Are Tier-Dependent

author.name: Zayx Shawn

entry.summary: The paper builds a controlled relay testbed where atomic facts are re-encoded across six hops in five message formats to test whether structure helps or hurts multi-agent information handoff. It finds that format effects are tier-dependent and that faithful copy fidelity, not one-shot generation, dominates in multi-hop relays.

entry.title: Replicating Belief, Not Bits: Epistemic State Replication for Agentic Systems

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: This paper argues that state-machine replication for agentic distributed systems should replicate belief and semantic equivalence rather than bitwise identical states, since stochastic model-driven replicas can diverge in tokens yet reach equivalent decisions. It proposes epistemic state replication to preserve execution flexibility.

entry.title: IdeaTrail: Full-Process Agent Trajectories for Scientific Ideation

author.name: Hengquan Guo

entry.summary: IdeaTrail is a dataset of 1,170 multi-turn trajectories capturing the full scientific ideation process, recording tool use, gathered evidence, intermediate artifacts, and reasoning from literature search through proposal construction. It is synthesized from human-selected research papers via a generator pipeline to capture the process rather than only final artifacts.

entry.title: Cross-Layer Misalignment Detection in Agent Skills: A Progressive Loading-Aware Contrastive Learning Approach

author.name: Chengjun Zhang, Yang Gao, Jianna Hur, Jingjing Zhang, Sagar Samtani

entry.summary: This work targets cross-layer misalignment in agent skills, where a skill's brief metadata does not match its true behavior, using progressive loading-aware hierarchical contrastive learning to detect inconsistencies. It models the layered structure of skills to learn cross-layer consistency for safer third-party skill selection.

entry.title: A Foundation Model for Multimodal Event Sequences in Financial Applications

author.name: Nikita Rusakov, Vladislav Meshkov, Konstantin Zorin, Gleb Zaripov, Alexander Uglov, Alexey Vasilev, Anton Klenitskiy

entry.summary: Presents a foundation transformer pretrained on multimodal user event sequences (transactions, digital interactions) unified into a chronological stream via next-event prediction, producing general-purpose representations for financial prediction tasks. It replaces separate task-specific feature-engineered models.

entry.title: Robust, Scalable Detection of Text Containment in Large Web-Crawled Corpora

author.name: Lars Henry Berge Olsen, Pierre Lison, Martin Jullum, Mark Anderson

entry.summary: Presents FindMyText, an open-source, distributed tool for detecting whether a text appears within large web-crawled corpora, extending document fingerprinting to capture chains of matching fingerprints for near-verbatim detection. It is aimed at verifying copyrighted material in training corpora.

entry.title: Adaptive Model Compression (AMC): Saliency-Driven Resource Allocation for Ultra-Low-Power Transformer Inference

author.name: Jiayin Hu, Kai Yuan, Vanessa Hu, Xuetao Yin, Jianhua Li, Sean Suchter

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Model Compression, a saliency-driven framework that dynamically allocates hardware resources by token importance, processing high-saliency tokens at full precision while aggressively reducing rank and bit-width for less important ones. It reports 59.2% energy reduction and 2.24x throughput on 45nm CMOS.

entry.title: Cost of Reasoning in non-English Languages: A Case Study on Japanese

author.name: Yuu Jinnai

entry.summary: Studies the feasibility and cost of training reasoning models that reason in Japanese rather than English, developing a Japanese-reasoning variant of Qwen-3-Swallow-8B via GRPO and evaluating on coding, math, and science. It examines the performance tradeoff of reasoning in a lower-resource language for interpretability and safety.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Dataset of MCP Implementations on GitHub

author.name: Benny Toeppe, Amine Barrak, Emna Ksontini

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale, evidence-based dataset of real-world Model Context Protocol implementations mined from GitHub, with 3,238 candidate repositories filtered and validated and each classified by operational role. It offers a systematic empirical view of how the rapidly adopted MCP standard is implemented.

entry.title: PhysMRV: Physical Memory Retrieval and Verification for Physics Plausibility Reasoning

author.name: Wenyuan Wang, Lianyu Hu, Hao Wang, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes PhysMRV, a training-free framework that builds a hierarchical memory bank from training videos and verifies physical plausibility, improving video-language models' reasoning about object interactions and causal dynamics. Unlike retrieval-augmented VLMs it transforms videos into structured physical memory rather than retrieving similar clips.

entry.title: SynthDocBench: Controlled Benchmark for Long-Context Visual Document Understanding

author.name: Abhigya Verma, Khyati Mahajan, Amit Kumar Saha, Shruthan Radhakrishna, Sagar Davasam, Vikas Yadav, Sai Rajeswar Mudumba

entry.summary: Introduces SynthDocBench, a fully synthetic benchmark for long-context visual document understanding that independently and combinatorially varies document length, layout complexity, modality composition, and question type. This controlled design enables attributing VLM failures to specific factors rather than confounded real-world variation.

entry.title: Large Language Models in Misinformation Ecosystems: Misuse, Defense, and Vulnerability

author.name: Lingwei Wei, Dou Hu, Wei Zhou, Songlin Hu, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a role-layer framework unifying how LLMs act as attackers, defenders, and vulnerable components across content, social contexts, evidence environments, and verification workflows in misinformation ecosystems. It organizes LLM-enabled attacks and defenses as an ecosystem-level security challenge rather than a content-only problem.

entry.title: When Does Restricting a Coding Agent to execute_code Help? A Regime $\times$ Agent-Design Ablation

author.name: Hong Yang, Qi Yu, Travis Desell

entry.summary: Runs a crossed ablation (baseline / bash-only / code-only) on coding agents to determine when restricting an agent to a single execute_code MCP tool helps, holding model, harness, and prompts fixed across two agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI) on synthetic and SWE-bench Mini tasks. It resolves contradictory prior claims about which tool surface matters.

entry.title: Learning from Local Walks on Dynamic Graphs with Bandit Feedback

author.name: Sourav Chakraborty, Amit Kiran Rege, Claire Monteleoni, Lijun Chen

entry.summary: Studies stochastic multi-armed bandits on dynamic graphs where arms are vertices with time-varying edges and the learner may only move to adjacent nodes, decoupling best-arm identification from reachability. It identifies a sliding-window mixing condition ensuring stable exploration and navigation and proves sublinear expected regret for local explore-then-commit algorithms.

entry.title: DiffUE: Enhancing Utility-Unlearnability Trade-off of Unlearnable Examples via Diffusion Autoencoders

author.name: Syed Irfan Ali Meerza, Oktay Ozturk, Amir Sadovnik, Jian Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DiffUE, which generates unlearnable examples via diffusion autoencoders operating in semantic latent space rather than pixel-space noise, aiming to resist relearning strategies (adversarial training, transformations, compression) while preserving image utility. It targets the privacy trade-off between protecting scraped personal images and maintaining perceptual quality.

entry.title: CGS: Configurable Graph Summarization with Bounded Neighborhood Loss and Query Support

author.name: Shubhadip Mitra, Sona Elza Simon, C Oswald, Arnab Bhattacharya, Arindam Pal

entry.summary: Proposes a configurable graph summarization method that lets users trade off lossless versus lossy compression, tolerable neighborhood loss, and loss type while supporting multiple graph queries with high accuracy on the summary. It targets scalability for growing graph datasets.

entry.title: An Empirical Study for Android-to-OpenHarmony GUI Test Migration

author.name: Yakun Zhang, Xinjia Chen, Yiyun Chen, Yuxia Zhang, Mingyi Zhou, Xiang Gao, Shaokun Zhang, Li Li, Yunming Ye

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic empirical study of migrating GUI test cases from Android to OpenHarmony, constructing a benchmark of 36 commercial apps with 108 manual test cases and evaluating state-of-the-art migration approaches. It provides empirical guidance previously lacking for the OpenHarmony ecosystem.

entry.title: Automated Textbook Auditing with Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Ciprian Cristescu, Adrian-Marius Dumitran, Angela-Liliana Dumitran, Gabriel Stefan

entry.summary: Presents a modular multi-agent LLM pipeline for auditing educational materials, combining a factual-and-technical track using specialized agents with web search and a linguistic-quality track to produce structured human-reviewable reports from textbook PDFs. It targets simultaneous checking of factual accuracy, technical correctness, and language quality.

entry.title: A Multimodal Dataset for Large Language Model Applications in the Energy Domain

author.name: Costas Mylonas, Magda Foti

entry.summary: Presents an open-access multimodal corpus for energy-sector LLM applications integrating around 50,000 texts, 20,000 images, 25 million time-series records, and 2 million geospatial entries harmonized into ready-to-use formats. It spans policy, scientific and news texts, imagery, electricity measurements, weather, and infrastructure data.

entry.title: Repairing Shape-Prior Shortcuts in Long-Range Single-Shot Fringe Projection Profilometry

author.name: Adam Haroon, Cody Fleming, Beiwen Li

entry.summary: PhiCalNet fixes a shape-prior shortcut in single-shot fringe projection profilometry by outputting a wrapped-phase representation and mapping it to depth through a fixed differentiable calibration layer, architecturally removing the shortcut instead of penalizing it via loss. It matters as a case study of correcting shortcut learning through architecture.

entry.title: BattVAE-GP: Generative Modeling of Long-Horizon Battery Degradation with Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Raghvender Raghvender, Mahdi Abid, Ferran Brosa Planella, Charles Delacourt, Arnaud Demorti\`ere

entry.summary: BattVAE-GP is a hybrid physics-probabilistic surrogate that encodes electrochemical battery-degradation trajectories into a VAE latent space organized by cycle progression and charging protocol, then predicts long-horizon degradation at unseen charging rates with uncertainty quantification. It matters for cheaply exploring battery operating conditions over long cycle life.

entry.title: Self-Evolving In-Context Learning for Direct Pilot-to-Beamformer Design in MU-MISO Systems

author.name: Yubo Zhang, Xiaodong Wang

entry.summary: This work develops a self-evolving in-context learning framework for direct pilot-to-beamformer design in multi-user MISO systems, using an ICL Transformer with pilot and beamformer encoder-decoders, curriculum learning from supervised imitation to unsupervised sum-rate maximization, and a self-evolving context mechanism handling multiple channel models without retraining. It matters for adaptable wireless beamforming.

entry.title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models

author.name: Muhammad Ashad Kabir, Sirajam Munira

entry.summary: This study evaluates feasibility of large language models for zero-shot early chronic kidney disease screening using a feature-guided framework built on clinically meaningful, readily available community-based features, without dataset-specific training. It matters for deployable screening in resource-limited settings robust to distribution shifts.

entry.title: Fisher Rank Inflation: A Spectral Signature of Memorization under Label Noise

author.name: Satwik Bathula, Anand A. Joshi

entry.summary: The authors identify Fisher Rank Inflation, a transient spectral expansion in per-example last-layer gradients that signals when networks begin memorizing corrupted labels under label noise. They derive a leave-one-out attribution formula linking spectral mass injection to memorization. It offers a diagnostic for the clean-then-memorize dynamic.

entry.title: Sample Efficient Generative Optimization for Molecular Design

author.name: Sarina Kopf, Cristina Nevado, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: SEGO frames molecular optimization as sample-efficient Bayesian optimization over adaptively generated molecules, using a surrogate to hypothesize promising chemical regions, steering a generative model to propose candidates there, then updating on evaluations. It targets tight-budget drug and materials discovery. Sample efficiency is the central metric.

entry.title: What Does Goodness Measure? A Likelihood-Ratio Account of Forward-Forward Learning

author.name: Paolo Giannitrapani

entry.summary: This work gives a generative-model interpretation of the Forward-Forward algorithm, showing its squared goodness is the sufficient statistic of a likelihood-ratio test between scale-differing populations and its threshold is the test boundary. It reframes FF heuristics as principled statistics, generalizing to Mahalanobis and heavy-tailed cases. It deepens theoretical understanding of local learning rules.

entry.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques

author.name: Daehoon Gwak, Minhyung Lee, Junwoo Park, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: This survey organizes efficient-inference techniques for masked diffusion large language models, covering algorithmic, architectural, and system-level acceleration and disentangling the trade-offs that conflate end-to-end latency in existing benchmarks. It argues parallel generation alone does not yield practical speedups. It provides a structured map of diffusion-LLM acceleration.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Learning of Gaussian Sobolev Operators

author.name: Ben Adcock, Michael Griebel, Gregor Maier

entry.summary: This paper presents Hermite-PCA approximation, a fully data-driven algorithm for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity, addressing the intrinsic curse of sample complexity for finitely regular operators. It provides provable approximation guarantees in reasonable time. It contributes to operator-learning theory.

entry.title: SymbOmni: Evolving Agentic Omni Models via Symbolic Concept Learning

author.name: Jinxiu Liu, Jianru Li, Tanqing Kuang, Xuanming Liu, Kangfu Mei, Yandong Wen, Weiyang Liu

entry.summary: SymbOmni is an agentic omni-model for visual generation that addresses the perpetual-novice problem by structuring experience into reusable symbolic concepts stored in a Symbolic Concept Box, enabling cumulative learning and better compositional generalization instead of from-scratch reasoning per task. It targets multimodal creation across text-to-image and video. Symbolic concept learning is the core mechanism.

entry.title: Robust In-Hand Manipulation via Priors in Reinforcement Learning and Mechanical Design

author.name: Yifei Chen, Shihan Lu, Ed Colgate, Kevin Lynch

entry.summary: This paper improves reinforcement-learned in-hand manipulation without external sensing by injecting two physics priors: a global grasp-quality reward-shaping term from classical grasp analysis and a local fingertip-curvature contact-geometry prior encoded in mechanical design. It aims to maintain well-conditioned grasps for sustained rolling. It combines RL with mechanical-design priors for robustness.

entry.title: FlashDiff: Efficient Regional Execution and Scheduling for Diffusion Model Serving

author.name: Yaqi Qiao, Ping He, Songrun Xie, Ayush Barik, Chensong Zhang, Zhengzhong Tu, Fan Lai

entry.summary: FlashDiff is a diffusion-model serving system that improves inference efficiency through adaptive regional execution and scheduling, avoiding the activation-exchange communication overhead that undermines existing multi-GPU parallelization of the all-region denoising pattern. It targets high-throughput serving of image, video, and audio diffusion. Serving-system efficiency is the focus.

entry.title: ANGLE: Angular Neural Generative Learning via Engression

author.name: Rajdeep Pathak, Archi Roy, Tanujit Chakraborty

entry.summary: ANGLE is a lightweight deep generative framework for non-parametric distributional regression on circular data (angles and directions), learning full conditional distributions via a generalized circular energy score loss. It addresses cases where mean regression is geometrically misleading for multimodal or skewed angular responses. It has theoretical propriety guarantees.

entry.title: G-SHARE: A Guideline-Based Structured Reasoning Framework for Human-Factor Event Diagnosis

author.name: Xingyu Xiao, Mao Du, Jiejuan Tong, Jingang Liang, Haitao Wang

entry.summary: G-SHARE operationalizes a nine-step nuclear-plant human-factor event diagnosis guideline into a multi-stage LLM pipeline with evidence extraction, stepwise reasoning, and post-hoc consistency repair. It aims to make LLM diagnostics align with formal guidelines and avoid logically inconsistent conclusions. It targets safety-critical operational event analysis.

entry.title: Hybrid Continual Learning for Low-Resource Australian Aboriginal Language Identification

author.name: Pravina Mylvaganam, Ting Dang, Eliathamby Ambikairajah, Vidhyasaharan Sethu, Jingyao Wu

entry.summary: This work proposes two hybrid continual-learning methods, replay-augmented elastic weight consolidation and constraint-guided knowledge distillation, to adapt pretrained speech models for endangered Australian Aboriginal language identification under extreme data scarcity. It mitigates catastrophic forgetting during transfer. It supports language revitalization and digital inclusion.

entry.title: Entropy in Semantic Memory Navigation in Blind and Sighted Individuals: The Effect of Visual Experience

author.name: Felipe D. Toro-Hern\'andez, Rodrigo Lagos, Sergio E. Chaigneau

entry.summary: This study measures semantic memory navigation in blind versus sighted individuals via a property-listing task, computing embedding-based semantic entropy to capture retrieval predictability. Mixed models reveal distinct navigation patterns, with sighted individuals showing higher entropy for abstract than concrete concepts. It tests whether conceptual grounding requires visual experience.

entry.title: RCWT: Measuring Task-Budget Displacement from Coordination Content in LLM Calls

author.name: Brenda Lelis, Rodrigo Cabral-Carvalho

entry.summary: RCWT is a controlled protocol measuring how coordination content (shared state, prior discussion, tool outputs, role instructions) crowds out task tokens within a fixed context budget in multi-agent and memory-augmented LLM systems. It varies coordination content while controlling budget, position, and task family. It quantifies a practical task-budget displacement effect.

entry.title: Fin-Analyst at FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: A Live Hybrid Trading Agent with LLM Specialists and Rule-Based Signals

author.name: Mohotarema Rashid, Lingzi Hong, Junhua Ding, K. S. M. Tozammel Hossain

entry.summary: Fin-Analyst is a hybrid trading agent combining an eight-specialist LLM pipeline over diverse financial data with a rule-based signal vote, submitted to a shared financial evaluation task. It reportedly ranked first on Tesla equity with strong returns and Sharpe while a Bitcoin vote stayed flat above a falling baseline. It provides live-deployment evidence for LLM trading agents.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Detection: A Multi-Dimensional Taxonomy of Cancer Misinformation on Reddit

author.name: Aria Pessianzadeh, Pooriya Jamie, Naima Sultana, Georgia Himmelstein, Yuliya Zektser, Patricia Ganz, Homa Hosseinmardi, Amir Ghasemian, Rezvaneh Rezapour

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-dimensional taxonomy for cancer misinformation on Reddit across breast, lung, colon, and prostate cancer, capturing seven dimensions including presence, information type, risk level, and stance. It evaluates multiple LLMs against expert-annotated data for scalable analysis beyond binary detection. It aims to characterize misinformation with clinically meaningful nuance.

entry.title: FAIR GraphRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Approach for Semantic Data Analysis

author.name: Marlena Fl\"uh, Soo-Yon Kim, Carolin Victoria Schneider, Sandra Geisler

entry.summary: FAIR GraphRAG integrates FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles and FAIR Digital Objects into graph-based retrieval-augmented generation for semantic data analysis in complex domains like medicine. It addresses the lack of structured FAIRification in existing RAG knowledge resources. It aims for standards-compliant information retrieval.

entry.title: Demonstration of the common dual-channel feature decoupling characteristic of front-door mediation causal inference methods in whole-slice image classification

author.name: Zhirui Zhang, Tianhang Nan, Yong Ding, Zhuolun Song, Dayu Hu, Xiaoyu Cui

entry.summary: This paper proposes and empirically supports two hypotheses about front-door causal-inference multiple-instance learning for whole-slide image classification, framing it as an independent parallel classification channel that eliminates false feature correlations. It relates channel divergence to effectiveness in removing spurious associations.

entry.title: Physically Aware Radiomics Without Interpolation: Disentangling Voxel Geometry and Signal Modification in CT and MRI

author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Sergio Rubio-Mart\'in, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: This work develops a voxel-spacing-aware radiomics framework that incorporates physical geometry into texture computation without resampling, disentangling voxel geometry from interpolation-induced signal changes in anisotropic CT and MRI. It compares native, isotropic-resampled, spacing-aware, and fake-isotropic configurations.

entry.title: Virtual Chromoendscopy with Tunable Visibility Enhancement

author.name: Yuhi Kanno, Yusuke Monno, Sho Suzuki, Tomohiro Tada, Masatoshi Okutomi

entry.summary: V-ECE combines virtual chromoendoscopy with tunable image enhancement to synthesize dye-sprayed appearance and further boost visibility of gastric lesions from standard endoscopy images without physical dye. This avoids the cost and time of preparing and spraying indigo carmine.

entry.title: Edge-Aware Thermal Infrared UAV Swarm Tracking

author.name: Yu-Hsi Chen

entry.summary: This single-author work presents an edge-aware thermal infrared tracker for UAV swarms that improves on the Kalman filter's constant-velocity assumption under highly dynamic motion and sensor jitter, while remaining efficient for edge deployment. It balances robustness and real-time computational constraints.

entry.title: CGRL: Concept-Guided Pruning and Representation Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification

author.name: Thuc Huynh, Tuan Le, Doanh C. Bui

entry.summary: CGRL introduces class-level concept prototypes derived from disease prompts into weakly supervised whole-slide image classification, pruning non-informative patches by concept relevance and improving alignment between instances and disease semantics. It targets weak semantic alignment in multiple instance learning pipelines.

entry.title: MAGE: Color-Invariant and Spatial Knowledge Distillation for Gastric Neoplasm Classification

author.name: Jiho Jun, Jeongwon Woo, Jaemin Song, Thanh Bong Nguyen, Dong-heon Yeon, Donghoon Kang, Jae-Myung Park, Sung-Jea Ko, Kwang-Hyun Uhm

entry.summary: MAGE proposes color-invariant and spatial knowledge distillation to classify gastric adenoma versus carcinoma from endoscopy, addressing high inter-class similarity and models' tendency to latch onto domain-specific texture biases like bleeding and lighting. It combines full-image context with spatial focus to reduce spurious correlations.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Spatio-Temporal Candidate Discovery of Dairy Farm Sites from Seasonal Satellite Imagery

author.name: Usman Haider, Fatima Khalid, Karl Mason

entry.summary: This work presents a weakly supervised pipeline for ranking dairy farm candidate clusters from seasonal Sentinel satellite imagery and OpenStreetMap priors, using a Barlow Twins encoder to learn multi-season tile embeddings without farm labels. It frames farm discovery as spatiotemporal candidate ranking under incomplete labels.

entry.title: Medical Image Segmentation based on Deep Active Contour and Mean Curvature Loss Function

author.name: Xiao-qiang Zhai, Zhi-feng Pang, Peng Zheng, Ze-wen Li, Yan-zhe Hou

entry.summary: Proposes a deep active contour segmentation method that adds mean curvature as a geometric constraint in the loss, extending Chan-Vese-style region and length terms to better characterize segmented regions in medical images.

entry.title: Towards Self-Evolving Agents: A Human-Inspired Adaptive Exploration-Exploitation Framework for Genetic Network Programming

author.name: Ali Kohan, Mohamad Roshanzamir, Roohallah Alizadehsani, Seyedali Mirjalili

entry.summary: Introduces a human-development-inspired adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism for Genetic Network Programming, where agents begin with broad experimentation that shifts toward deliberation over time, targeting interpretable graph-based decision structures.

entry.title: A new dual-population constrained multi-objective evolutionary optimization algorithm with repair constraint handling for structural optimization

author.name: Fardad Homafar, Jasmin Jelovica

entry.summary: Introduces a dual-population constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm with a repair-based constraint handling scheme for structural optimization problems with many variables and non-convex feasible regions. Two interacting populations improve global exploration.

entry.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game

author.name: Jens V. R\"uppel, Tim Schreiter, Andrey Rudenko, Achim J. Lilienthal

entry.summary: Studies how a robot game partner's mutual versus referential gaze affects human visual attention during a collaborative word-association game with an LLM-driven NAO robot, using eye-tracking to measure whether humans direct confirmation-seeking gazes toward the robot.

entry.title: Statistical Properties and Power Analysis of Divergence Measures for Credit Risk Model Monitoring

author.name: Abdullah Karasan, Alper Hekimo\u{g}lu

entry.summary: Derives statistical properties and chi-square benchmark values for Jensen-Shannon and Kullback-Leibler divergences as alternatives to the Population Stability Index for detecting distributional shift in credit risk model monitoring, and demonstrates their application on financial data.

entry.title: Your Brain Has an Attack Surface

author.name: IgorPereverzevDev

entry.summary: An independent AI safety researcher describes a setup for studying covert communication between language models, where one model tries to pass a hidden signal past a monitor while both refine their encoding over rounds. The work grew out of Redwood Research and Apart Research hackathons and treats steganographic coordination as a control problem for multi-agent AI systems.

entry.title: PHITSBench: an execution-scored benchmark for AI-assisted PHITS radiation-transport input generation using natural language

author.name: Xianglin Ji, Svetlana V. Boriskina

entry.summary: PHITSBench is an execution-scored benchmark of 282 radiation-transport tasks for the PHITS Monte Carlo code, covering parameter editing, syntax repair, and full simulation generation from natural language. It evaluates several configurations of an existing frontier model, showing strong edit/repair performance but weaker end-to-end generation without domain knowledge.

entry.title: Commenting with Copilot: A Taxonomy and Multi-Year Analysis of Student Code-Generation Specifications

author.name: Nasser Giacaman, Valerio Terragni, Paul Denny, Viraj Kumar

entry.summary: Analyzes a four-year dataset of student code-generation comments used as specifications in AI-assisted programming and introduces a taxonomy across comment type, code expression level, and construct. It examines how specification patterns change across attempts with automated classification.

entry.title: LSTrans: Efficient Knowledge Transfer for Lightweight and Automated ECG Classification

author.name: Yi Zhao, Jiajun Gao, Chenyang Xu, Yuxi Zhou, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight hybrid convolution-Transformer model with low-rank adaptation and knowledge distillation for efficient ECG classification on wearable devices. It captures both rhythmic trends and morphological detail while compressing parameters.

entry.title: Structure-Feature Aligned Graph Learning via Alternating Constrained Optimization

author.name: Chengcheng Yan, Qingsong Wang

entry.summary: This work presents a constrained two-view graph learning framework that aligns structure-conditioned GNN embeddings with a structure-free feature prior from an anchor model, plus a channel-split gated GNN that routes between spectral smoothing and spatial discrimination. It matters for robustness to topology noise and heterophily in graph node prediction.

entry.title: Time-Lag-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling in PPVC Module Factories

author.name: Ziheng Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper adapts a dual-attention deep RL scheduler for flexible job-shop scheduling in prefabricated construction module factories, explicitly handling long post-operation time-lags from curing, ponding, and drying that inflate optimal makespan by around 67 percent. It matters for a realistic industrial scheduling setting that standard methods handle poorly.

entry.title: OmniPMNet: Bridging discrete and gridded PM10 forecasts via omni-query neural processes

author.name: Shuangshuang He, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: OmniPM-Net is a convolutional conditional neural process model that fuses discrete station-level PM10 forecasts with gridded chemical-transport-model outputs into a shared spatial representation using terrain-aware set convolution and multi-scale spatial attention. It matters for producing both accurate station forecasts and continuous fields, especially during dust storms.

entry.title: Scale-Aware Attention for Scarce Neural Data: An RG-Flow Transformer on Sleep-EDF EEG

author.name: Dibakar Sigdel
