entry.summary: This paper introduces an RG-Flow Transformer with a renormalization-group inductive bias (scale-aware attention, learnable anomalous dimension, block-spin coarse-graining, entropy-gated synchronization) and tests whether it beats a parameter-matched vanilla transformer on scarce, real Sleep-EDF EEG. It matters as a physics-inspired inductive bias for scale-free neural signals.

entry.title: OOD-RL-Bench: A Benchmark Framework for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Emil Mittag, Richard Dazeley, Peter Vamplew

entry.summary: OOD-RL-Bench is an extensible benchmark framework for out-of-distribution detection in reinforcement learning, injecting categorized anomalies into observations, transitions, and trajectory dynamics that existing static-classifier OOD benchmarks ignore. It fills a gap for action-dependent temporal structure. It aims to standardize RL safety-monitoring evaluation.

entry.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups

author.name: Martine Dyring Hansen, Marta Ghirardelli, Elena Celledoni, David Martin de Diego, Brynjulf Owren

entry.summary: This work presents an architecture that learns forced multibody mechanical dynamics on Lie groups from position-only data using discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations, preserving geometric invariants and conservation laws. It handles external control inputs and manifold-valued configurations. It targets structure-preserving dynamics learning.

entry.title: Reproducible Reservoir Computing with Thermally Driven Superparamagnets: Controlling Temperature Sensitivity

author.name: Zhengfei Chen, Alex Welbourne, Matthew O. A. Ellis, Dan A. Allwood, Eleni Vasilaki, Thomas J. Hayward

entry.summary: This paper simulates how ambient temperature fluctuations degrade the performance of superparamagnetic nanodot reservoir computing substrates and studies how to control that temperature sensitivity for robust deployment. It quantifies performance loss outside the training temperature range. It advances hardware reservoir-computing reliability.

entry.title: GeoSEAN: Explainable Country-Level Image Geolocation for ASEAN Regions

author.name: Muhamad Syukron, Danish Rafie Ekaputra, Tintrim Dwi Ary Widhianingsih

entry.summary: GeoSEAN presents an explainable country-level image geolocation pipeline for 11 ASEAN countries using a collected dataset of about 4,850 images and comparing CLIP zero-shot, LightGBM, and other approaches. It emphasizes interpreting how visual evidence contributes to location predictions in visually similar regions.

entry.title: A Dynamic Scene Interaction Reasoning Framework for Scene-level Lane-Change Intention and Trajectory Prediction of Multiple Interacting Vehicles

author.name: Joshua Kofi Asamoah, Blessing Agyei Kyem, Eugene Denteh, Armstrong Aboah

entry.summary: This work proposes a dynamic scene-graph attention framework that jointly predicts lane-change intention and future trajectories for every relevant vehicle in a local traffic scene, modeling the scene as a time-varying interaction graph. It moves beyond single-target prediction toward explicit maneuver-level scene forecasting.

entry.title: Scaffolding the Strategist: Architecture-Dependent Reasoning Interventions in Hotelling Spatial Markets

author.name: Pratyush Singh

entry.summary: Using Hotelling's spatial-competition model as a diagnostic, the study tests whether structured reasoning interventions improve strategic economic reasoning and finds effects depend on model architecture. It reports a statistically significant crossover between scaffolding type and model type across an existing instruction model and a reasoning-optimized model.

entry.title: How Much Does Correctness Cost? Budgeted Placement of Strong Correctors in a Weak Multi-Agent Swarm

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: This paper studies how to cheaply steer an unreliable multi-agent swarm to correct consensus using a few strong oracle correctors, modeling consensus on a graph and measuring quality via a coherence trace metric. It proves submodularity so greedy placement achieves near-optimal results and derives a budget-correctness frontier.

entry.title: A Symbolic Neural CPU for Quantization-Simulated Writeback and Interpretable Program Execution

author.name: Jose Luis Lima de Jesus Silva

entry.summary: The paper introduces a trace-supervised symbolic neural CPU that combines recurrent control, an operation router over a differentiable ALU bank, and destination-masked register writeback to make every state transition interpretable during learned program execution. It exposes selected operations, registers, and writeback semantics at each step with quantization-simulated replay.

entry.title: UNIT: Unleash Large Language Models Potential for Graph Continual Learning

author.name: Tairan Huang, Yili Wang, Beibei Hu, Yiting Shi, Qiutong Li, Changlong He, Jianliang Gao

entry.summary: UNIT is a framework that fine-tunes LLMs for graph continual learning, addressing semantic-structural separation and imbalanced knowledge transfer in streaming graph data. It aims to combine topological modeling with deep semantics while transferring early-task knowledge to new tasks.

entry.title: STEC: Evidence Compression for Deep Search in Open-domain Multi-Hop QA

author.name: Xinkang Li, Rong Jiang, Xin Song, Ye Wang, Yue Han, Changjian Li

entry.summary: STEC introduces evidence compression for deep-search open-domain multi-hop QA, addressing the final-answer selection problem when multiple search trajectories support different candidates with heterogeneous, redundant, or conflicting evidence. It compresses trajectory evidence so a verifier can compare candidates on aligned support rather than noisy raw traces or bare answer strings.

entry.title: Toward Contemplative LLM: A Modular Framework for Evaluating and Enhancing LLM Alignment in Mental Health

author.name: Asher Sprigler, Yang-Yang Feng, Iftach Amir, Jonathan E. Bogard, Todd S Braver, Yi Ding, David Kinney, Yixue Zhao

entry.summary: This paper presents a modular, extensible evaluation framework, initially for mental health, to systematically assess whether contemplative principles like mindfulness and compassion enhance LLM alignment across evolving models and benchmarks. It aims to replace ad hoc, non-generalizing evaluation of contemplative alignment approaches.

entry.title: LOGOS: A Living Logic for AI Agent Teams That Evolve With Humans

author.name: Yuma Ichikawa, Yamato Arai, Kosaku Kimura, Akira Sakai, Hiromichi Kobashi

entry.summary: LOGOS is a pluggable self-evolution and governance layer for multi-agent frameworks that compiles heterogeneous multimodal inputs into versioned agent packs containing agents, tools, knowledge, tests, permissions, and policies. It emphasizes controlling what agents are allowed to become through auditable, portable governance of agent activity.

entry.title: Prompting-MammAlps: Fine-Grained Text-to-Video Retrieval for Camera-Trap Data

author.name: Valentin Gabeff, Baptiste Maquignaz, Jennifer Shan, Sepideh Mamooler, Gencer Sumbul, Blair Costelloe, Devis Tuia, Alexander Mathis

entry.summary: Presents Prompting-MammAlps, the first text-to-video retrieval benchmark for camera-trap ecological data, plus a method that converts spatiotemporal action localization into structured text queried by an LLM. It targets fine-grained, interpretable retrieval of wildlife events.

entry.title: An LLM-powered Agentic Recommendation System for Connected TV Content Discovery

author.name: Lei Shi, Di Wang, Harry Tran, Helsing Xu, Yuchen Lu, Dhara Ghodasara, Wilson Chaney, Xueting Liao, Jerry Yu, Huayu Ding, Mingze Gao, Shike Mei, Shuo Tang, Zhe Zhang, Jianming He, Abhishek Kumar, Haotian Wu, Hamed Firooz, Li Li

entry.summary: Describes an LLM-powered agentic recommendation system for Connected TV content discovery that ingests unstructured contextual signals (trending topics, breaking news, cultural events) via reasoning rather than hand-engineered feature pipelines. It integrates these signals into ranking without bespoke heuristics.

entry.title: Quantum Circuit Vision: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Visual AI Agents for Quantum Code Generation

author.name: Dongping Liu, Aoyu Zhang, Luyao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Quantum Circuit Vision, a cost-aware benchmark of 132 circuits testing whether multimodal AI agents can read quantum circuit diagrams and generate verified executable Braket code with unitary-fidelity checks. It finds a mid-tier Claude model offers the best cost-accuracy balance versus the strongest model.

entry.title: Breaking the Quality--Intelligibility Trade-off in Streaming Target Speaker Extraction via Deep-Feature-Anchored Preference Optimization

author.name: Shuhai Peng, Jinjiang Liu, Hui Lu, Liyang Chen, Guiping Zhong, Jiakui Li, Shiyin Kang, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: Tackles the quality-versus-intelligibility trade-off in streaming target speaker extraction, arguing it stems from an inappropriate optimization anchor causing reward hacking that erases pronunciation-critical content. It proposes an enlarged Conformer convolution kernel and WavLM-anchored preference optimization to break the trade-off.

entry.title: Motif: Discovering and Automating Personal Web Workflows

author.name: Shaokang Jiang, Daye Nam

entry.summary: Presents Motif, a system that passively observes everyday browser activity to discover recurring programmable interaction patterns, recommends automations, and generates installable programs users can review and refine in natural language. It removes the assumption that users already know what to automate.

entry.title: Tool-Adaptive LLM Reranker

author.name: Zichuan Liu, Ruijin Hua

entry.summary: Proposes TALRanker, a tool-adaptive LLM reranker that formalizes pointwise relevance scoring as an agentic Markov decision process, learning when to selectively invoke external search tools during reranking to avoid the latency of indiscriminate tool calls. A two-stage training paradigm with a language-preserving hybrid loss prevents catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Lightning Fast Matching Dependency Discovery with Desbordante

author.name: Alexey Shlyonskikh, Michael Sinelnikov, Daniil Nikolaev, Yurii Litvinov, George Chernishev

entry.summary: Describes optimization techniques for HyMD, a state-of-the-art matching dependency discovery algorithm, delivering large speedups for a computationally intensive data-quality task. Contributions span technical and algorithmic improvements integrated in the Desbordante tool.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Token-Efficient and Semantic-Preserving Opinion Summarization

author.name: Fabrizio Marozzo, Stefano Iannicelli

entry.summary: Presents a framework for token-efficient opinion summarization that combines multidimensional classification with stratified sampling to select compact yet representative opinion subsets before prompting an LLM. It aims to preserve viewpoint diversity while minimizing token usage.

entry.title: Same Stories, Different Journeys: From Social Comparison to Sensemaking in AI-Mediated Peer Career Exploration

author.name: Pengping Tan, Baoquan Zhao, Zhenhui Peng

entry.summary: Presents an interactive system that turns real social-media career posts into persona-grounded conversational agents, shifting job-seekers from passive scrolling to dialogue-driven sensemaking. It aims to preserve authentic peer content while reducing detrimental upward social comparison and cognitive overload.

entry.title: Enhancing LLMs through human feedback: a journey towards self-improvement

author.name: Tatiana Pelc, Gila Kamhi, Asaf Avrahamy, Adi Fledel-Alon

entry.summary: Introduces a methodology for refining a primary retrieval-augmented generation system using an auxiliary feedback RAG that continuously collects, classifies, and integrates human feedback into the inference workflow for iterative self-improvement. It targets accuracy and relevance in information retrieval.

entry.title: Transformer-Guided Swarm Intelligence for Frugal Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Romain Amigon

entry.summary: This paper proposes a frugal, memetic neural architecture search combining an autoregressive Transformer controller trained with RL for global search and an artificial bee colony algorithm for local exploitation, with a dynamic entropy mechanism to avoid premature convergence on consumer GPUs. It matters for democratizing NAS on modest hardware.

entry.title: Evaluating Reliability in Machine Learning Models for Early Chronic Kidney Disease Prediction: A Systematic Review of Data Leakage and Predictor Stability

author.name: Mashrul Hossain, Nafesa Kibria, Fahim Shahriar

entry.summary: This systematic review of nineteen studies on machine-learning-based early chronic kidney disease prediction assesses methodological reliability, focusing on data leakage, temporal record limitations, and inconsistency in reported clinical indicators. It matters for exposing reproducibility and validity problems in clinical prediction research.

entry.title: Beyond Coordinate Gauge: An Audited Protocol for Detecting Donor-Specific Functional Fingerprints after Neural Collapse

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh, Phan Thanh Duc

entry.summary: This paper introduces an audited protocol using verified affine-correct alignment to test whether donor-specific functional fingerprints of independently trained networks remain distinguishable after Neural Collapse converges networks toward shared low-dimensional geometry, addressing the detectability claim. It matters for understanding whether trajectory-specific variation survives convergence.

entry.title: The Geometry of Memorization: Finite-Time Spectral Sensitivity as a Diagnostic for Flow Matching Models

author.name: Shuchan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Finite-Time Spectral Sensitivity, a gradient-free forward-pass metric tracking singular values of the state-transition matrix to expose the geometry of flow-matching generative trajectories and detect a spectral-collapse pathology under data scarcity. It links overfitting to measurable geometric change. It offers a diagnostic for memorization in flow models.

entry.title: TAKE: Trajectory-Aware Knowledge Estimation for Text Dataset Distillation

author.name: Tri-Nhan Vo, Dang Nguyen, Sunil Gupta

entry.summary: TAKE is a text dataset distillation framework that uses influence functions convolved along the training trajectory into per-sample knowledge scores, reducing corpora to as little as 0.1 percent of size while preserving downstream fidelity. It targets the growing cost of training and continual learning on large text corpora. Trajectory-aware influence estimation is the core idea.

entry.title: Contrastive Joint-Embedding Prediction for Representation Learning in Structural MRI

author.name: Fabian Mager, Lars Kai Hansen

entry.summary: COJEPA is a self-supervised framework for volumetric brain MRI combining a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a contrastive loss to capture both local predictivity and global discriminability, extending I-JEPA to 3D with foreground-aware masking and world-space positional encodings. It trains without labels on over 2000 scans and evaluates across multiple downstream tasks. It targets label-scarce medical imaging.

entry.title: Learning the Graphical Nature of Symmetries

author.name: Rashid Barket, Enrico Grimaldi, Yacoub Hendi, Edward Hirst, Adam Onus, Harmeet Singh

entry.summary: This work constructs a dataset of 131,406 Cayley graphs covering nearly all groups up to order 767 with exact algebraic labels and rich graph, cycle, distance, and spectral statistics to study how finite-group properties are reflected in graph observables. It contributes new enumerative sequences and benchmarks for machine learning on algebraic structure. It bridges group theory and geometric data.

entry.title: Label-Decoupled Style Augmentation for Domain Generalization in Multi-Label Remote Sensing Scene Classification

author.name: Alaa Almouradi, Erchan Aptoula

entry.summary: The paper proposes label-decoupled style augmentation for domain generalization in multi-label remote sensing scene classification, confining style perturbation to label-specific regions so one class does not contaminate another's augmentation. It uses per-label attention to localize perturbations. It fills a gap where multi-label remote-sensing domain generalization was understudied.

entry.title: Evaluating Health Misinformation in Low-Resource Languages: Integrating Small Language Models with a Culturally-Sensitive Responsible NLP Framework (Bangla as a Case Study)

author.name: Farnaz Farid, Raihan Alam, Al Al-Areqi, Farhad Ahamed, Muhammad Hassan Khan, Sadia Hossain, Irena Veljanova, Anika Tabassum Binte Hossain

entry.summary: This research integrates small language models with a culturally-sensitive responsible-NLP framework to detect health misinformation in low-resource languages, using Bangla as a case study. It addresses data scarcity and cultural nuance that cause current tools to underperform for culturally and linguistically diverse communities. It targets equitable trustworthy health information access.

entry.title: Translation as a Computationally Efficient Bridge: Feasibility of English BERT for Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Hielke Muizelaar, Giulia Rivetti, Marco Spruit, Marcel Haas

entry.summary: This study compares translation-based fine-tuning (translating non-English data to English and fine-tuning English BERT) against native-language BERT across six NLP tasks and multiple languages. It assesses whether translation offers a computationally efficient bridge for low-resource languages. It provides a structured feasibility comparison rather than a new model.

entry.title: NEEDL-Bench: Dataset for Swiss Needle Cast and Stomata Detection in Microscopy Images

author.name: Benjamin Blake, Declan McIntosh, J\"urgen Ehlting, Nicolas Feau, Joey B. Tanney, Alexandra Branzan Albu

entry.summary: NEEDL-Bench introduces a microscopy detection benchmark for Swiss Needle Cast disease in Douglas-fir trees, annotating pseudothecia and stomata across 3250 images from over a thousand needles. It fills the absence of a computer vision dataset for scaling severity measurement of this fungal disease.

entry.title: Lesion Segmentation in Moderate to Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: An nnU-Net Based Approach with Adaptive Normalization in the AIMS-TBI 2025 Challenge

author.name: Inhwa Son, Gaeun Lee, Sohyeon Sim, Kwang-Hyun Uhm

entry.summary: This paper describes an nnU-Net-based lesion segmentation solution with adaptive intensity normalization confined to brain parenchyma for the AIMS-TBI 2025 challenge, targeting heterogeneous traumatic brain injury lesions in T1-weighted MRI. It reports competitive performance on the held-out test set.

entry.title: From ML Predictions to Informed Diagnostic Assistance Using the Toulmin Model of Argumentation

author.name: Anca Marginean, Adrian Groza

entry.summary: The paper decomposes image-based medical diagnosis into components of the Toulmin argumentation model, using a biomarker-extraction model for grounds and a MedGemma agent for the warrant linking evidence to a claim. It aims to make ML retinal diagnoses more interpretable and auditable than raw predictions or standard explainable-AI methods.

entry.title: YUKTI: From Natural-Language Situations to Robust, Verifiable Decisions An Uncertainty-Typed Proposition IR, Assumption-Robust Pareto Frontiers, and a Regret Certificate

author.name: Suyash Mishra

entry.summary: YUKTI reframes natural-language-to-optimization pipelines by representing problems as typed-proposition graphs carrying coefficient uncertainty and provenance rather than committing to single objectives and point values. It routes stages to exact, nonlinear, or evolutionary solvers and produces assumption-robust Pareto frontiers with a regret certificate.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Control with Rule-Aligned Small Language Models and Multi-Agent Self-Correction

author.name: Yuchen Wang, Javal Vyas, Tong Liu, Mehmet Mercangoz

entry.summary: The work retrains a compact small language model for industrial control reasoning and embeds it in a validator-guided multi-agent self-correction loop that checks candidate actions against a plant-aware digital twin before execution. It targets low-latency, edge-deployable closed-loop control from natural-language specifications.

entry.title: BatteryLake: Agentic, Physics-Grounded Curation of Heterogeneous Battery Aging Data and Benchmarking

author.name: Tianwen Zhu, Hao Wang, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: BatteryLake is a governed data lakehouse that turns messy public battery-aging datasets into benchmark-ready assets via an agentic, physics-grounded curation framework where LLM agents extract metadata, synthesize converters, and ground outputs in verbatim evidence while abstaining when none exists. It addresses reproducibility and schema inconsistency in battery health research.

entry.title: Dynamic Agent Skills: A Lifecycle Survey and Taxonomy of Evolving Skill Libraries

author.name: Yubo Li

entry.summary: This taxonomy-driven survey audits 124 papers to characterize how LLM agent skill libraries (code functions, instructions, workflow graphs, adapters) evolve over time as lifecycle-managed, verified, evolving artifact stores. It synthesizes stages from evidence collection and skill proposal through verification, retrieval, repair, and governed sharing.

entry.title: Verifier-Based Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Reasoning Models for Thermal Energy Storage Control

author.name: Takumi Shioda, Kohei Terashima, Tatsuo Nagai

entry.summary: This paper adapts an open-weight reasoning model via reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable rewards for thermal energy storage control, converting exact offline dynamic-programming action values into dense rewards and training with only 30 prompts to output hourly heat-pump setpoints. It aims to scale scheduling across buildings where MPC and standard RL do not. It applies RLVR to building energy control.

entry.title: Do You Remember? Toward Memory-Centric Multimodal AI

author.name: Xuguang Yu, Weigang Zheng, Minyue Yu

entry.summary: DoYouRemember introduces reconstructive memory into multimodal LLMs via a VQ-VAE encoder, a LoRA-fine-tuned LLM jointly attending to visual and text tokens, and a diffusion decoder reconstructing images from hidden states, finding that LLM hidden states contain near-zero recoverable visual information. This negative result challenges assumptions about multimodal internal representations. It probes whether MLLMs truly retain visual detail.

entry.title: Your Brain Has an Attack Surface part 2

author.name: IgorPereverzevDev

entry.summary: The second post in a series analyzing a covert communication channel in latent space, distinguishing relocation, where a monitor is evaded by moving separable signal clouds that can be recovered by retraining, from collapse, where classes merge irreversibly and their distinguishing information is destroyed. Extends earlier single-network results.

entry.title: GES-TSP: Graph Edge Sparsification for TSP

author.name: Tianfeng Chen, Xianyue Li

entry.summary: GES proposes a learning-based graph edge sparsification method for Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problems that adaptively generates instance-specific sparse graphs using geometric structure. It aims to accelerate exact solving by reducing graph size beyond fixed heuristics.

entry.title: Verification of Adaptive Agentic Controllers through Finite Rule Revision

author.name: Roberto Garrone

entry.summary: The paper formulates a bounded verification protocol for adaptive agentic controllers represented as finite symbolic rules with diagnostic predicates, explanation logs, and held-out re-evaluation. It characterizes which controller failure classes can be detected and localized under non-determinism and weak observability.

entry.title: KGCQual: An Interpretable Framework for Evaluating the Knowledge Graph Construction Quality from Text

author.name: Nipun Misra, Vikranth Udandarao, Aanchal Gupta, Yogender Kumar, Manuj Mukherjee, Raghava Mutharaju

entry.summary: KGCQual proposes an interpretable intrinsic metric for knowledge-graph construction quality that measures how closely an extracted graph approximates an ideal graph capturing key noun phrases, predicate relations, and linguistic phenomena like negation. It combines complementary components to assess structural and semantic fidelity beyond task-specific metrics.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Hierarchical Search for Regulation-Driven Fine-Grained Classification

author.name: Siyu Wang, Wei Tan, Lulu Chen

entry.summary: The paper tackles regulation-driven fine-grained classification (e.g., customs tariffs, export controls) where correct labels depend on rule-defined boundaries, thresholds, and exclusions rather than semantic similarity. It proposes constraint-aware hierarchical search to jointly enforce the regulatory hierarchy and rule conditions, unlike flat classifiers or retrieval-augmented LLMs.

entry.title: Personalized Emotional Intelligence in Generative AI through Symbolic Affective Reasoning

author.name: Qing Lin, Mengmi Zhang

entry.summary: EROS is a hybrid framework integrating symbolic reasoning with deep learning to enable personalized emotion augmentation through visual content, discovering generalizable affective rules from large image-emotion datasets. It aims to move beyond generating realistic content toward understanding, predicting, and personalizing human emotional responses.

entry.title: First-Order Modal Logic in HOL: Deep and Shallow Embeddings with Automated Faithfulness (Extended Preprint)

author.name: Christoph Benzm\"uller, Daniel Kirchner

entry.summary: This extended preprint provides three side-by-side embeddings (deep, heavyweight maximal-shallow, and lightweight minimal-shallow) of first-order modal logic with constant-domain Kripke semantics into classical higher-order logic in Isabelle/HOL. The minimal-shallow embedding uses a locale form admitting a global faithfulness theorem recovering exactly deep validity.

entry.title: What You Train Is What You Get: Gender Bias, Training Composition, and Post-Hoc Mitigation in Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Aishwarya R. Fursule, Vamshi Nallaguntla, Shruti Kshirsagar, Anderson R. Avila

entry.summary: Investigates gender bias in audio deepfake detection using controlled ASVspoof5 splits, training attack-specific models across nine gender compositions and evaluating post-hoc threshold calibration methods. It finds training data composition strongly predicts bias direction.

entry.title: Efficiently Adapting Spoken Language Models for the Singaporean Context

author.name: Ng Jia Sheng Jason

entry.summary: Adapts an open-source spoken language model to Singapore's four official languages across five speech tasks under conditions where original training data is inaccessible, using LoRA, a surrogate text-QA anti-forgetting dataset, and a speech-adapted multi-task reweighting scheme. The resulting 5B HT-Moonstone matches or beats models up to 7x larger.

entry.title: SALT-GNN: Handling Dense Neighborhoods in Anti-Money Laundering Graphs via Statistics-Aware Attention

author.name: Lidia Losavio, Francesco Sovrano, Dario Fenoglio, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: Introduces SALT-GNN, a statistics-aware attention graph neural network for anti-money laundering that handles dense recipient neighborhoods, and proposes recipient-degree stratified evaluation revealing performance degradation hidden by aggregate F1. It shows suspicious signals are harder to isolate for high-activity accounts.

entry.title: FlowPainter: Inpainting Optical Flow via Confidence-Guided Completion

author.name: Yuang Meng, Chenyang Wu, Xianshun Liu, Chun-Le Guo, Zichen Liang, Lina Lei, Jie Liang, Hui Zeng, Chongyi Li, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FlowPainter, a diffusion-based optical flow framework that treats flow estimation as confidence-guided inpainting, denoising only uncertain regions while a lightweight network handles reliable motion. This reduces denoising burden and improves handling of large displacements versus denoising the full field from noise.

entry.title: EmoStyle: Affective Conditioning of Style-Specialist Experts for Emotional Image Generation

author.name: Dexiang Hong, Yijie Guo, Weidong Chen, Xinyan Liu, Zixuan Zou, Zhendong Mao, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes EmoStyle, a framework for emotion-aware artistic image generation that converts prompts into fine-grained visual and affective conditions (color, lighting, brushwork, composition) to bridge the gap between test prompts and needed control signals. It uses affective conditioning of style-specialist experts.

entry.title: Mitigating LLM Sycophancy in Code Smell Detection Using Evidence-Guided Reasoning Prompts

author.name: Istiaq Ahmed Fahad, Kamruzzaman Asif, Md. Nurul Ahad Tawhid

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of sycophancy bias in LLM-based code smell detection using the MLCQ dataset, showing how confirmation bias, contradictory hints, and false premises shift predictions, and proposes evidence-guided reasoning prompts to mitigate it. It quantifies how external cues override objective code analysis.

entry.title: Learning the Brain's Dynamics as a Port-Hamiltonian System

author.name: Dibakar Sigdel

entry.summary: Models human motor cortex during a wrist-extension BCI task as a port-Hamiltonian system combining conservative gyroscopic coupling with a dissipative port driven by a GNN surrogate, integrated with a fluctuation-dissipation-consistent noise channel. Trained on real EEG, it reproduces scale-free criticality signatures and generates closed-loop neuromodulation signals.

entry.title: Abstractiveness Metrics for Evaluating Text Summarization: A Refined Formulation with Empirical Validation

author.name: Praveenkumar Katwe, Rakesh Chandra Balabantaray, Kali Prasad Vittala

entry.summary: Proposes refined heuristic metrics for measuring how abstractive versus extractive a generated summary is, using harmonic mean of document lengths modulated by a non-overlap factor. It validates the metrics on XSUM across several summarization models.

entry.title: Programming Language Policy as an AI Literacy Equity Problem: A 15-Nation Comparative Analysis

author.name: Adrian-Marius Dumitran, Iulia-Maria Popescu

entry.summary: Compares secondary computer-science curricula and examination frameworks across fifteen countries, arguing that reliance on general-track subjects for universal AI literacy while specialist informatics serves STEM pathways creates structural inequity. It identifies students who finish secondary education without any formal programming exposure.

entry.title: IG-GAN: A Generative Adversarial Network for Aerodynamic Data Generation Based on Intrinsic Geometry

author.name: Ying Yan, Liwei Hu, Xiaoming Zhang

entry.summary: IG-GAN is a generative adversarial network for aerodynamic data that represents shapes as piecewise-smooth Bezier-surface manifolds and uses a radial-basis-function discriminator, aiming to respect the manifold structure of physical data. It matters mainly to aerodynamic surrogate design rather than to general ML.

entry.title: LoRA-Based Cascaded Multimodal Fusion for Action Recognition in Medical Training Environments

author.name: Divya Mereddy, Jeevan Beedareddy

entry.summary: This work presents a cascaded LoRA-based multimodal fusion framework that integrates modalities in stages using parameter-efficient adapters, fusing closely related modalities first and adding heterogeneous ones without retraining, evaluated on nursing action-recognition datasets. It matters for scalable multimodal adaptation in medical training environments.

entry.title: Mitigating The Effect of Class Imbalance in Data with Hierarchical and Dependable Structure

author.name: Bipin Chhetri, Deepika Giri, Avishek Kadel, Rabin Kumar Karki, Akbar Siami Namin

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchy-aware RoBERTa framework with learnable parent-class embeddings for CWE vulnerability text classification, examining whether oversampling techniques like SMOTE and ADASYN help under extreme class imbalance and strong hierarchical dependencies. It matters for reliable cybersecurity weakness categorization.

entry.title: Quantum Port-Hamiltonian Neural Networks: Learning Conservative and Dissipative Dynamics via Measurement-Induced Nonlinearity

author.name: Dibakar Sigdel

entry.summary: Q-pHNNs are parameterized quantum circuits that learn conservative and dissipative classical dynamics by mapping port-Hamiltonian structure onto unitary evolution plus measurement-induced nonlinearity. Conservation and passivity are enforced by construction rather than penalty terms. It is a niche intersection of quantum computing and structure-preserving neural dynamics.

entry.title: ReDiTT: Retrieval Augmented Conditional Diffusion Transformers for Asynchronous Time Series

author.name: Saiyue Lyu, Zhitian Zhang, Ruizhi Deng, Thibaut Durand

entry.summary: ReDiTT is a retrieval-augmented conditional diffusion transformer for asynchronous time series that retrieves structurally similar latent sequences as cross-attention conditions to stabilize long-horizon event forecasting. It predicts next inter-event time and type. It targets temporal point-process style prediction with generative diversity.

entry.title: From Preimage Search To Source-Grounded Feature Inversion

author.name: Kaixiang Shu

entry.summary: This paper formulates source-grounded feature inversion, conditioning a network feature's inverse on the local network geometry at the input that generated it rather than matching any input that reproduces the feature. It addresses the ill-posedness of standard feature inversion. It contributes to interpretability of internal representations.

entry.title: Contrastive-Collapsed Loss for Flexible and Geometrically Optimal Embeddings and Faster Convergence

author.name: Blanca Cano-Camarero, \'Angela Fern\'andez-Pascual, Jos\'e R. Dorronsoro

entry.summary: CoCo is a loss function encouraging intra-class collapse and inter-class angular separation while retaining flexibility to approximate geometrically optimal embeddings, with theoretical positioning relative to dot regression and cross-entropy showing better initialization and gradient informativeness. It is validated on tabular OpenML benchmarks. It targets well-structured representation learning.

entry.title: AAAI-26 Dual Submissions: Novel Challenges

author.name: Kiri L. Wagstaff, Joydeep Biswas, Erich Merrill III, Bo An, Ida Camacho, David J. Crandall, Matthew E. Taylor

entry.summary: This report from AAAI-26 organizers documents dual submissions, where near-identical papers are simultaneously submitted to multiple archival venues without disclosure, and describes their detection pipeline combining title-abstract similarity with an LLM-based overlap assessment across nine venues. It addresses a growing peer-review integrity problem. It is a meta-scientific and community-governance contribution.

entry.title: MAGE: Understanding Stability-Performance Trade-offs in Multi-component Prompt Optimization

author.name: Prateek Singh

entry.summary: MAGE is a controlled analysis framework integrating episodic memory, multi-objective Pareto selection, and adaptive evaluation to study how components of iterative prompt optimization interact, uncovering a Prompt Optimization Coupling Effect where combined stochastic signals simultaneously improve performance and amplify variance. It is positioned as an ablation platform rather than a superior optimizer. It offers insight into prompt-optimization dynamics.

entry.title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI

author.name: Induk Um, Youngung Han, Kyeonghun Kim, Yului Jeong, Jina Jeong, Hyunsu Go, Dohyun Kweon, Sungha Park, Junga Kim, Anna Jung, Suah Park, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Pa Hong, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: SpikeDS is a spiking-neural-network Spikformer for perineural invasion prediction from 3D MRI in cholangiocarcinoma that jointly exploits activation sparsity from binary spikes and spatial sparsity via firing-rate-based window pruning, reducing the prohibitive cost of volumetric analysis. Dual Sparsity Spiking Attention is the core module. It targets efficient clinical volumetric prediction.

entry.title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis

author.name: Dandan Chen, Yan Zhao, Xuepeng Chen

entry.summary: This study builds a physically constrained robustness evaluation for deep-learning PV power forecasting under realistic, correlated numerical-weather-prediction errors, using virtual PV power to isolate input-uncertainty propagation. It compares six representative models. It aims for predictable behavior under uncertain inputs rather than only nominal accuracy.

entry.title: Optimization Is Not All You Need

author.name: Minh Hua, Rita Raley

entry.summary: This humanities-oriented essay reinterprets LLM alignment and fluency improvements as an expression of optimization culture, tracing the belief that measurable improvement along predefined axes exhausts the question of value through pretraining, decoding, preference tuning, benchmarking, and interfaces. It argues optimization can measure improbability but not whether unlikelihood is error or meaning. It offers a critical cultural genealogy of NLP practice.

entry.title: A Calibrated Multimodal Ensemble for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition: System Description and Private-Test Submission Strategy

author.name: Josep Cabacas-Maso, Ismael Benito-Altamirano, Carles Ventura

entry.summary: This system description reports a calibrated equal-weight ensemble over frozen face, audio, text, and pose embeddings for ambivalence and hesitancy recognition in the ABAW challenge, reaching about 0.74 macro-F1 on the public test set. It documents a five-submission private-test strategy on a disjoint participant set.

entry.title: Overview of Cross-Component In-loop Filters in Video Coding Standards

author.name: Zhaoyu Li, Xuewei Meng, Jiaqi Zhang, Cheng Huang, Chuanmin Jia, Siwei Ma, Yun Jiang

entry.summary: This paper surveys cross-component in-loop filters in state-of-the-art video coding standards, covering the Cross-Component Adaptive Loop Filter and Cross-Component Sample Adaptive Offset that exploit luma-chroma correlations. It summarizes how these filters reduce compression artifacts and improve chroma fidelity.

entry.title: HSEmotion Team at the 11th ABAW Challenge: Multi-Task Learning and Ambivalence/Hesitancy Video Recognition

author.name: Aleksei Bakin, Andrey V. Savchenko

entry.summary: This system report describes the HSEmotion team's ABAW challenge entry using frozen lightweight facial extractors with separate heads and extensive post-processing for multi-task affect prediction and ambivalence/hesitancy video recognition. It reports ensembles exceeding baseline performance on validation sets.

entry.title: Practical Judgment, Virtue, and Intuition in the Use of Opaque AI-Enabled Systems

author.name: Nathan G. Wood, Andrew P. Rebera

entry.summary: A philosophy paper arguing that concerns about opaque, autonomous AI-enabled systems, such as reliability, control, and ethical or legal compliance, can be mitigated by leveraging practical judgment, virtue, and intuition in how such black-box systems are used.

entry.title: Making Credible Deals With AI

author.name: Ram Potham

entry.summary: This post proposes concrete mechanisms for making credible commitments to a scheming, weakly superhuman AI so that trading favorable behavior for things it values could reduce takeover risk. It confronts the core credibility problem that a lab controls the AI's training data, tool outputs, and context, making promises hard to trust.

entry.title: SupplyNetPy: An Open-Source Python Library for High-Fidelity Modeling and Simulation of Arbitrary Supply Chain and Inventory Networks

author.name: Tushar Lone, Neha Karanjkar

entry.summary: SupplyNetPy is an open-source Python library for discrete-event simulation of arbitrary multi-echelon supply-chain networks, supporting perishable inventory, disruptions, and stochastic demand and lead times. It is validated against analytical benchmarks, a commercial tool, and a published case study.

entry.title: Task-Conditioned Synthetic Data Generation for Improving Machine Learning Performance in Agricultural Prediction Tasks

author.name: Hamid Ebrahimy, Moritz Lucas, Martin Atzmueller

entry.summary: The paper proposes a task-conditioned synthetic data generation method pairing a Bayesian network generator with a transformer-based tabular foundation model to improve ML performance on agricultural prediction tasks with limited reference data. It combines teacher-student transfer with in-context tabular learning.

entry.title: Exploring Agentic Workflows for Generating High Quality Math Visual Aids

author.name: Rizwaan Malik, Ashna Khetan, Isabel Sieh, Samin Khan

entry.summary: The paper introduces an agentic workflow where LLM agents evaluate and iteratively refine generated K-12 math diagrams through a self-improvement feedback loop. It targets the reliability gap in producing accurate, pedagogically sound visual aids from descriptions.

entry.title: AI YOU Town: Make Friends and Money with Your Digital Twin

author.name: Yan Lin, Yuyang Dai, Jiahui Geng, Yuxia Wang

entry.summary: AI YOU continually updates a 22-dimension personality profile from conversation and embodies it in a personal digital twin, combining prompting, Bayesian updating, and conformal prediction with a layered memory to preserve persona consistency over long interactions. It reports calibrated conformal coverage and improved uncertainty handling for persona inference.

entry.title: MRUF: Multi-granularity Routing with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Haoran Ma, Yinfeng Yu, Liejun Wang

entry.summary: MRUF is a reliability-aware multimodal sentiment-analysis fusion method that combines multi-granularity routing with uncertainty calibration, supervising modality routing via leave-one-out error increases and refining gates through inverse-variance reweighting. It counters conventional fusion over-trusting unreliable modalities under noise or occlusion.

entry.title: WattCouncil: Context-Aware Household Energy Scenario Generation With Governed LLMs

author.name: Mohannad Takrouri, Nicolas M. Cuadrado A., Martin Tak\'a\v{c}

entry.summary: WattCouncil is a data-generation framework where a council of role-specialized LLM agents generate, audit, and validate structured household energy scenarios under explicit constraints, addressing scarcity of high-resolution demand data due to privacy and regulatory barriers. It targets smart-grid ML research needs.

entry.title: SMETA-ZSL:Semantic Meta-Alignment for Zero-Shot Threat Classification

author.name: Ivan Alejandro Montoya Sanchez, Anantaa Kotal, Aritran Piplai

entry.summary: Proposes SMETA-ZSL, a semantic meta-alignment approach for generalized zero-shot threat classification in cybersecurity, using LLMs to convert unstructured threat-intelligence reports into semantic prototypes for unseen threat categories. It targets challenges like semantic overlap, class imbalance, and open-set conditions.

entry.title: Workload-Driven Optimization for On-Device Real-Time Subtitle Translation

author.name: Tsz-To Wong

entry.summary: Studies on-device English-to-Traditional-Chinese subtitle translation under short-input, low-latency, batch-size-one, privacy constraints, finding vocabulary projection becomes a dominant decode cost after quantization. It replaces a 151k vocabulary with a 64k domain tokenizer and adapts via embedding calibration and fine-tuning.

entry.title: PhenoEmbed: Self-Supervised Multispectral UAV Time-Series Embeddings for Individual Tree Crown Phenology

author.name: Taimur Khan

entry.summary: Develops PhenoEmbed, a self-supervised crown-centric temporal embedding model trained with contrastive and masked reconstruction objectives on an 18-date UAV multispectral time series for forest crown phenology. It treats seasonal crown dynamics as phenological appearance change and anchors crops on segmented crown polygons.

entry.title: GRC-ProbNet: Uncertainty-aware Feature Extraction for Cardiovascular Disease Classification

author.name: Yash Shah, Omar Todd, Philipp Seeb\"ock, Georg Langs, Ben Glocker, Raghav Mehta

entry.summary: Proposes GRC-ProbNet, extending a hybrid radiomic/geometric CVD classification pipeline by replacing deterministic segmentation with a deep ensemble producing multiple masks and extracting uncertainty features from them. It analyzes these uncertainty features for correlation with and contribution to cardiovascular disease classification from CT.

entry.title: The evolution of AI from image interpretation toward scientific inference in nanoparticle electron microscopy

author.name: Evropi Toulkeridou, Jiafei Li, Leonardo Lari, Panagiotis Grammatikopoulos

entry.summary: Reviews how AI in nanoparticle electron microscopy is evolving from descriptive image interpretation toward quantitative structural interpretation, dynamic analysis, and scientific inference across TEM, HRTEM, STEM, and in situ TEM. It organizes methods around principal nanoparticle-characterization challenges.

entry.title: A Stepwise Questioning Expert-Editor Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Document Summarization

author.name: Lingyun Shen, Xuejia Guo

entry.summary: Proposes an expert-editor stepwise-questioning multi-agent method for long-document summarization where expert and editor agents pose targeted questions and clues to guide another agent in refining summaries beyond input-length limits. It is evaluated on long scientific document datasets.

entry.title: Spatula: Exploring On-Demand In-Situ Interfaces and Interaction for Attribute Control

author.name: Boyu Li, Linjie Qiu, Lin-Ping Yuan, Duotun Wang, Yue Jiang, Zeyu Wang, Hongbo Fu

entry.summary: Presents Spatula, a proof-of-concept system that generates on-demand, in-situ attribute-control interfaces for creating motion graphics by analyzing animation context and framing attribute control as an explorable landscape across discoverability, resolution, scope, and expandability. A 12-user study found intuitive interactions.

entry.title: Annotation-Free Furniture Codes: What They Encode, and How Far They Transfer

author.name: Benjamin Friedman

entry.summary: Investigates whether a single self-supervised geometry-derived token from an FSQ point-cloud autoencoder can replace both the class label and canonical-pose annotations used by layout-based 3D scene synthesizers. Probes recover fine-category, super-category, and yaw information from the codes, and changing the reconstruction target trades off pose versus class signals.

entry.title: Characterising AI Models for Cataloguing

author.name: Miguel Arana-Catania, Neil Jefferies

entry.summary: Evaluates the application of AI models to the often-overlooked task of creating catalogue records for digital collections, comparing implementations and models with qualitative and quantitative analysis. It offers recommendations for using AI in cataloguing beyond the specific use case.

entry.title: Toward Inclusive Avatar Design with Limb Differences Through Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Fernanda Miyuki Yamada, Jo\~ao Paulo Gois, Hiroki Takahashi

entry.summary: This is a review and position paper surveying technical approaches for inclusive 3D avatar customization for people with limb differences and amputations, highlighting dataset scarcity and animation limitations for non-normative bodies. It matters for accessibility and representation in extended reality.

entry.title: Closing the Loop: An Access-Control Architecture for Automated, Anomaly-Driven Network Revocation in IoT Deployments

author.name: Muhammet Emir Korkmaz, Kemal Bicakci, Yusuf Uzunay

entry.summary: This paper presents an IoT access-control architecture that closes the loop from anomaly detection to automated enforcement using standard protocols (802.1X/EAP-TLS, RADIUS Change-of-Authorization, certificate revocation) rather than requiring programmable data planes. It matters for practical, deployable network security in real IoT environments.

entry.title: Evaluating RE Practices for Explainability: Synthesizing Insights from Daimler Truck into an Explainable RE Framework Proposal

author.name: Umm-e- Habiba, Lucas Mauser, Jonas Fritzsch, Justus Bogner, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: This qualitative industry study with practitioners at Daimler Truck investigates how existing requirements-engineering practices support explainability requirements across the RE lifecycle, synthesizing findings into a proposed explainable-RE framework. It matters for operationalizing explainability in safety-critical industrial AI development.

entry.title: Exploring Zero-Shot Foundation Models for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Martin Uray, Saverio Messineo, Roland Kwitt, Stefan Huber

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether a univariate time-series foundation model (TimesFM) can perform zero-shot multivariate anomaly detection on an industrial water-treatment benchmark using per-feature forecasting strategies. It probes foundation-model transfer without task-specific training. It informs practical industrial monitoring.

entry.title: AdaPCLA: Adaptive Prior-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Longitudinal EHR Generation

author.name: Shuai Cui, Chen Wenxuan, Wenjie Du, Jian Lou, Dan Li, Wenjie Feng

entry.summary: AdaPCLA improves generative modeling of longitudinal electronic health records for rare subpopulations by adaptively fitting the co-occurrence structure of tail events via distribution-aware training and simulated annealing, with training-free zero-shot distribution control. It targets privacy-preserving synthetic EHR fidelity. Tail-event faithfulness is the focus.

entry.title: GenDiff: A Dose and Anatomy Aware Diffusion Model with Structural Prior Refinement for Low-Dose CT Reconstruction and Generalization

author.name: Md Imam Ahasan, Guangchao Yang, A F M Abdun Noor, Kah Ong Michael Goh, S. M. Hasan Mahmud, Md Mahfuzur Rahman

entry.summary: GenDiff is a generalizable diffusion framework for low-dose CT reconstruction that jointly conditions on continuous radiation dose and anatomical information via a dose-anatomy encoder, aiming for robustness across dose levels and body regions unlike fixed-setting methods. It uses structural prior refinement. It targets clinical CT denoising generalization.

entry.title: VQCSim: When Does Compile-Once Statevector Simulation Beat Generic Quantum Frameworks?

author.name: Anton Firc, Martin Pere\v{s}\'ini, Vojt\v{e}ch Mr\'azek, Kamil Malinka, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Zbyn\v{e}k Li\v{c}ka, Nouhaila Innan, Walid El Maouaki, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: VQCSim is a compile-once, PyTorch-native statevector execution path with native autograd for hybrid quantum-classical ML, answering when compile-once specialization beats generic quantum frameworks for static variational circuits and reporting large median speedups across GPUs. It targets orchestration-overhead-dominated training regimes. It is a quantum ML systems contribution.

entry.title: TraceSynth: Generating Production-Quality Kernel Traces with Constraint-Guided Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuvraj Sehgal, Sneh Patel, Mahsa Panahandeh, Naser Ezzati-Jivan, Francois Tetreault

entry.summary: TraceSynth is a diffusion-based framework that generates synthetic operating-system kernel execution traces as multi-channel sequences using a Transformer denoising process with constraint-guided repair to enforce system invariants, augmenting scarce real traces for ML diagnostics. It finds strong workload dependence across six benchmarks. It targets privacy- and cost-constrained systems telemetry.

entry.title: Evaluating Nonuniform Dependability Across Response Conditions: A Conditional Generalizability Framework Illustrated in Automated Essay Scoring

author.name: Yi Gui

entry.summary: The paper introduces a conditional generalizability framework for automated essay scoring, treating scoring configurations as a universe of admissible measurement conditions and comparing analytical D-study projections with empirical configuration sweeps. It shows aggregate reliability can mask heterogeneity across response strata. It advances measurement-theoretic evaluation of scoring designs.

entry.title: How to Realize Recursively Self-Improving Agents and Personal Singularity: A Goal-, Scope-, Tool-, and Benchmark-Driven Multi-Agent Architecture

author.name: Chengshuai Yang

entry.summary: This single-author position/architecture paper proposes a governed multi-agent architecture for recursively self-improving agents and introduces personal singularity as a bounded human-AI co-development objective. Agents are defined by goal contracts, bounded scope, validated tool registries, and benchmarks.

entry.title: Filtering-out poor-quality images for data preparation

author.name: Roopdeep Kaur, Gour Karmakar, Muhammad Imran

entry.summary: This paper studies filtering poor-quality images during data preparation, reviewing classical filters and CNN-based denoising and noting their drawbacks such as fixed resizing requirements and narrow noise-type coverage. It positions image quality filtering as a key preprocessing step for downstream vision tasks.

entry.title: Helping AI models to meet the real world

author.name: David Chandler | Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

entry.summary: An MIT News profile of LIDS researcher Devavrat Shah, describing his work on resource-efficient, real-time decision-making methods and a foundation model for tabular time-series data commercialized through the spinoff Ikigai Labs. It highlights the gap between generic AI systems and organization-specific operational data.

entry.title: From ambiguous utterances to governed reuse classes: canonicalization, quotient invariance, and conditional decidability

author.name: Cosimo Spera, Ray Garcia

entry.summary: This note redefines semantic caching reuse on a mathematically characterized quotient of resolved conversational demands rather than embedding-similarity heuristics, introducing reading, resolution, and reuse identity relations forming a refinement chain. It shows pipeline outputs are invariant along the chain and links reuse to conditional decidability with authorization and versioning.

entry.title: Embark Now: User Demand Oriented Framework for Multi-day Urban Travel Itinerary Planning

author.name: Rongbo Qi, Yaqi Zhang, Shijun Yan, Xuemeng Liu, Xiangrui Cai, Chunyao Song

entry.summary: Embark Now integrates LLMs to capture user requirements with an enhanced Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure for multi-day urban travel itinerary planning, handling many points of interest, diverse preferences, and constraints like opening hours. It balances satisfaction and feasibility within limited computation time.

entry.title: A Knowledge-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Security Control Recommendation

author.name: Carolina Fern\'andez-Mart\'inez, Shuaib Siddiqui, Vanesa Daza

entry.summary: Presents a knowledge-based multi-agent decision support system that recommends security control sub-families from minimal user requirements, grounded in a Multi-Agent Influence Diagram game-theoretic model over seven security dimensions. It aims to help teams lacking cybersecurity expertise harden IT environments.

entry.title: ML in a Box: Analyzing Containerization Practices in Open Source ML Projects

author.name: Faten Jebari, Emna Ksontini, Amine Barrak, Wael Kessentini

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale empirical study of 1,993 ML-related Dockerfiles, analyzing container roles, build performance, caching, and refactoring practices across training, inference, and infrastructure. It reveals how the iterative nature of ML workflows shapes container footprint and build dynamics.

entry.title: Transcript-Free Lightweight Detection of Alzheimer's Disease from Spontaneous Speech Using Handcrafted MFCC-Dominant Acoustic Biomarkers

author.name: Rashin Gholijani Farahani, Azam Bastanfard

entry.summary: Presents a transcript-free, audio-only baseline for Alzheimer's detection from spontaneous speech using 99 handcrafted acoustic-temporal features (pauses, prosody, MFCCs) on 176 DementiaBank recordings, avoiding ASR and heavy deep models. It targets low-cost, language-independent screening.

entry.title: Comparing Socially-Equitable Renewable Energy Budget Allocation MDP Policies in Mature and Emerging Economies

author.name: Riya Kinnarkar, Mansur M. Arief, Yan Pratama Akhra, Dino Arla

entry.summary: Formulates socially-equitable renewable-energy budget allocation as a Markov Decision Process and compares the same policies across mature (eight US cities) and emerging (West Java) economies with differing decision levers. A receding-horizon value-iteration policy dominates in both settings.

entry.title: Polarization Detection: A Hybrid Approach with AfroXLMR-Social and DeBERTa for Low- and High-Resource Settings

author.name: Muhammad Abdullahi Said

entry.summary: Describes a hybrid system for the POLAR 2026 shared task on detecting polarized discourse in English and Hausa, using DeBERTa for English binary detection and the domain-adapted AfroXLMR-Social for Hausa and fine-grained subtasks. It emphasizes multilingual, low-resource polarization detection.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Microgrid Energy Coordination

author.name: Usman Haider, Karl Mason

entry.summary: This work proposes constraint-aware aggregation for federated reinforcement learning in microgrid energy coordination, incorporating estimated constraint violation into server-side updates via a simple reward-minus-penalty weighting rule. It aims to prevent unsafe global behavior that standard FedAvg induces. It targets safe distributed energy control.

entry.title: Transforming LLMs into Efficient Cross-Encoders via Knowledge Distillation for RAG Reranking

author.name: Shreeya Dasa Lakshminath, Shubhan S

entry.summary: This work fine-tunes an 8B LLaMA 3 model into an efficient cross-encoder reranker via supervised fine-tuning with LoRA plus 4-bit quantization, replacing costly cross-encoders in a BM25-plus-dense RAG pipeline and reporting double-digit percentage gains on a domain QA benchmark. It targets real-time RAG deployment. Efficiency for reranking is the focus.

entry.title: Removable Defects: The Economics and Limits of Deliberate Deficiency

author.name: Cheng Qian

entry.summary: This theoretical paper treats a model's deliberate deficiency as a design variable that can be economically retained and removed on demand by routing to a compensation channel, giving an advantage condition, a two-sided removability characterization via a coupling lemma, and connections to insurance and costly-state-verification economics. It formalizes when keeping a blind spot pays. It bridges ML competence trade-offs with economic theory.

entry.title: Towards Objective Dysgraphia Detection: A Multi-Branch Deep Learning Approach for Online Handwriting Analysis

author.name: Lydia Ouhib (LIASD), Yassine Ouzar (LIASD), Zo\'e Pinseel (LIASD), St\'ephane Bouilland (LIASD), Mehdi Ammi (LIASD)

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-branch deep learning framework for objective detection of dysgraphia in children using online handwriting captured on digitizing tablets, combining handcrafted kinematic features with learned embeddings. It aims to replace subjective clinician assessments with automated screening.

entry.title: A Production-Oriented Framework for Evaluation of SFX Generation

author.name: M\'elodie Desbos, Yara Bahram, Eric Granger, Mohammadhadi Shateri

entry.summary: Presents a production-oriented evaluation framework for reference-guided sound effects generation and editing, identifying nine production requirements and enabling structured comparison across heterogeneous audio methods. It targets the gap left by text-to-audio and unconditional-generation evaluations.

entry.title: Introducing Human-Centeredness in AI-Assisted Lexicography

author.name: Antonio San Martin, Catherine Trekker

entry.summary: This paper proposes a human-centered AI framework for AI-assisted lexicography, identifying four dimensions (augmented lexicographer, sociotechnical context, bias, and tool design) and arguing AI should augment rather than replace lexicographers. It matters for preserving linguistic and cultural diversity as generative AI enters dictionary work.

entry.title: Constructed Reality, Contested Priors: Decoupling and the Architecture of Cognitive Relapse Under the Free Energy Principle

author.name: MD Ibrahim Hossain Ridoy

entry.summary: This paper studies ontological inversion under the free energy principle using a convolutional variational autoencoder with a recurrent latent predictor as a proxy, asking whether a predictive system can adopt a synthetic environment as its default hypothesis, permanently displacing its original one. It matters as a computational exploration of belief entrenchment and cognitive relapse.

entry.title: Understanding Structured Health Data through Interaction-Aware Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ji Hwan Park, Ying Ding, Tianjin Guo

entry.summary: This short paper studies interaction-aware mixture-of-experts for post-stroke rigidity prediction from multi-level views of structured health records, finding minimal accuracy gains but that routing attribution reveals systematic view-importance differences relevant to interpretability. It matters mainly for view construction and interpretability in structured clinical data.

entry.title: PolarBM: Complex-valued Boltzmann Machine for Modeling Audio Signals in Polar and Log-polar Coordinates

author.name: Toru Nakashika, Kohei Yatabe

entry.summary: PolarBM is a complex-valued Boltzmann machine that models audio spectra directly in polar coordinates, with phase explicitly dependent on amplitude to preserve the physical amplitude-phase relationship. It avoids simplifying complex signals into real-valued frameworks. The scope is audio signal modeling.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks on Online Handwriting using Salience-based Temporal Editing

author.name: Yataro Tamura, Brian Kenji Iwana, Jiseok Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes a salience-guided temporal editing attack on online handwriting recognizers, generating adversarial perturbations of pen trajectories that avoid the unnatural jitter of additive spatial noise. It adapts adversarial attacks to time-series pen input. It exposes vulnerabilities in deployed handwriting systems.

entry.title: A Behavioral State Vocabulary in Sony ERS-111 R-CODE

author.name: Christopher A. Tucker

entry.summary: Presents a corpus-level analysis of behavior state diagrams from Sony's R-CODE scripts for the ERS-111 AIBO robot, identifying a compact recurring control grammar of initialization, sensing, iterative action, synchronization, and recovery. Argues this abstraction is useful for building new behavior routines on constrained robots.

entry.title: Can AI build a jet engine? JARVIS Challenge tests role of AI copilots in tough-tech engineering

author.name: Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics

entry.summary: MIT News reports on the JARVIS Challenge, an undergraduate sprint testing whether AI copilots can compress the design-build-test cycle for a complex physical system like a jet engine. The takeaway is that AI can accelerate safety-critical hardware engineering but human engineering judgment and manufacturing remain the decisive bottlenecks.

entry.title: Boltzmann MapReduce: A Partition-Function Reduce for Forkable Sandboxes

author.name: Yossi Eliaz

entry.summary: This theoretical piece reinterprets the MapReduce reduce step as a partition-function integral, showing that under local asymptotic normality each worker emits a Gibbs-Boltzmann confidence density with inverse temperature equal to sample size. It connects distributed aggregation to precision-weighted pooling and frequentist consistency as a zero-temperature limit.

entry.title: Feedback-Coupled Memory Systems in Continuous Time

author.name: Stefano Grassi

entry.summary: The Feedback-Coupled Memory Systems architecture fills in two previously undefined operators with a decentralized price-mechanism agent update and a non-Markovian coupled memory graph process treating the environment as a history-recording substrate. The resulting continuous-time instantiation claims global Lyapunov stability guarantees.

entry.title: Instruction Set and Language for Hypergraphs

author.name: Mario Pascual-Gonzalez, Ezequiel Lopez-Rubio

entry.summary: Presents IsalHG, a method for encoding any finite connected hypergraph of bounded arity as a string over a compact instruction alphabet, executed by a small virtual machine with a circular doubly-linked list and traversal pointers. It provides greedy and backtracking algorithms for encoding hypergraphs into strings.

entry.title: Exploratory Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting Meteorological Parameters in the Agricultural Sector

author.name: Piotr Sikora, Sotirios Kontogiannis

entry.summary: Comparatively evaluates recurrent (GRU, LSTM) and hybrid CNN-recurrent architectures for multivariate meteorological forecasting relevant to agriculture (evapotranspiration, vapor pressure deficit, wind) using 134k hourly ERA5 observations from Greece. It assesses 24-hour and 168-hour forecast horizons.

entry.title: Neutralizing Structural Inequality in the Nigerian FinTech Sector

author.name: Muhammad Abdullahi Said

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical human-AI triage model for point-of-sale fraud detection in the Nigerian FinTech sector, aiming to prevent discrimination laundering where infrastructure noise (rural network timeouts) is misread as fraud. It uses a three-tier routing policy with a calibrated ensemble and uncertainty-based escalation to human analysts.

entry.title: From Stochastic to Stable: Rank Stability and Structural Sufficiency in AI Visibility Measurement

author.name: Ronald Sielinski

entry.summary: Introduces a sequential convergence framework for AI-visibility measurement (which domains generative search engines cite) based on rank-stability and structural-sufficiency criteria to decide when enough data has been collected. It aims to give practitioners principled stopping rules for comparative citation studies.

entry.title: WasteAssistant: Regulation-Guided Visual Question Answering Framework for Intelligent Waste Segregation and Sustainable Managemen

author.name: Khush Kataruka, Harshit Maurya, Anuja Vats, Murari Mandal, Kiran Raja, Praveen Kumar Chandaliya

entry.summary: Introduces a vision-language question-answering framework and a 13,500-pair dataset for waste segregation aligned with Indian regulations. It applies multimodal models to a sustainability-focused classification and reasoning task.

entry.title: Benchmarking Sensor Robustness in Plasma Diagnostic Models: A Systematic Evaluation on TokaMark

author.name: Neerav Gupta

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic robustness benchmark for tokamak plasma diagnostic ML, evaluating multiple architectures across physically grounded sensor-failure scenarios on 11,573 MAST shots and introducing a standardized Robustness Score. Its central finding is that disruption-proximate sensor failures are especially damaging. It exposes fragility of models evaluated only on clean data.

entry.title: Ontology-Amplified Distillation and Contextuality Auditing for Sovereign Enterprise Language Models: A Combined Proof-of-Mechanism and Negative-Results Method Study

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan

entry.summary: This paper combines a proof-of-mechanism study of ontology-amplified distillation, adapting a Qwen student model to an enterprise ontology via SFT and ontology-grounded DPO on synthetic preference pairs, with a contextuality-auditing negative-results study, aimed at sovereign on-premise language models for regulated financial institutions. It reports high grounded rates on Vietnamese financial tasks. It targets data-residency-compliant enterprise LLMs.

entry.title: Dynamic Online Processor-Native Inference for State Estimation

author.name: Orestis Kaparounakis

entry.summary: This paper presents a Bayesian filtering technique using processor-native uncertainty tracking for both uncertainty propagation and inference, implementing deterministic hierarchical importance restructuring as a native operation to give bounded memory and deterministic latency for arbitrary code-defined models. It benchmarks against particle and Monte-Carlo filters on nonlinear state-space systems. It targets efficient on-device state estimation.

entry.title: Gemma The Unstopping: a Behavioral Experiment

author.name: TheVinci

entry.summary: A small behavioral experiment testing whether giving a Gemma model a stop_run tool changes its behavior on agentic tasks, both when step counts are known and unknown. Across hundreds of runs the model almost never voluntarily stopped, only ending runs politely when steps ran out, suggesting limited self-terminating tendency.

entry.title: LegalFarePlan: A Label-Setting Framework for Fare-Transparent Urban Rail Route Planning under Non-Additive Fare Rules

author.name: Tanghui Li

entry.summary: LegalFarePlan is a fare-transparent urban rail route planner that models legal exit-and-reentry operations as explicit auditable constraints under non-additive fare rules. It implements shortest-time baselines, greedy splitting, bounded exact label-setting, and Pareto search to produce explainable multi-segment route plans.

entry.title: Lightweight Multi-Scale Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Raheen Junaid Wani, Smruti R. Sarangi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale autoencoder for time-series anomaly detection on resource-constrained edge devices, balancing detection accuracy against memory, latency, and power. It targets IoT and sensor-network deployment. The emphasis is efficiency under strict constraints.

entry.title: A hybrid analytical-PINN model for subsurface simulation of geothermal heat exchangers in heterogeneous underground

author.name: Moke Rao, Thomas Hamacher, Smajil Halilovic

entry.summary: A parametric physics-informed neural network models heterogeneous soil thermal behavior around geothermal borehole heat exchangers, removing source singularities via analytical line-source models and using learned corrections as universal correctors. It targets subsurface geothermal engineering simulation. Impact is domain-specific.

entry.title: Learning-based Probabilistic Load Forecasting with Post-hoc and In-model Uncertainty

author.name: Sarah Al-Shareeda, Gulcihan Ozdemir, Heung Seok Jeon

entry.summary: This paper studies where to place uncertainty in smart-building load forecasting when deployment inputs are coarser than training data and missing features must be reconstructed, comparing post-hoc residual-quantile schemes against integrated in-model quantile approaches. It focuses on calibrated prediction intervals under input uncertainty. Impact is applied energy forecasting.

entry.title: Learning from Complementary Ultrasound Representations for Liver Disease Classification

author.name: Sabahattin Mert Daloglu, Gokce Bekar, Ceren Coskun, Senanur Sahin, Harvey Castro, Soner Hacihaliloglu, Halley P. Letter, Ilker Hacihaliloglu

entry.summary: This work combines conventional B-mode ultrasound with physics-guided and local-phase image representations, evaluated via masked autoencoders and graph convolutional networks, to improve differentiation of NASH from NAFLD on a multi-site Mayo Clinic cohort of over 2500 scans. It investigates whether complementary representations from one acquisition help subtle-tissue classification. It targets liver-disease diagnosis.

entry.title: Self-Consistent Flow: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Rectified Flow Models

author.name: Xu Han, Jiajing Hu, Li-Ping Liu

entry.summary: SPar-GAN adapts a Hamiltonian generative adversarial architecture to model planetary parachute and entry-vehicle dynamics from scarce, expensive test data, conditioning on canopy state to produce physically plausible trajectories where governing equations are incompletely known. It targets entry, descent, and landing modeling. It is a physics-aware generative approach for aerospace dynamics.

entry.title: From Patterns to Maze Structures: SMT-Based Path Synthesis and 2D/3D Construction

author.name: Shengyi Wang

entry.summary: This report encodes maze-path synthesis from input patterns like text or shapes as SMT global constraints on adjacency, continuity, and coverage, solving each fixed-bound instance in one call. It extends a conference paper toward planar mazes and 3D woven-maze constructions.

entry.title: Analyzing Image Encoder Choices and Graph Homophily in GCN Frameworks for Breast Ultrasound Classification

author.name: Sabahattin Mert Daloglu, Ceren Coskun, Harvey Castro, Soner Hacihaliloglu, Ilker Hacihaliloglu

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates five convolutional and transformer image encoders for graph-convolutional-network-based breast ultrasound classification, examining how encoder choice affects cosine-similarity kNN graph construction, homophily, and downstream accuracy. It targets automated screening under speckle noise and acquisition variability. The contribution is empirical encoder-graph analysis.

entry.title: AGM-like Paraconsistent Partial Meet Abductive Expansion Operation

author.name: Ulisses Franceschi Eliano

entry.summary: This formal-logic paper presents a paraconsistent AGM-style abductive expansion operation that can absorb contradictory explanatory hypotheses without collapsing into triviality, building on Pagnucco's earlier operation and a recent paraconsistent logic. It provides postulates and a transitively relational partial-meet construction.

entry.title: Semantic Drift and the Stability of Operator Control in Reasoning-Class Decision Support Systems

author.name: M. L. Kaluzhsky, V. A. Efirov

entry.summary: The article reports a two-month longitudinal experiment on human-machine co-authoring, describing a latent semantic context drift phenomenon in reasoning LLMs and proposing an operator control stability coefficient. It frames the problem within a cognitome theory of human-machine interaction.

entry.title: Biodefense, Biologics, and Bombs

author.name: Austin Morrissey

entry.summary: A biosecurity-focused piece arguing that rising biological weaponization risk from non-state actors represents a neglected market opportunity for venture capital, recommending investment in screening technologies and onshoring of chemical precursor manufacturing. It draws on the Tokyo attacks and a Senate biotechnology commission as context.

entry.title: Why frontier labs are scaling-pilled

author.name: invertedpassion

entry.summary: A crossposted essay arguing why frontier labs commit to scaling, grounding the argument in the bitter lesson and framing compute as scalable search over patterns for open-ended general intelligence. It is explanatory commentary on scaling philosophy rather than new results.

entry.title: Twitter Thoughts For You

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A commentary post updating the author's advice on how to use Twitter effectively in 2026, covering the resurgent For You feed, the platform's API changes, link handling, bots, and the rise of low-quality content. Primarily personal advice rather than research.

entry.title: Some Quick Thoughts on AI 2027

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: An opinion piece critiquing the AI 2027 forecasting scenario, arguing its endgame is too conventional and understates the potential for extreme miniaturization, self-replication, and synthetic-biology or nanotech discontinuities. It is speculative commentary rather than original research.

entry.title: What if AI Safety employees unionised?

author.name: beyarkay (Boyd Kane)

entry.summary: A policy-flavored thought experiment proposing that AI safety researchers form a union to collectively enforce red lines when companies abandon their safety commitments. It frames the problem of individual researchers being unable to hold labs accountable as a coordination problem suited to labor organizing.

entry.title: Our response to Séb Krier on Plan A

author.name: MKodama

entry.summary: A rebuttal to a critique of the AI 2040 Plan A governance proposal, correcting perceived mischaracterizations and defending the plan's iterative, transparency-based approach. It is an internal policy debate exchange.

entry.title: Posting Some Prompts

author.name: Arjun Panickssery

entry.summary: A meta commentary responding to calls that AI-assisted writers should just publish their prompts, presenting a set of the author's own prompts to a research-report scaffold alongside the resulting outputs. It functions as an experiment in transparent, prompt-first publishing.

entry.title: What if we actually want to solve the "hard problem of phenomenological consciousness"

author.name: mishka

entry.summary: A philosophical essay revisiting the hard problem of consciousness and qualia in the context of AI, framed explicitly for readers who already find the qualia concept meaningful. It is largely a conceptual and definitional discussion rather than empirical or technical research.

entry.title: A (Romanticised) Taxonomy of Thinkers

author.name: Ashe Vazquez Nuñez

entry.summary: A creative, romanticized taxonomy characterizing different archetypes of thinkers, such as the dialectician, the gardener, and the artist. It is reflective personal writing with no technical or empirical content.

entry.title: The Case for a Safety-Focused Vape Company

author.name: CMLKevin

entry.summary: A tongue-in-cheek pitch styled as an effective-altruism venture proposal for a safety-focused vape company with a capped-profit structure and non-profit lobbying arm. It is satire or a cultural in-joke rather than AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 14, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on foundational advances in scaling laws, sequence architectures, and training efficiency, complemented by high-impact safety and formal-verification work.

Architecture & efficiency:

  • DSSMs augment diagonal state-space recurrences with delayed-state feedback from delay differential equations, addressing fixed-state compression limits.
  • Requential Coding (Wilson, Finzi) reframes model compression via teacher-selected self-generated training data.
  • M+Adam hybridizes additive and multiplicative updates to stabilize low-precision training.
  • Sticky Jump Diffusions unify masked, continuous, and hybrid diffusion in one simulation-free framework.

Scaling, evaluation & world models:

  • Domain-Aware Scaling Laws formalize and quantify cross-domain data synergy in pretraining mixtures.
  • AdvancedMathBench offers 296 process-aware problems for proof generation and verification.
