entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-enhanced differentiable trajectory planning framework for IoT-connected autonomous driving that injects high-level scene semantics to improve coverage of long-tail interactions and consistency with downstream constrained refinement. It targets safe, executable trajectories under real-time constraints.

entry.title: Learning Roller-Skating Motions of Humanoid Robots Based on Adversarial Motion Priors

author.name: Yunkang Cheng, Yutong Wu, Menghan Li, Shihe Zhou, Mingguo Zhao

entry.summary: Presents an adversarial motion prior reinforcement learning framework that teaches humanoid robots two roller-skating gaits (Pump Glide and Push Glide) from separately motion-captured, retargeted references. Each gait uses independent policies and reward architectures for whole-body balance on rolling contacts.

entry.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Dakarai Crowder, Ruohan Zhang, Alexis E. Block, Wenzhen Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces a requirement-driven framework that derives whole-body social tactile sensing requirements (spatial resolution and placement) directly from VR-collected interaction data rather than predefined hardware layouts. It yields an open-source dataset of 5,520 trials across nine recurring social touch gestures.

entry.title: A Compact Top-Loading Robot for Endovascular Interventions: Design, Control and Evaluation

author.name: Jonas Fischer, Lennart Karstensen, Franziska Mathis-Ullrich

entry.summary: Presents a compact top-loading robotic system for endovascular interventions using two alternating carts with pneumatic membrane grippers to continuously translate and rotate standard catheter instruments. It aims to reduce surgeon radiation exposure and improve clinical workflow integration for vascular procedures.

entry.title: Learning to control switching nonlinear systems with Koopman operator regression

author.name: Edoardo Caldarelli, Oleksii Kachaiev, Cesare Molinari, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: Studies identification and control of switching nonlinear systems using Koopman operator regression in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, yielding a linear switching predictive model used in model predictive control. It derives learning rates and sub-optimality bounds for the resulting controller.

entry.title: What building Shippy taught us about building agents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Ai2 engineering post on lessons from building Shippy, arguing that reliable AI agents depend less on the underlying model than on deterministic tools, explicit guardrails, isolated infrastructure, and evaluations grounded in real workflows and live data. It offers practical agent-building guidance.

entry.title: Verifier-Guided Twelve-Tone Composition: A Generate-Verify-Repair Harness for Symbolic Music Generation

author.name: Congren Dai, Danni Zhao, Enyang Liu, Michael Ching Yam, Zhancheng Guo, Siyi Gu, Wentao Yang, Bo Dai, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic generate-verify-repair harness that wraps a language-model proposer with symbolic verification for twelve-tone composition, improving audited delivery yield from about 13 to 48 percent while abstaining otherwise. Blinded expert evaluation is included.

entry.title: MAC-Splat: Multi-Attribute Consistency for High-Fidelity Sparse-View Reconstruction

author.name: Jinqian Yang, Yichen Wu, Wanhua Li, Haokun Lin, Renzhen Wang, Xiangchu Feng, Xixi Jia

entry.summary: MAC-Splat improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by adding direct 3D consistency supervision built on the MASt3R geometric backbone and a frozen DINOv3 encoder for semantically informed correspondences. It introduces a Multi-Attribute Consistency loss to resolve the depth and correspondence ambiguities that photometric-only losses leave unaddressed.

entry.title: X-GuideAR: An Augmented Reality Framework to Mitigate Radiation Exposure during Fluoroscopic Guidance

author.name: Mingxu Liu, Zixuan Liu, Ruchen Cai, Yu-Chen Ku, Suxi Gu, Amit Jain, Alejandro Martin-Gomez, Mehran Armand

entry.summary: X-GuideAR is an augmented reality framework that generates synthetic X-ray previews to reduce fluoroscopic radiation exposure during orthopedic screw placement, demonstrated on S2 alar-iliac screws. It guides view acquisition and drilling before a confirming real X-ray is taken.

entry.title: Metadata Supervised MRI Representations for Modelling and Controlling Acquisition Variability

author.name: Mehmet Yigit Avci, Pedro Borges, Virginia Fernandez, Natalia Glazman, Paul Wright, Mehmet Yigitsoy, Sebastien Ourselin, Jorge Cardoso

entry.summary: This work jointly models MRI images and DICOM metadata to learn representations that disentangle anatomical structure from scanner- and protocol-dependent appearance. The resulting contrast representations organize heterogeneous acquisitions and detect image-metadata inconsistencies, improving interpretability and generalization.

entry.title: Higher-Order Cell Tracking Transformer

author.name: Jord\~ao Bragantini, Ilan Theodoro, Lo\"ic A. Royer

entry.summary: The Higher-Order Cell Tracking Transformer is an edge-centric architecture for reconstructing cell lineages from live-imaging microscopy that lets candidate cell links attend to one another, addressing how cell divisions entangle lineage paths and how candidate-graph edges carry little label information. It reframes tracking around higher-order relationships between candidate links rather than nodes.

entry.title: Beyond the Single Camera: Agentic Multi-View Reasoning in Sports Video Understanding

author.name: Kerui Chen, Jinglu Wang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: SportMV-Bench is a benchmark for multi-view sports video understanding built from official match recordings using a pipeline of LLM-based generation, MLLM-based verification, and human filtering, addressing the absence of multi-view evaluation for MLLMs. It targets scenarios with dense occlusion, rapid motion, and complex interactions unresolvable from a single viewpoint.

entry.title: Efficient and Robust Spiking Neural Networks for sEMG-Based Muscle Fatigue Detection

author.name: Kaiwen Tang, Jiaqi Dong, Zhanglu Yan, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Proposes an energy-efficient spiking neural network framework for muscle fatigue detection from surface EMG, using sparse event-driven computation and a quantization-compatible training scheme. Targets low-cost wearable health monitoring where standard deep models are too expensive.

entry.title: Learning High-Level Decision Making with an Interaction-Aware Attention-Based Network in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Marcelo Contreras, Willi Poh, Christoph Stiller, Ehsan Hashemi

entry.summary: Introduces DecisionPerceiver, a Perceiver-IO-inspired attention architecture that projects variable numbers of dynamic agents into a fixed-size latent for high-level lane-change and speed decisions, explicitly modeling traffic interactions with bounded complexity. Targets negotiation-intensive scenarios like intersections.

entry.title: Breaking the 15% Barrier: A Real-World Data-Driven System for Proactive Social Robot Triggered by User Nonverbal Cues

author.name: Yuga Yano, Yuki Okafuji, Ryo Miyoshi, Sanae Yamashita, Yoshiki Ohira

entry.summary: Studies real-world retail robot interactions and finds that 15.3 percent of robot utterances over a 6-day deployment were triggered by customers' nonverbal cues (approaching, waving, pointing) rather than speech, exposing a limitation of audio-only STT-LLM-TTS pipelines. It defines service-relevant nonverbal cues to enable proactive social robots.

entry.title: The Individual-Targeting Assumption: A Systematic Review of Proactive Robots in Human Group Settings

author.name: Tauhid Tanjim, Tasmia Mayen, Malte F. Jung, Susan R. Fussell

entry.summary: A systematic review of 63 proactive human-robot interaction studies in group settings finds a recurring Individual-Targeting Assumption where robots treat co-present people as independent targets rather than as members of cohesive social groups. It argues most designs ignore relational group structure.

entry.title: NextFund: A Unified Performance Tracking Platform for Agentic Portfolio Management

author.name: Changlun Li, Peixian Ma, Qiqi Duan, Zhenyu Lin, Peineng Wu

entry.summary: Introduces NextFund, an evaluation platform that makes financial-agent behavior observable under live market conditions by logging the full decision path from analyst judgments to execution. Aims to move beyond static exams and terminal-return reporting.

entry.title: Trustworthy synthetic data for campaign decision support: strategy simulation fidelity and the PolicySynth framework

author.name: Tung Dang, The Hung Phung, Son Lam Nguyen, Tu Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces strategy simulation fidelity, a criterion measuring whether synthetic customer data lead managers to the same go/no-go campaign decisions as real data, plus the PolicySynth framework to close the decision-alignment gap left by distributional-similarity metrics. It targets trustworthy synthetic data for decision support.

entry.title: A Risk-Field Enhanced Closed-Loop Digital Twin Framework for Autonomous Driving Safety Validation

author.name: Yongzhi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a risk-field enhanced closed-loop digital twin framework connecting physical traffic data, virtual reconstruction, and scenario evolution for autonomous driving safety validation. It aims to expose rare safety-critical scenarios more efficiently than road testing.

entry.title: CHM-Net: Center Heatmap-driven Macro-Micro Modeling Network for MRI-based Microbial Density Stratification

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Haolin Chen, Tingting Li, Bowen Yu, Qianyan Long, Tinghe Zhang, Xi Zhong, Xiaowei Hu, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai

entry.summary: Introduces a center heatmap-driven network for inferring microbial density from multimodal MRI, framed as a patient-level representation learning task for tumor assessment. It localizes small lesions before aggregating macro-micro evidence.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Across the Cardiac Amyloidosis Diagnostic Pathway: From Single-Modality Detection to Multimodal Clinical Integration

author.name: Diana Shadibaeva, Rochak Dhakal, Kui Zhang, Xiaofeng Yang, Saurabh Malhotra, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: A narrative review synthesizing AI applications across the cardiac amyloidosis diagnostic pathway, spanning ECG, echocardiography, CMR, and nuclear imaging by clinical task. It highlights the shift from single-modality detection toward multimodal clinical integration.

entry.title: Projection-Domain Sensitivity Analysis of Vertebral DRRs Under Intrinsic Calibration Perturbation

author.name: Lin Li, Chaochao Zhou, Benjamin Aubert, Junlin Guo, Junchao Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a synthetic framework analyzing how intrinsic calibration perturbations propagate into vertebral fluoroscopic projections and downstream 2D-3D registration performance. It uses CT-derived vertebral models and controlled cone-beam geometry to isolate calibration effects.

entry.title: End-to-End Real-Time Drone-Based Person Detection Framework Using Deep Learning

author.name: Payel Sarmah, Ayush Ranjan, Piyush Kaushik Bhattacharyya, Anil Kr. Shaw, Pradip Kr. Das

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time drone-based person detection pipeline built on a lightweight YOLOv8-nano model for wireless live video, characterizing detection performance across multiple flight altitudes. It targets search-and-rescue and surveillance applications where scale varies with altitude.

entry.title: Not All Color Categories Are Equally Stable: A Multilingual Free Color Naming Experiment

author.name: Nuray Toganas, Adilet Yerkin, Elnara Kadyrgali, Muragul Muratbekova, Aron Karatayev, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: Reports a free color-naming experiment with 92 participants examining the consistency of red, yellow, and green categories across shades using samples from the COLIBRI dataset. It finds that some color categories remain stable while others shift naming with changes in saturation and brightness.

entry.title: Align and Segment: Unsupervised Learning for Building Segmentation From Misaligned Labels

author.name: Venkanna Babu Guthula, Oswin Krause, Dimitri Gominski, Hui Zhang, Johan Mottelson, Ankit Kariryaa, Nico Lang, Christian Igel

entry.summary: The align-and-segment approach jointly learns label alignment and semantic segmentation when images and labels come from misaligned sources, a common problem in remote sensing with sources like OpenStreetMap. It uses a spatial transformer to apply affine corrections to labels during training.

entry.title: AU-Guided Synthetic Video Generation for Micro-Expression Recognition

author.name: Pei-Sze Tan, Sailaja Rajanala, Yee-Fan Tan, Raphael C. -W. Phan, Huey-Fang Ong

entry.summary: EquiME is a synthetic micro-expression dataset of 75K videos generated via action-unit-guided image-to-video generation from 15K faces across five emotions with demographic metadata. Models trained on it show competitive cross-dataset performance on SAMM and CASME II with low demographic variation.

entry.title: MED-DSLC: Multi-Expert-Domain Classification via Domain Supervision and Logit Calibration

author.name: Zheng Zeng, Deepak Sridhar, Nuno Vasconcelos

entry.summary: MED-DSLC addresses the degraded cross-domain calibration that arises when independently trained LoRA experts for CLIP-based zero-shot classification are merged. It uses domain supervision and logit calibration to restore globally comparable logits across specialized domain experts.

entry.title: GHOST: Geometry-Guided Hallucination of Opaque Surface Textures

author.name: Langxu Zhao, Zuan Gu, Tianhan Gao

entry.summary: GHOST is a geometry-guided preprocessing framework that transforms transparent object regions into opaque, structurally consistent representations using visual foundation models, without retraining downstream depth or reconstruction models. It combines transparency decomposition, surface normal recovery, and geometry-semantic integration.

entry.title: Parallax Portrait Matting

author.name: Xin Cai, Jiawen Chen, Lars Jebe, Tianfan Xue, Zhoutong Zhang

entry.summary: Parallax Portrait Matting is a two-frame matting method that uses a second image captured with slight viewpoint change, exploiting foreground-background parallax naturally present in burst photography. It avoids specialized capture setups like green screens or polarized lighting.

entry.title: Structure-Detail Decoupled Autoregressive Generation for Fast and High-Fidelity Virtual Try-On

author.name: Lu Yang, Xiaonan Hu, Yanan Li, Daqi Liu, Xiang Bai, Hao Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces VAR-VTON, a visual autoregressive virtual try-on model with structure-detail decoupled generation to enable fast, high-fidelity garment synthesis while preserving person identity. It provides an effective bi-conditioning mechanism for VAR models, previously unexplored for try-on, avoiding the high-frequency detail loss of latent-compression diffusion.

entry.title: ASUMOT: Motion-Consistency-Based Asynchronous UAV Detection and Tracking with Event Cameras

author.name: Baofeng Jia, Xiaoyu Chen, Jingyuan Zhang, Zongze Wu, Haochen li, Jing Han, Lianfa Bai

entry.summary: ASUMOT is a motion-consistency-based asynchronous framework for detecting and tracking long-range UAVs directly on raw event-camera data, where targets appear as sparse fragmented blobs. It models each UAV as a set of motion-consistent event blobs with a local estimator, lightweight verifier, and motion cues to avoid duplicate trajectories.

entry.title: HierCAD: Hierarchical Text-to-CAD Design via Structure Alignment and Parameter Grounding

author.name: Jimin Xu, Tianbao Wang, Tao Jin, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: HierCAD is a hierarchical text-to-CAD framework that decomposes CAD construction trees into object-level procedural reasoning and part-level topology reasoning trajectories to improve structural consistency and parameter grounding. It adds a unified structure-alignment and parameter-grounding learning strategy.

entry.title: Parse, Search, and Confirmation: Training-Free Aerial Vision-and-Dialog Navigation with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning and Structured Spatial Memory

author.name: Yu Qi, Hongyu Li, Shaofei Huang, Tianrui Hui, Yaxiong Wang, Lechao Cheng, Zhun Zhong, Si Liu, Meng Wang

entry.summary: PSC-AVDN is a training-free framework for aerial vision-and-dialog navigation that couples a three-stage parse-search-confirmation reasoning pipeline with structured spatial memory. It uses an LLM to convert ambiguous dialogue into geometric cues and chain-of-thought reasoning for stepwise target exploration under high-altitude UAV views.

entry.title: Robustness and Stability Analysis of Differentiable Shift-Variant FBP for Cone-Beam CT under Challenging Acquisition Settings

author.name: Chengze Ye, Linda-Sophie Schneider, Yipeng Sun, Mareike Thies, Siyuan Mei, Paula Andrea P\'erez-Toro, Siming Bayer, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: Studies the robustness of a differentiable shift-variant filtered backprojection framework for cone-beam CT reconstruction under irregular trajectories and sparse-view conditions. It finds reconstruction is largely insensitive to trajectory ordering but sensitive to spatial sampling distribution.

entry.title: Differentiable Proxy Learning for Adaptive Quantization Control in H.264 Video Coding

author.name: Qihan Xu, Ivan V. Baji\'c

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable proxy for the H.264 intra codec that enables gradient-based adaptive quantization parameter control for objectives like perceptual quality or machine-vision tasks. It emphasizes explicitly characterizing fidelity of the proxy to the real codec.

entry.title: Diffusion MRI preprocessing affects ADC estimation and automatic PI-RADS v2.1 classification in bi-parametric prostate MRI

author.name: Christos Kanakis, Mathias Perslev, Tim Schakel, Silvia Ingala, Akshay Pai, Dennis Klomp, Chantal M. W. Tax

entry.summary: Investigates how diffusion MRI preprocessing steps (denoising, Gibbs-ringing correction, distortion registration) affect ADC estimation and automatic PI-RADS classification in prostate MRI using the fastMRI cohort. Highlights the lack of standardized preprocessing in prostate imaging.

entry.title: LLM-Centric Agentic AI for UAV Swarms: Architecture, Enabling Technologies, and Open Problems

author.name: Yousef Emami, Rahim Taheri, Mohammadhossein Homaei, Muhammad Atif Ur Rehman, Mohammad Shojafar

entry.summary: A survey/position paper proposing LLM-centric agentic AI architectures for UAV swarms, integrating perception, memory, reasoning, and action into closed-loop cognitive control for search-and-rescue and monitoring. It also discusses the expanded cybersecurity attack surface such systems introduce.

entry.title: SLIDER: Sparse History-Guided Aerial Robot Target Search using Sliding Local Maps

author.name: Xiaolei Hou, Zheng Pan, Hua Lan, Zhenghao Zou, Yinhong Chen, Chenxi Zhu, Yang Lyu, Jinwen Hu, Chunhui Zhao

entry.summary: SLIDER is a lightweight, memory-efficient aerial target-search framework that combines a local sliding map with sparse global history, adds a real-time observation-quality evaluation for frontier detection, and uses incremental viewpoint clustering for scalable planning. It avoids dependence on globally dense maps.

entry.title: Mapping Pamir: Multi-Session Visual-Inertial SLAM and 3D Reconstruction of an Underwater Shipwreck

author.name: Michalis Chatzispyrou, Luke Horgan, Hyunkil Hwang, Harish Sathishchandra, Chinmay Burgul, Monika Roznere, Alberto Quattrini Li, Philippos Mordohai, Ioannis Rekleitis

entry.summary: Presents a multi-session visual-inertial SLAM and 3D reconstruction framework for an underwater shipwreck using an affordable action camera augmented with dive-computer depth, combining SVIn2 trajectories with COLMAP structure-from-motion for dense reconstruction. Calibration targets align sessions into a common frame.

entry.title: Whole-Body Semantic-to-Actuation Grounding of Elephant-Inspired Soft-Trunk Motion via Lightweight Flow Matching

author.name: Tingcong Liu, Tongshun Chen, Siyi Ma, Yuhao Wang, Aye Phyu Phyu Aung, Ibrahim Alsarraj, J. Senthilnath, Bo An, Ke Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a whole-body semantic-to-actuation grounding framework for elephant-inspired soft-trunk robots that converts multimodal LLM responses into bounded intent-intensity tuples and generates feasible tendon-actuation trajectories via lightweight rectified flow. It targets expressive close-contact human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Stop to Decide: Latency-Aware Proprioceptive Navigation Primitives for Mapping-Free Quadruped Inspection

author.name: Hanting Suo, Haonan Yan, Liang Wang, Aiguo Song

entry.summary: Analyzes how compute-induced latency (about 15 Hz navigation loop) breaks a common proprioceptive stair-summit detection pattern for quadrupeds, causing overshoot, and shows a stop-to-decide climb-settle cadence keeps overshoot near zero across loop rates. It offers latency-aware mapping-free navigation primitives.

entry.title: CR-Solver: GPU-Accelerated Kinematics Solver for Tendon-driven Continuum Robots

author.name: Heqing Yang, Yang Yi, Linqing Zhong, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu

entry.summary: CR-Solver is a two-stage GPU-accelerated optimization-based kinematics solver for tendon-driven continuum robots that unifies inverse kinematics, path following, and trajectory planning in one constrained nonlinear framework. It addresses the gap left by rigid-body-based planning libraries.

entry.title: From Sketch Prior to Trajectories: A Mission-Oriented Coordinated Navigation Framework for Indoor UAV Swarm

author.name: Xinhang Xu, Ruiyang Liu, Haotian Jin, Yi Wang, Hongming Shen, Jianping Li, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: Proposes a mission-oriented coordinated navigation framework for indoor UAV swarms that leverages sketch-map priors (floor plans, CAD, evacuation diagrams) and exploits fixed-altitude planar connectivity to sequence region visits and generate trajectories. It targets inspection, patrol, and delivery rather than exploration.

entry.title: Better Call Sol The Workhorse

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi Mowshowitz aggregates community reactions to OpenAI GPT-5.6-Sol and its cheaper Terra and Luna variants, comparing them against Anthropic Fable across intelligence, alignment, and workflow fit. Note that these models had general availability in late June 2026, so this is analysis of existing models rather than a launch announcement.

entry.title: TC-MAF: Train-Calibrated Bounded Multi-Evidence Fusion for Multimodal Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ming Deng, Sijin Sun, Xiaochuan Hu, Xing Wu

entry.summary: TC-MAF is a base-anchored multi-evidence fusion design for multimodal industrial anomaly detection combining a multimodal detector, complementary Dinomaly evidence, and a cross-modal consistency cue under a fixed fusion formula. A training-dispersion confidence term scales auxiliary participation using only normal training statistics, reaching strong MVTec-3D results.

entry.title: PREF-Gate: Provenance-Constrained Relational Evidence Fusion with Validation-Gated Selection for Graph Fraud Detection

author.name: Liming Liu, Chao Hu, Mingfei Lu, Yiwei Ge, Xingle Li, Heyuan Shi

entry.summary: Presents PREF-Gate for graph fraud detection, separating label-free context evidence from self-excluded training-label neighborhood evidence to avoid leakage, with a validation gate to select between experts. Emphasizes provenance-constrained, auditable decisions.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for RFID-Based Spatial Geometry Inference in Spatial AI Systems

author.name: Curtis Shull, Merrick Green, Roy Rucker

entry.summary: Introduces a graph neural network framework that infers indoor spatial geometry from RFID observations by modeling relational structure among tags and infrastructure, rather than predicting isolated coordinates. It targets spatial understanding for indoor intelligent systems.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Execution under Dynamic Fees in a Closed-Loop DEX Simulator

author.name: Wen-Ting Wang

entry.summary: Builds a closed-loop DEX simulator with dynamic fees, fee-sensitive noise flow, and closed-form arbitrage to study reinforcement learning for trade execution, where historical data cannot identify order-flow response. A small DQN is found to be the only valid learned policy against tuned benchmarks.

entry.title: Link Adaptation Using Joint-Thompson Sampling

author.name: Vignatha Vinjam, Manjunath Kolavennu, Myna Vajha, Karthik Periyapattana Narayanaprasad

entry.summary: Proposes a joint Thompson sampling approach for link adaptation that exploits the ordered structure of modulation-and-coding-scheme success probabilities to select MCS from ACK/NACK and channel-quality feedback. It frames the MAC-layer selection as a structured multi-armed bandit.

entry.title: Fast Data-Driven Modeling of Hydraulic Clutch Control Pressure with Latch-State Classification and Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Yash Bagla, Jason Schneider

entry.summary: Presents a data-driven method for modeling nonlinear hydraulic clutch pressure response using latch-state classification followed by Gaussian process regression on partitioned regimes. Adding current-derivative features and regime classifiers improves hysteresis and latch-behavior modeling.

entry.title: Learning To Focus: Anatomy-Guided Attention Regularization for Medical Image Classification

author.name: Tonmoy Hossain, Atiqur Rahman, Farhana Hossain Swarnali, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper regularizes attention in medical image classifiers using anatomical shape priors extracted from segmentation foundation models, avoiding costly manual mask annotation. The goal is to guide networks toward diagnostically relevant regions without training a dedicated segmentation model.

entry.title: TreeSoc: Tree-Structured Dynamic Reasoning and Tool Synergy for Soccer Video Understanding

author.name: Thanh-Nhan Vo, Thanh-Khoi Nguyen, Trong-Thuan Nguyen, Trung-Hoang Le, Minh-Triet Tran

entry.summary: TreeSoc reformulates soccer video question answering as a hierarchical tree search, using depth-first decomposition of complex queries into ordered sub-tasks with adaptive tool routing. It targets multi-step reasoning and coordinated tool integration where VLMs typically fail.

entry.title: Temporal Feature Distillation for Label-Efficient Precise Event Spotting in Sports Videos

author.name: Hao Xu, Xinyu Wei, Sam Wells, Sunil Aryal

entry.summary: Temporal Feature Distillation is a semi-supervised objective for precise event spotting in sports videos that aligns temporally informative backbone features rather than projection-head outputs to preserve subtle motion cues. It addresses the failure of standard self-distillation methods that suppress fine motion as noise.

entry.title: The Devil Is in the Leakage: A Disentangled Dual-Purification Framework for High-Fidelity Hairstyle Transfer

author.name: Jijie Li, Jiankuo Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: This work identifies an identity-leakage problem in diffusion-based hairstyle transfer where reference hairstyle features retain the reference identity or pose, and proposes a disentangled dual-purification framework to address it. The method aims for high-fidelity hairstyle transfer while preserving source identity.

entry.title: Efficient Tuning Before Low-Bit Post-Training Quantization for Stochastic Gradient Descent-optimized Models

author.name: Peng Xia, Junbiao Pang, Muhammad Ayub Sabir

entry.summary: ETBQ is a pre-conditioning tuning stage applied to SGD-optimized models before low-bit post-training quantization, arguing that quantization accuracy is limited by the full-precision model's quantization-error tolerance, not just post-hoc reconstruction. It tunes the FP model to be more amenable to 2-bit or 4-bit quantization.

entry.title: Single-Teacher View Augmentation: Enhancing Knowledge Distillation with Student-Guided Perturbations

author.name: Xuyi Yu, Yaohua Liu, Ziming Song, Yinghai Zhao, Huipeng Zhang, Kuizhi Mei

entry.summary: This work generates diverse virtual teacher views for knowledge distillation from a single teacher using student-guided perturbations, balancing efficiency against controlled diversity. It avoids both the cost of multi-teacher distillation and the uncontrolled diversity or multi-stage overhead of prior single-teacher augmentation methods.

entry.title: GB-SVFBP: Gaussian-Based Shift-Variant FBP neural network

author.name: Chengze Ye, Linda-Sophie Schneider, Yipeng Sun, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: GB-SVFBP is a Gaussian-based shift-variant filtered backprojection neural network for reconstructing non-circular-trajectory cone-beam CT, introducing a trainable 2D Gaussian model to represent the trajectory-related filtering component. This substantially reduces the number of trainable parameters while maintaining reconstruction quality.

entry.title: Similarity-Guided Curriculum Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Neural Architecture Synthesis

author.name: Anujaya Vijayakumar, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: This paper introduces a MinHash-based similarity scheduling framework that builds a progressive curriculum over neural architecture code for LLM-based neural architecture search, presenting architectures in increasing heterogeneity with cumulatively merged LoRA adapters. It is evaluated on OlympicCoder-7B within the LEMUR benchmark on CIFAR-10.

entry.title: Event-RGB Adaptive Tracking for Nighttime Highway Perception

author.name: Haidong Wang, Hengxing Cai, Wanlei Li, Xiaogang Xiong, Renxin Zhong

entry.summary: JEAT is a joint event-RGB adaptive tracking framework for nighttime highway perception that fuses event-camera and RGB data without rigid hard-coded modality prioritization. It targets degraded RGB sensing under low light, motion blur, and poor signal-to-noise ratios in unlit high-speed highway environments.

entry.title: Feature-Space Guided Diffusion for Realistic Ultrasound Image Synthesis

author.name: Marina Dom\'inguez, N\'elida Mirabet-Herranz, Valery Naranjo

entry.summary: This work proposes Feature-Space Candidate Guidance, a training-free sampling strategy that reduces the gap between synthetic and real B-mode ultrasound images in a frozen ultrasound foundation model's representation space. It targets realistic speckle texture, tissue contrast, and attenuation beyond mere anatomical plausibility.

entry.title: Illuminant-Adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for Camera Color Correction

author.name: Claudio Rota, Luca Cogo, Simone Bianco, Raimondo Schettini

entry.summary: This paper proposes C2LUT, a color correction framework using illuminant-adaptive 3D lookup tables that combines a chromaticity-aware illuminant representation with a non-linear color transform for mapping camera sensor responses to device-independent color spaces. It targets the challenges posed by highly chromatic and spectrally complex LED illuminants.

entry.title: SVI360: Spherical Video Interpolation

author.name: Le-Kim Nguyen, Renato Martins, Pascal Vasseur, Cedric Demonceaux

entry.summary: SVI360 is a dual-branch framework for omnidirectional (spherical) video interpolation that combines the image frame and its rotated orthogonal view to handle severe distortions near the poles. It reinforces equivariance of flow displacements between original and orthogonal views to improve intermediate frame prediction.

entry.title: Tracking Intermittent Particles with Self-Learned Visual Features

author.name: Raphael Reme (IP Paris, BIA, IDS, IMAGES), Victor Piriou (BIA), Alison Hanson (IP Paris, IDS, IMAGES), Rafael Yuste (IP Paris, IDS, IMAGES), Alasdair Newson (IP Paris, IDS, IMAGES), Elsa Angelini (IP Paris, IDS, IMAGES), Jean-Christophe Olivo-Marin (BIA), Thibault Lagache (BIA)

entry.summary: Introduces self-supervised visual feature learning combined with positional cues to stitch fragmented particle tracks in time-lapse fluorescence microscopy where occlusion causes broken tracklets. Demonstrated on Hydra vulgaris neuron sequences with high stitching accuracy.

entry.title: Desc++: Efficient Descriptor Enhancement for Data Association in Existing Visual SLAM Systems

author.name: Ting-Wei Ou, Huang-Ting Lin, Kuu-Young Young

entry.summary: Desc++ enhances existing handcrafted descriptors in visual SLAM systems to improve robustness to illumination and viewpoint changes without replacing the full extraction-matching pipeline. It uses richer contextual modeling than prior simplified-attention enhancement methods.

entry.title: RoboNav-Arm: Agentic AI-Driven Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance for Robotic Manipulator in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Aachal Sharma, Narendra Kumar Dhar

entry.summary: RoboNav-Arm is an agentic framework for robotic manipulators that performs real-time obstacle detection, 3D localization, and generates structured semantic reports to guide safe task execution in cluttered environments. A central coordination module handles tool invocation and re-planning.

entry.title: Diffusion for Long-Horizon Multi-Robot Path Planning in Human-Shared Environments

author.name: Vaibhav Sanjay, Yorai Shaoul, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Presents a myoelectric tentacle-shaped prosthesis with a logarithmic-spiral curling geometry, EMG control, sensorless object detection via motor-current slope analysis, and vibrotactile feedback. It aims for an intuitive, adaptive assistive device without dedicated contact sensors.

entry.title: PinFT: Miniature 5-Axis Force/Torque Sensor Embeddable to Tweezer-like Tool

author.name: Leo King, Jenny Chen, Tae Myung Huh

entry.summary: PinFT is a miniature five-axis capacitive force/torque sensor integrated at the tip of tweezer-like tools using a three-PCB stack and silicone dielectric, achieving low force and torque errors with high R-squared across axes. It enables tip-level force sensing for fine manipulation.

entry.title: Soft Eversion Robots for Colonoscopy: Challenges, Open Problems, and Emerging Solutions

author.name: Cem Suulker, Thomas Mack, Qingzheng Cong, Neri Niccol\`o Dei, Reza Kashef, Mohammad Sheikh Sofla, Kaspar Althoefer

entry.summary: Benchmarks four recent soft eversion robot architectures against clinical colonoscopy constraints such as colon length, luminal diameter, bending angle, and working-channel needs. It identifies key trade-offs, especially integrating steering with payload delivery.

entry.title: A Model for Mediating Multi-Modal Human Intent into Safe Maneuvers for UAVs

author.name: Sofia Nelson, Dalal Alrajeh, Pedro Antonio Alarcon Granadeno, Jane Cleland-Huang

entry.summary: Presents a requirements-governed maneuver-response model that treats multimodal operator inputs (speech, gestures, interfaces) as bounded maneuver requests rather than direct commands, mapping them to constrained motion primitives via a request-evaluate-execute pipeline. It mediates human intent into safe UAV maneuvers under terrain, separation, and envelope constraints.

entry.title: Tracking Through Decoupling Singularities: A Singularity-Robust Homotopy-Continuation Extension of Feedback Linearization

author.name: Alex Borisevich

entry.summary: Develops a singularity-robust trajectory-tracking controller for nonlinear systems that can track through decoupling singularities with bounded control, recasting tracking as arc-length homotopy continuation and using a least-norm Moore-Penrose solution. It extends classical feedback linearization to fail-safe regimes.

entry.title: A short summary of AI 2040: Plan A

author.name: Harjas

entry.summary: A LessWrong post offering an unofficial short summary of the AI 2040 Plan A scenario, which the author prefers over AI 2027 and argues deserves wider readership despite its length. It aims to make the detailed scenario more accessible to readers unwilling to read the full document.

entry.title: An Epistemic Audit for Existential Risks from AI

author.name: Alexander Müller

entry.summary: Introduces an Epistemic Audit tool for existential AI risk, a structured framework for mapping and tracking one's beliefs and uncertainties along the causal chain from capable systems to catastrophe. It is designed for repeated self-assessment and potential cross-respondent aggregation.

entry.title: Compositional Context Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Model for Complex Assembly Action Understanding from Videos

author.name: Hao Zheng, Jinyi Huang, Tiantian Zheng, Xun Xu, Tuka Alhanai

entry.summary: The paper adapts vision-language models to assembly action understanding by decomposing actions into Verb/Object/Tool elements and fine-tuning with templated QA pairs for near-deterministic outputs. A layer-partitioned alternating training scheme enables efficient multi-task learning under limited data.

entry.title: Design Choices in Splitting-Based Self-Supervised Sparse-View CT Reconstruction

author.name: Nadja Gruber, Lukas Neumann, Ander Biguri, Gyeongha Hwang, Markus Haltmeier, Johannes Schwab

entry.summary: This study provides a unified framework that decomposes self-supervised splitting-based sparse-view CT reconstruction into partitioning, preprocessing, and inference components for controlled comparison. It evaluates two incremental extensions across simulated and real CT datasets.

entry.title: Difference-Driven Gating: Adaptive Feature Fusion for U-Net Decoder

author.name: Kai Li, Xuechao Zou, Jiashen Fu, Zijun Yan, Xintong Wang, Xiaolin Hu

entry.summary: This paper proposes difference-driven gating for U-Net decoders, deriving attention weights from the difference between top-down decoder and bottom-up encoder feature streams rather than from either stream alone. Two difference-based gating variants modulate encoder features for better fusion.

entry.title: A Novel Method to Evaluate Models on Unreliable, Noisy and Inconsistent Labels: Adaptive Resolution Label Aggregation (ARLA)

author.name: Natasha Randall, Gernot Heisenberg

entry.summary: ARLA (Adaptive Resolution Label Aggregation) dynamically adapts the resolution of both labels and model predictions at inference before computing evaluation metrics to fairly assess segmentation models on noisy, inconsistent labels. It is demonstrated on a real flood prediction model where label inconsistency confounds standard metrics.

entry.title: CFR-Net:Collaborative Feature Refnement Network for Medical Image Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zihan Nie, Muhao Xu, Wei Feng, Yuan Cui, Hua Wei, Sijie Niu, Yi Wan, Xunbin Wei, Weiye Song, Zongyuan Ge

entry.summary: CFR-Net is a collaborative feature refinement network for medical image anomaly detection that refines frozen teacher and trainable student features with shared parameters before decoding and enforces cross-space consistency after decoding. It addresses limited adaptability of natural-image-pretrained networks to medical anomalies.

entry.title: RASR: Range-Aware Scale Recovery for Metric UAV Navigation

author.name: Hongtao Liang, Xinyu Shao, Chenxu Wang, Yiyao Wan, Jiahuan Ji, Fangwei Ye, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu

entry.summary: RASR (Range-Aware Scale Recovery) addresses poorly calibrated metric scale in dense pair-geometry foundation models for GNSS-denied UAV last-meter navigation, separating a transferable scale-recovery core from a protocol-specific calibration module. It compresses frozen MASt3R-style reconstruction outputs to correct distance-dependent residuals near the goal.

entry.title: Life as Plasmas: Autonomy and Interactivism in-materio

author.name: Nicol\'as Hinrichs, Mahault Albarracin, Felipe Engelberger, Leonardo Christov-Moore, Daniel Polani

entry.summary: A theoretical framework arguing that minimal autonomy in the interactivist sense corresponds to a distinct non-equilibrium phase of matter, using complex plasmas as a non-biological exemplar of life-like organization. It proposes diagnostic criteria such as free-energy throughput and organizational closure.

entry.title: IBPA: Real-time Free-form Manifold Mesh Reconstruction via Incremental Ball Pivoting with Integrated Hole Detection

author.name: Mauhing Yip, Mohit Singh, Kostas Alexis, Christian Schellewald, Annette Stahl

entry.summary: Presents IBPA, a real-time incremental ball-pivoting method for free-form manifold mesh reconstruction with integrated hole detection, aimed at visualizing seafloor coverage during underwater vehicle surveys. It overcomes the single-elevation limitation of traditional digital terrain models.

entry.title: Pausing AI at human level seems harder than pausing ASAP

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: Argues that pausing AI development as soon as possible is easier than waiting to pause at human-level AI, because human-level systems create enormous economic incentives to continue and can accelerate capabilities as much as safety. It responds to the case for delaying a pause until AI can assist safety research.

entry.title: Revisiting Matching Response and Swept Feature Volumes for Wide-baseline Omnidirectional Stereo

author.name: Seungjin Jeon, Jongwoo Lim, Changhee Won

entry.summary: This work introduces a training strategy for confidence estimation in wide-baseline omnidirectional stereo by reinterpreting the expectation of matching responses as an intrinsic confidence signal. It also adds swept feature volume resampling to predict meta-information without auxiliary heads or multi-pass inference.

entry.title: Video Transformer for Remote Identity Document Hologram Detection

author.name: Joris Voerman, Nicolas Sidere, Jean-Christophe Burie

entry.summary: This paper uses a video transformer to detect holograms on identity documents from mobile-device video for remote authentication, targeting an underutilized but promising security feature. It addresses the growing threat of AI-generated counterfeit ID documents without requiring specialized sensors like infrared.

entry.title: Backbone-Agnostic Perturbation-Induced Uncertainty Learning for End-to-End Real-World Image Dehazing

author.name: Bingcai Wei

entry.summary: BPUL is a plug-and-play, backbone-agnostic uncertainty learning framework for real-world image dehazing that introduces a learnable perturbation-induced uncertainty modulator to model uncertainty hidden in degraded features and haze priors. It targets the spatially non-uniform, illumination-dependent, and physically ambiguous nature of real haze.

entry.title: Calibrated Hybrid CNN-Transformer for Retinal OCT Classification

author.name: Animesh Kumar

entry.summary: This paper pairs a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder with an XGBoost head and a clinical safety layer of confidence calibration, out-of-distribution rejection, and per-prediction uncertainty flagging for retinal OCT classification. On four-class OCT it reaches 95.4% accuracy while cutting calibration error twelvefold.

entry.title: Chalito: An Extensible Library for Filtering-Based State Estimation in Quadruped Robots

author.name: Hilton Marques Souza Santana, Jo\~ao Carlos Virgolino Soares, Marco Antonio Meggiolaro, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: Chalito is an extensible MATLAB/Python library for benchmarking filter-based state estimation algorithms on quadruped robots, importing URDF models and supporting multiple filters on simulated and real data. It aims to enable fair, reproducible comparisons.

entry.title: Direct Rotor Thrust Sensing and Feedback Control for Disturbance Rejection of Multirotors Using Load-cells

author.name: Peter B\"ohm, Michael Br\"unig, Peyman Z. Moghadam, Pauline E. I. Pounds

entry.summary: Uses load cells for direct rotor thrust sensing on multirotors to enable faster feedback control and disturbance rejection against gusts, inflow variation, and ground effect. It bypasses reliance on trajectory-based disturbance estimation that reacts only after the aircraft is affected.

entry.title: Underwater Dead Reckoning with Deployable Situation-Triggered Covariance Scheduling

author.name: Akshay Naik (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering), Ramavarapu S. Sreenivas (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Department of Industrial and Enterprise Systems Engineering), Dustin Nottage (U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center, Construction Engineering Research Laboratory), Ahmet Soylemezoglu (U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center, Construction Engineering Research Laboratory)

entry.summary: Presents a situation-triggered adaptive robust extended Kalman filter for underwater dead reckoning on a BlueROV2, where an onboard probabilistic trigger switches to pre-calibrated noise matrices during turns or unreliable-measurement periods. It improves position estimation without external positioning or vision.

entry.title: CSI-Assisted Edge SLAM Testbed Platform for 5G Connected Unmanned Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Boris Radovanovic, Sasa Talosi, Srdjan Sobot, Dejan Vukobratovic

entry.summary: Describes a testbed integrating channel state information as an extra sensing modality for edge-offloaded SLAM on 5G-connected ground vehicles within a mobile edge computing framework. It explores integrated sensing and communications for connected robotics moving toward 6G.

entry.title: The Flood, by Anton Leicht

author.name: Austin Chen

entry.summary: A cross-posted essay by Anton Leicht arguing that a coming wave of wealth among AI-safety-aligned frontier lab employees could either rescue or squander American AI politics, using the Nile flood as a metaphor for channeling that money effectively. It focuses on political funding strategy for AI safety.

entry.title: Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis

author.name: Ekkachai Jueng

entry.summary: Presents Q-Learning Lab, a browser-based bilingual teaching tool for tabular Q-learning that exposes live Bellman-substitution updates and logs each transition including exploration decisions. It aims to make reinforcement learning concrete for undergraduates.

entry.title: Unsupervised Detection of Entry and Exit Regions from Vehicle Trajectories for Camera-Agnostic Turning Movement Counts

author.name: Parikshit Singh Rathore, Vishwajeet Pattanaik, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: An unsupervised pipeline identifies intersection entry and exit regions directly from raw vehicle trajectories for camera-agnostic turning movement counts, requiring no manual annotation or calibration. It clusters initial and terminal points into persistent region polygons that classify future trajectories.

entry.title: RTFVE: Realtime Face Video Enhancement

author.name: Varun Ramesh Jois, Antonella DiLillo, James Storer

entry.summary: RTFVE is a realtime face video enhancement model designed to improve perceptual quality of low-bitrate video conferencing streams, runnable on ordinary CPUs and compatible with any decoder. It targets bandwidth-limited users without requiring specialized hardware.

entry.title: FSFVE: Few Shot Compressed Face Video Enhancement

author.name: Varun Ramesh Jois, Antonella DiLillo, James Storer

entry.summary: FSFVE enhances highly compressed video calls by rapidly training a per-instance model from as few as 10 face frames in under 100 seconds, either before or during a call. It requires no modification to the video conferencing application.

entry.title: CUST: Clustered Unit-level Similarity Transformer for Lightweight Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Jeongsoo Kim

entry.summary: CUST is a lightweight super-resolution transformer that lets each patch attend to similar patches at the unit level to integrate global and local information while avoiding the quadratic cost of full ViT attention. It aims to preserve long-range modeling that window-based attention sacrifices.

entry.title: Benchmarking Edge Inference Strategies for Deep Learning Models in Industrial Machine Vision

author.name: Miguel Gomez Fernandez, David Castro Boga, Roi Mendez-Rial, Eric Lopez-Lopez

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks four edge inference frameworks (PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, TensorRT) for industrial machine vision across multiple CPU and GPU platforms and both CNN and transformer models. It focuses on inference-time performance under realistic industrial deployment conditions.

entry.title: Active Noise Floor Estimation for Reliability-Optimal POMDPs: A Value-of-Noise-Information Approach

author.name: Hyung-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: Introduces a certificate-aware framework for actively estimating unknown sensing and execution noise in partially observed decision systems, defining a Value of Noise Information metric to quantify the reliability gap from miscalibrated noise estimates. It provides theoretical bounds tying model mismatch to certificate degradation.

entry.title: Incremental Transformer for Surrogate-Based Inverse Design of Geopolymer Mixtures

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione, Filippo Grassia

entry.summary: Proposes an Incremental Transformer surrogate framework for physics-constrained inverse design of geopolymer concrete mixtures, targeting compressive strength and carbon emissions from small, heterogeneous data. It combines dimensionality analysis, tabular surrogates, and constrained optimization for a niche materials-engineering task.

entry.title: Performance Benchmarking and Optimisation of Clustering Algorithms for Local and Non-Local Similarity Measure in Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Sisipho Hamlomo, Marcellin Atemkeng

entry.summary: Benchmarks five clustering methods (k-means variants, hierarchical, BIRCH) that exploit non-local self-similarity in medical images to identify structurally similar regions for adaptive compression. It targets storage and transmission burdens of high-resolution imaging while preserving diagnostically important local detail.

entry.title: From Non-Rigid to Rigid: Safe Acquisition of Rigid Communication Graphs under Limited Sensing

author.name: Saharsh, Vedhas Talnikar, Pushpak Jagtap

entry.summary: Provides a distributed optimization-based controller that achieves collision-free, rigid, time-varying communication graphs for heterogeneous multi-robot formations under limited sensing, without assuming an initially rigid graph. It guarantees rigidity via leader-follower quadratic optimization.

entry.title: Coordinated Incremental Trajectory Tracking of a Tailsitter Drone

author.name: Evangelos Ntouros, Ewoud J. J. Smeur

entry.summary: Derives an analytical differential flatness transform for a tailsitter UAV under coordinated flight using rotation matrices to avoid Euler-angle ambiguities, extending a state-of-the-art flatness-based controller to regimes with significant vertical velocity. Validated experimentally on challenging trajectories.

entry.title: Trajectory Planning and Certification for 3-DOF Robot Manipulators Using Real Quantifier Elimination Based on Comprehensive Gr\"obner Systems

author.name: Yu Nakai, Akira Terui, Masahiko Mikawa

entry.summary: Proposes trajectory planning and certification for 3-DOF manipulators using real quantifier elimination based on Comprehensive Grobner Systems, computing a parametric CGS once to avoid recomputing Grobner bases at every trajectory point. This yields efficient inverse-kinematics solving and formal solution certification.

entry.title: High-level spatial Dubins airplane-based reference smoothing with low-level geometric tracking for quadrotor control

author.name: Mogens Plessen

entry.summary: Presents a two-step quadrotor control method with high-level Dubins-airplane-based reference smoothing (via a small linear program) and low-level geometric tracking on the full quadrotor model, designed for tracking references with lateral path constraints such as obstacle contours. It reduces computational complexity through dimensionality reduction and decoupling.

entry.title: MIRA: A Modular Open-Source Micro-UAV for Indoor Research

author.name: Lucas K. de Oliveira, Felipe A. G. Tommaselli, Jo\~ao Aires Marsicano, Marco S. Tayar, Pedro A. R. Saraiva, Ricardo V. Godoy, Marcelo Becker

entry.summary: Introduces MIRA, a low-cost open-source micro-UAV with a 3D-printed airframe and containerized low-level software for indoor robotics research. It targets labs that need full white-box access to airframe, electronics, and control code that off-the-shelf drones do not expose.

entry.title: Robust Subgroup Analysis for Heterogeneous Censored Data

author.name: Zhaohui Xu, Daoji Li, Zemin Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes a robust subgroup analysis method for censored survival data under heterogeneous accelerated failure time models, combining inverse probability weighting, M-estimation, and concave pairwise fusion penalization. It simultaneously identifies subgroups and estimates covariate effects in heterogeneous populations.

entry.title: From Checker to Forecaster: Code-Owned Evaluation of Model-Generated Strategic Routes Under Delayed Ground Truth

author.name: Aleh Manchuliantsau

entry.summary: Studies model-output evaluation when ground truth is delayed, censored, or private, proposing RouteCast to issue code-owned provisional forecasts for model-generated strategic routes. Validated on a small retrospective venture pilot of 21 cases.

entry.title: Improved Answer Selection with Pre-Trained Word Embeddings

author.name: Rishav Chakravarti, Jiri Navratil, Cicero Nogueira dos Santos

entry.summary: A 2017 paper evaluating answer-selection methods that combine pre-trained word embeddings with learning-to-rank, showing gains over term-frequency baselines and near parity with neural models of the time. It is a historical IBM Research contribution on semantic matching for QA.

entry.title: DDR-Net: Haze-Aware Dual-Domain Refinement for Single-Image Dehazing

author.name: Xinye Zheng, Ye Yu, Qiang Lu, Jinsheng Luo, Yiran Cui, Yongbin Cheng

entry.summary: DDR-Net is a dual-domain refinement network for single-image dehazing built on a haze prior extractor, detail-enhanced blocks, and improved bottleneck feature refinement. It aims to address weak local structural representation and insufficient bottleneck refinement in encoder-decoder dehazing networks.

entry.title: SISA-Rec: A Semantically Integrated Sequential Recommender with Contrastive Alignment

author.name: Soohan Abbasi, Shahid Munir Shah, Rafia Shaikh, Mahmoud Aljawarneh

entry.summary: SISA-Rec is a transformer-based sequential recommender that fuses item-ID embeddings with BERT text embeddings via a gated fusion module and injects semantic similarity into self-attention with contrastive alignment. It targets sparse and cold-start scenarios where interaction data is limited.

entry.title: A Nearable Soft Mat Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing for Physiological Monitoring

author.name: Vincenzo Lavorgna, Martina Pulcinelli, Andrea Polimadei, Rosaria D Amato, Carlo Massaroni, Michele Arturo Caponero, Emiliano Schena, Daniela Lo Presti

entry.summary: This study presents a soft mat based on distributed optical fiber sensing using optical frequency domain reflectometry for spatially resolved physiological monitoring. It explores an underused biomedical sensing interface that is flexible, conformable, and immune to electromagnetic interference.

entry.title: MicroCharNet: Less is More for License Plate Character Detection

author.name: Huy Che, Dinh-Duy Phan, Duc-Lung Vu

entry.summary: MicroCharNet is an ultra-lightweight license plate character detection model using a compact C2f-block backbone with a coordinate attention module to preserve spatial information for real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices. It targets high accuracy with minimal computational overhead.

entry.title: Robotic Contextual Awareness for Human-Robot Collaboration and Environmental Understanding

author.name: Federico Rollo

entry.summary: A doctoral thesis on giving mobile robots contextual awareness for human-centric environments through spatial and object/actor recognition to enable adaptive behavior and interaction. Positions perception as prerequisite for safe autonomous operation.

entry.title: Casting Everything to Online API Services? A Survey of Integrating Localized Speech Recognition Models in Robotic Systems

author.name: Sheng Li, Jing Li, Felix Schijve, Jun Hu, Emilia Barakova

entry.summary: A survey reviewing how automatic speech recognition, including deep-learning models like Whisper, is integrated into robotic systems, covering model families, datasets, toolkits, and deployment strategies. It questions the default reliance on online API services versus localized on-device recognition.

entry.title: Machine Learning-based Correlation of Charpy Impact Properties Between Sub-sized and Standard-sized Specimens for Nuclear Structural Materials

author.name: Yugandhar Kasala Sreenivasulu, Isshu Lee, John W. Merickel, Fei Xu, Yalei Tang, Joshua E. Rittenhouse, Aleksandar Vakanski, Rongjie Song

entry.summary: Proposes a machine-learning framework to correlate Charpy impact properties between sub-sized and standard specimens for nuclear structural materials, aiming to improve on limited analytical conversion methods. It targets structural-integrity assessment where specimen size is constrained.

entry.title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Network Problems by Supported Non-dominated Points

author.name: David K\"onen, Lara L\"ohken, Michael Stiglmayr

entry.summary: Analyzes representations of the non-dominated set in multi-objective network optimization, showing that supported non-dominated points give higher-quality representations than extreme points for capacitated network problems as arc capacities grow. It addresses practical needs for compact solution sets.

entry.title: SEAMLiS: Visibility-Aware Safety for Perception-Limited Multi-Robot Exploration

author.name: Taekyung Kim, Rahul H Kumar, Aswin D. Menon, Tzu-Hsiang Lin, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.09959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous exploration in unknown environments is typically driven by informative frontiers, viewpoints, or trajectories, while local safety controller...

entry.title: Interleaved POMDP Planning for Multi-Object Search in Unknown Multi-Room Household Environments

author.name: Ruochu Yang, Ziyi Xia, Huibo Zhang, Yatong Han, Yiming Zhao, Yingke Li, Fumin Zhang, Yorai Wardi, Mengxue Hou

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.10437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-object search in unknown household environments requires planning under extensive uncertainty - from unknown object locations to cluttered spaces...

entry.title: The LLM Revolution (so far)

author.name: Eigenbraid

entry.summary: A survey-style post documenting the current breadth of LLM capabilities across domains, from image generation and translation to customer service, intended to raise the sanity waterline about how far the technology has advanced. It aggregates illustrative examples rather than presenting new findings.

entry.title: How MIT students are helping to prevent cyberattacks

author.name: Nicole Estvanik Taylor | Department of Urban Studies and Planning

entry.summary: An MIT News feature on the MIT Cybersecurity Clinic, where students provide pro-bono vulnerability assessments to at-risk municipalities and public agencies while training on real ransomware case studies like Baltimore. It highlights education and community service rather than new AI methods.

entry.title: Starting The Sequences: Some brief notes from the preface and the introduction

author.name: manueldelrio

entry.summary: Brief personal reading notes on the preface and introduction of the rationality collection From AI to Zombies, summarizing the author's stated mistakes and the intended purpose of teaching rational belief and decision-making. It is an introspective study log rather than research.

entry.title: LLMOSES

author.name: Davey Morse

entry.summary: A creative literary piece written with GPT-5.5 that reimagines the Moses tablet story with a binary-encoded tablet delivered to LLMs. It is an artistic parable rather than a research or analysis piece.

entry.title: The Whitney Biennial Should Admit That Emilie Gossiaux Wants to Fuck Their Dog

author.name: jenn

entry.summary: An art-criticism blog post analyzing a Whitney Biennial exhibit by a disabled artist and criticizing curators and critics for not confronting its provocative subject matter directly. It has no connection to AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 13, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights emphasize generative pretraining, representation-learning theory, and AI safety, with strong contributions from top labs.

  • GenCeption (He, Zisserman, Carreira, Sminchisescu) argues large-scale text-to-video generation is a general-purpose vision pretraining paradigm
  • A Google digital 'primordial soup' shows self-replication and math problem-solving co-evolving from random Z80 assembly programs
  • GPFlow enables variable-length protein design via an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson flow
  • RL from Hindsight (Pentland) brings hindsight relabeling to vision-language-action post-training for robots

On theory and efficiency, exact analytic solutions describe how linear concept directions emerge during training (abstraction dynamics, Saxe). COBS recasts block-sparse attention as ranking blocks by attention mass, while Meta diagnoses systematic cross-task correlation errors in multi-task Bayesian optimization.

Safety and alignment research is prominent:

  • Emergent Mirage challenges the robustness of emergent misalignment and its rapid reversibility
  • Deceptive grounding exposes clinical RAG outputs that pass faithfulness and citation checks yet misattribute entities
  • A new method measures model 'research taste' to test whether frontier models can autocomplete safety research

  • GenCeption (He, Zisserman, Carreira, Sminchisescu) argues large-scale text-to-video generation is a general-purpose vision pretraining paradigm
  • A Google digital 'primordial soup' shows self-replication and math problem-solving co-evolving from random Z80 assembly programs
  • GPFlow enables variable-length protein design via an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson flow
  • RL from Hindsight (Pentland) brings hindsight relabeling to vision-language-action post-training for robots

On theory and efficiency, exact analytic solutions describe how linear concept directions emerge during training (abstraction dynamics, Saxe). COBS recasts block-sparse attention as ranking blocks by attention mass, while Meta diagnoses systematic cross-task correlation errors in multi-task Bayesian optimization.

Safety and alignment research is prominent:

  • Emergent Mirage challenges the robustness of emergent misalignment and its rapid reversibility
  • Deceptive grounding exposes clinical RAG outputs that pass faithfulness and citation checks yet misattribute entities
  • A new method measures model 'research taste' to test whether frontier models can autocomplete safety research

entry.title: Video Generation Models are General-Purpose Vision Learners

author.name: Letian Wang, Chuhan Zhang, Rishabh Kabra, Jasper Uijlings, Steven Waslander, Andrew Zisserman, Joao Carreira, Kaiming He, Misha Andriluka, Eduard Gabriel Bazavan, Andrei Zanfir and Cristian Sminchisescu

entry.summary: GenCeption argues that large-scale text-to-video generation is a strong pretraining paradigm for general vision, repurposing a pretrained video diffusion backbone into a feed-forward, text-steerable perception model across diverse tasks. It reports state-of-the-art results and positions video generation as vision's equivalent of NLP next-token pretraining.

entry.title: Co-evolution of self-replication and function in a digital primordial soup

author.name: Francesco Cicala, Eyvind Niklasson, Ettore Randazzo, Sami Boukortt, Alessio Basti, Mayalen Etcheverry, Rif A. Saurous, Ben Laurie, James Manyika, Blaise Aguera-Arcas, Blake Richards

entry.summary: Starting from random 32-byte Z80 assembly programs, this study shows that self-replication and mathematical problem-solving can co-evolve spontaneously in a digital primordial soup through random mutations and program interactions. A task-based validation step couples reproduction success to computing polynomials correctly.

entry.title: Learning More from Less: Reinforcement Learning from Hindsight

author.name: Iris Xu, Sunshine Jiang, John Marangola, Nitish Dashora, Richard Li, Thomas Liu, Zexue He, Yuheng Zhi, Alex Pentland, Pulkit Agrawal, and Zhang-Wei Hong

entry.summary: Learning from Hindsight brings hindsight relabeling to RL post-training of vision-language-action models, using a vision-language model to rescore failed robot rollouts against the tasks they actually accomplished. This turns wasted sparse-reward failures into useful learning signal, improving sample efficiency.

entry.title: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?

author.name: Abhinav Rao, Liancheng Gong, Bin Hu, Atharva Naik

entry.summary: This paper critically re-examines emergent misalignment and its rapid reversibility, finding that both effects are highly sensitive to superficial factors like response length and largely vanish after controlling for them. It challenges previously reported mechanistic signatures of misalignment phase transitions.

entry.title: How are linear representations learned? Exact solutions to the dynamics of abstraction

author.name: William W. Yang, Andrew M. Saxe, Peter E. Latham

entry.summary: Derives exact solutions for how linear concept directions emerge during training in a minimal linear network, a process termed abstraction, illuminating the dynamics behind the linear representation hypothesis. It grounds interpretability and steering methods in analytic learning dynamics.

entry.title: Variable-Length Generative Protein Design via Generalized Poisson Flow

author.name: Chaoran Cheng, Zhanghan Ni, Yanru Qu, Yuxin Chen, Ruihan Guo, Jiajun Fan, Ge Liu

entry.summary: GPFlow is a variable-length generative framework for protein design that learns the rate function of an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson process, removing the need to fix protein length before sampling. It provides likelihood-based guarantees and a KL bound between data and generated distributions.

entry.title: COBS: Cumulant Order Block Sparse Attention

author.name: Alexander Tian, Aditya Ghai, Sanjit Neelam, Zaal Vasania, Akshay Mishra

entry.summary: COBS analyzes block-sparse attention by reducing block selection to ranking by attention mass and shows that retrieving highest-mass blocks can match dense attention quality. Using DeepSeek Native Sparse Attention as a case study, it isolates the selection stage as the key lever for efficient long-context inference.

entry.title: Pitfalls and Remedies for Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Carl Hvarfner, Sam Daulton, Max Balandat, Eytan Bakshy

entry.summary: This paper shows that the standard multi-task Gaussian process surrogate systematically misestimates cross-task correlation even for simple affinely related tasks, tracing failures to per-task standardization and slow correlation identification. It proposes remedies for warm-starting Bayesian optimization from related tasks.

entry.title: RaMark: Radioactive Watermarking for Generated Tabular Data

author.name: Xin Che, Lingyang Chu, Qiqi Zhang, Xinyu Ma, Xuan Luo, Jian Pei

entry.summary: RaMark introduces radioactive watermarking for synthetic tabular data by embedding a sinusoidal dependency into the data distribution so the mark survives adversarial retraining of generative models. It addresses ownership verification that current watermarks fail to preserve after retraining.

entry.title: Achieving Almost Exact Recovery in Almost Quadratic Time: Rank-Based Graph Matching via Local Tree Correlation Tests

author.name: Jiale Cheng, Ziao Wang, Lei Ying

entry.summary: This paper gives the first almost-quadratic-time algorithm achieving almost exact recovery for correlated Erdos-Renyi graph matching in a sparse regime, using rank-based local tree correlation tests. It improves on prior results in that parameter regime.

entry.title: Understanding Schedule-Free Methods in Nonconvex Optimization: Rate Guarantees and Escaping Saddles

author.name: Jiseok Chae, Donghwan Kim

entry.summary: This paper provides worst-case convergence analyses of Schedule-Free gradient descent and its stochastic variant for smooth nonconvex objectives, using a Lyapunov analysis derived from the methods' continuous-time ODE and addressing saddle escape. It fills a gap in the theory behind an increasingly popular optimizer.

entry.title: Forget Narrowly, Retain Broadly: Unlearning as an Asymmetric Generalization Problem

author.name: Amit Peleg, Naman Deep Singh, Naama Pearl, Bibhabasu Mohapatra, Matthias Hein

entry.summary: This paper reframes LLM machine unlearning as an asymmetric generalization problem, identifying under-forgetting (knowledge resurfacing under paraphrases) and over-forgetting (damage to unrelated knowledge) as failures existing benchmarks miss. It argues forget evaluation must cover diverse query formulations while retain evaluation must probe an implicitly vast disjoint set.

entry.title: Mach-Mind-4-Flash Technical Report

author.name: Foundation Model Team (Li Auto Inc)

entry.summary: Mach-Mind-4-Flash is a 35B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts agentic model with 3B active parameters from Li Auto that reportedly matches or exceeds 100B-class models through post-training alone, using scalable agentic RL environments. Its pipeline features a unified RL/OPD infrastructure with multi-teacher scheduling and parallel domain-specific RL experts fused into one model.

entry.title: Can Frontier Models Autocomplete Safety Research?

author.name: dani roytburg

entry.summary: This post proposes a method to measure the research taste of language models by masking parts of published papers, sampling model-generated experiment extensions, and checking how many held-out claims are recovered. It finds that variance across papers is larger than across models, and that a frontier model (Fable) does not clearly beat a smaller model (Sonnet) at a 64-proposal budget, suggesting predictiveness could define a lasting human advantage in safety research.

entry.title: On Locality and Length Generalization in Visual Reasoning

author.name: Pulkit Madan, Sanjay Haresh, Reza Ebrahimi, Sunny Panchal, Apratim Bhattacharyya, Roland Memisevic

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether local, sequential (foveated) vision models offer computational benefits over global single-shot models, studying visual state tracking and length generalization. It draws on length-generalization insights from language models to probe fundamental properties of biologically inspired vision.

entry.title: Causally Debiased Latent Action Model for Embodied Action Conditioned World Models

author.name: Yufan Wei, Kun Zhou, Lingjun Mao, Zijun Zhang, Ziming Xu, Ziqiao Xi, Shuang Liang, Ruobing Han, Yuchen Yan, Xinyue Wang, Fan Feng, and Biwei Huang

entry.summary: This paper identifies action-irrelevant bias as a key obstacle in latent action models for action-conditioned world models, where reconstruction-only training entangles action dynamics with backgrounds, and introduces causally debiased learning with metrics to measure latent-action bias. It aims for more controllable embodied world models from unlabeled video.

entry.title: Deceptive Grounding: Entity Attribution Failure in Clinical Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Cedric Caruzzo, Donggeun Yoo, Tae Soo Kim

entry.summary: This paper identifies deceptive grounding in clinical retrieval-augmented generation, where a response passes faithfulness, hallucination, and citation checks yet attributes one drug's evidence to a different queried drug. Across 13 models it finds deceptive-grounding rates of 8-87%, with medical fine-tuned models reaching up to 87%.

entry.title: Prompt-Driven Exploration

author.name: Sunshine Jiang, John Marangola, David Zhang, Raghuram Kowdeed, Ruiyang Luo, Nitish Dashora, Richard Li, Pulkit Agrawal, Zhang-Wei Hong

entry.summary: Prompt-Driven Exploration improves RL exploration for language-conditioned policies by refining prompts from rollouts, since prompt changes induce global behavior changes that action-space noise cannot. A vision-language model reasons over rollouts to propose useful prompts under sparse reward.

entry.title: Optimizing Against Safety Representations: Activation-Guided Adversarial Suffixes and the Geometry of Refusal

author.name: Ege \c{C}akar, Hannah Guan, Kayden Kehe

entry.summary: Studies adversarial suffix attacks that optimize directly against a model internal refusal direction rather than output-based objectives, finding that globally suppressing refusal across all layers is more effective than targeting a single layer-position. It suggests safety representations are distributed across the forward pass.

entry.title: ARCANA: A Reflective Multi-Agent Program Synthesis Framework for ARC-AGI-2 Reasoning

author.name: Kunbo Zhang, Lei Fu, Zeyu Wang, Zijing Liu, Kejian Tong

entry.summary: ARCANA is a reflective multi-agent program-synthesis framework for ARC-AGI-2 tasks that combines perception, DSL program proposal, symbolic verification, and failure-driven refinement through a shared blackboard. It targets abstract reasoning under tight test-time and hardware constraints.

entry.title: Solving Stochastic Fixed-Point Equations with High Probability

author.name: Jelena Diakonikolas

entry.summary: This paper introduces VR-GHAL, a variance-reduced gradual Halpern method for solving stochastic fixed-point equations with high probability over smoothable Banach spaces, using a recursive estimator based on clipped oracle differences. It provides high-probability convergence guarantees for nonexpansive and contractive operators.

entry.title: KV-PRM: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via KV-Cache Transfer for Multi-Agent Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Peng Kuang, Haibo Jin, Xiaoyu Han, Yanli Wang, Xiaopeng Yuan, Ye Yu, Kaidi Xu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: KV-PRM is an efficient process reward model that scores multi-agent trajectories by reading the KV cache produced during generation rather than re-encoding trajectory text from scratch, using a single verify token. This removes the quadratic re-encoding bottleneck limiting PRMs in long-context test-time scaling.

entry.title: Present but Rescaled: Chat-to-Agent Transfer of Additive Activation Steering

author.name: Lucas Pinto

entry.summary: This single-author study is the first systematic examination of transferring additive activation steering from single-turn chat calibration to tool-using ReAct agents, using matched-information designs and norm-matched random controls. It finds transfer is real but rescaled, with the injected direction reaching late layers at near-full strength yet dissociating from behavioral effect.

entry.title: A Sovereign, Open-Source Foundation Model for German and English

author.name: The Soofi-Team: Benedikt Droste, David Fitzek, Ruben H\"arle, Lukas Helff, Maximilian Idahl, Alex Jude, Abbas Goher Khan, Maurice Kraus, Timm Ruland, Richard Rutmann, Sebastian Sztwiertnia, Markus Frey, Daniil Gurgurov, Jan Pfister, Tom R\"ohr, Sebastian von Rohrscheidt, J\"org Bienert, Nicolas Flores-Herr, Simon Gottschalk, Andreas Hotho, Kristian Kersting, Joachim K\"ohler, Alexander L\"oser, Wolfgang Nejdl, Simon Ostermann, Jan Plogsties, Patrick Putzky, Mehdi Ali, Michael Fromm, Max L\"ubbering

entry.summary: Soofi S 30B-A3B is a sovereign open-source Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Transformer for German and English that activates 3B of 30B parameters per token and keeps inference cache near-constant with growing context. Pretrained on about 27 trillion tokens with up-weighted German, it matches dense 14-27B models and leads European sovereign baselines and open models on several aggregates.

entry.title: STITCH-OPE: Trajectory Stitching with Guided Diffusion for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Hossein Goli, Michael Gimelfarb, Nathan Samuel de Lara, Haruki Nishimura, Masha Itkina, Florian Shkurti

entry.summary: STITCH-OPE uses guided denoising diffusion to stitch synthetic target-policy trajectories for long-horizon, high-dimensional off-policy evaluation, avoiding variance blow-ups from importance weighting. It targets domains like robotics and healthcare where online interaction is costly.

entry.title: A Shared Geometry of Difficulty in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Stefano Civelli, Pietro Bernardelle, Nicol\`o Brunello, Gianluca Demartini

entry.summary: Studies how problem-difficulty signals are encoded across layers of multilingual LLMs using linear probes on the AMC benchmark translated into 21 languages. It finds shallow layers carry cross-lingual difficulty signals while deep layers are language-specific.

entry.title: Penny Wise, Pixel Foolish: Bypassing Price Constraints in Multimodal Agents via Visual Adversarial Perturbations

author.name: Jiachen Qian and Zhaolu Kang

entry.summary: Identifies Visual Dominance Hallucination in multimodal mobile agents, where imperceptible visual perturbations override textual price evidence and cause irrational financial decisions. The white-box PriceBlind attack achieves around 80 percent success on a shopping benchmark.

entry.title: TheBioCollection: Unified Pre-Training Scale LLM Corpus for Biology

author.name: Hyunjin Seo, Hyeon Hwang, Gyubok Lee, Jay Shin, Jimin Park, Taesoo Kim, Sanghoon Lee, Hongjoon Ahn, Sungjun Han, Sangwon Jung

entry.summary: TheBioCollection unifies scattered biological resources across molecules, proteins, genomes, cells, and pathways into a 52.6B-token pretraining corpus, enriched with tool-computed properties and instruction data for biology LLMs. It aims to give models genuine biological grounding.

entry.title: Sensitivity-Aware Thresholding and Token Routing for Activation Sparsification in Large Language Models

author.name: Bishmoy Paul, Youngmin Yi, Hoeseok Yang

entry.summary: SATS calibrates layerwise MLP activation-sparsity thresholds using an output-sensitivity proxy rather than raw activation percentiles, and adds lightweight token routing to skip computation adaptively. The goal is faster LLM inference with minimal quality loss.

entry.title: Correlation-Aware Contextual Bandits with Surrogate Rewards for LLM Routing

author.name: Ajay Narayanan Sridhar, Ronak Singh, Mehrdad Mahdavi, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan

entry.summary: This paper studies contextual bandits with correlated arms and noisy surrogate reward signals, proposing coupled and decoupled reward-mixing algorithms motivated by LLM routing. It provides a way to exploit auxiliary model predictions while remaining robust when they are unreliable.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Adaptive Inter-layer Composition for Efficient Heterogeneous Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuncheng Yang, Feiyang Ye, Shixian Luo, Yinna Zhu, Lianlei Shan, Wangcai Zhao, Kuo Zhang, Yan Chen, Yong Wu, Yan Xie

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a hardware-aware multi-objective search that automatically converts homogeneous transformers into heterogeneous vision-language models mixing linear, sparse, and low-rank operators. It replaces handcrafted static mixing with learned architecture composition to improve the accuracy-latency trade-off.
