entry.title: Attention to Detail: Evaluating Energy, Performance, and Accuracy Trade-offs Across vLLM Configurations

author.name: Nada Zine, Tristan Coignion, Vincenzo Stoico, Cl\'ement Quinton, Romain Rouvoy, Patricia Lago

entry.summary: This large-scale controlled study measures how three vLLM inference-engine configurations (attention kernel, prefix caching, chunked prefill) affect energy, latency, and output quality across five open-weight LLMs and five tasks, totaling thousands of runs. It quantifies an often-overlooked deployment lever beyond model architecture and hardware.

entry.title: Toward Auditable AI Scientists: A Hypothesis Evolution Protocol for LLM Agents

author.name: Izumi Takahara, Teruyasu Mizoguchi

entry.summary: The Hypothesis Evolution Protocol makes an LLM agent's scientific reasoning auditable by turning hypothesis generation, evaluation, and revision into explicit, logged operations rather than burying them in unstructured logs. Demonstrated on materials-science tasks, it aims at transparency and human oversight of autonomous AI scientists.

entry.title: OpenProver: Agentic and Interactive Theorem Proving with Lean 4

author.name: Mat\v{e}j Kripner, Milan Straka

entry.summary: OpenProver is an open-source LLM-driven automated theorem proving system integrated with Lean 4 formal verification, using a Planner-Worker-Verifier architecture with a scratchpad and repository of intermediate findings. It supports reproducible evaluation and interactive human-guided proof search.

entry.title: Geopolitical alignment: Endorsement effects in large language models

author.name: Maxim Chupilkin

entry.summary: This endorsement experiment tests whether LLMs' policy judgments are shaped by which country is described as supporting a policy, finding GPT-5, Claude Sonnet, and Gemini rate China- and Russia-endorsed policies lower than identical US/EU-endorsed ones, with DeepSeek an exception. It probes how geopolitical cues bias model evaluations.

entry.title: A Survey on the Green Development of Large Models: From Resource-Efficient Architectures to Hardware-Software Co-Design

author.name: Linhui Xiao, Guiping Cao, Mingyue Guo, Xianchao Guan, Fan Yang, Ming Tao, Xin Li, Yuxin Peng, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: This survey reviews green development of large models spanning resource-efficient architectures, sparsification, parameter-efficient tuning, and full-stack hardware-software co-design. It synthesizes algorithmic and systems-level approaches to reducing AI's energy and environmental cost.

entry.title: Beyond Metadata: CAPRA for Hidden Subgroup Analysis under Missing Metadata in Medical Imaging

author.name: Yawen Li, Yan Li, Zhe Xue, Yingxia Shao, Meiyu Liang, Guanhua Ye

entry.summary: CAPRA enables hidden subgroup auditing of medical imaging models when demographic and acquisition metadata are missing, by predicting image-derived semantic axes and calibrating them on a small labeled split via patient-level cross-fitting. It supports failure analysis and robust learning without deployment-time subgroup labels.

entry.title: IB-Flow: Information Bottleneck-Guided CFG Distillation for Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Yiting Wang, Jingyi Zhang, Wenhu Zhang, Ke Chao, Yves Liang, Kun Cheng, Kang Zhao

entry.summary: IB-Flow uses an information-bottleneck view to make classifier-free-guidance distillation for few-step text-to-image generation state-aware, adapting guidance strength and supervisor timestep to the progressive entropy reduction of generation. It replaces static, blind guidance injection to improve few-step quality.

entry.title: BeyondSight: Object Permanence for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Sandro Papais, Letian Wang, Mudit Jain, Behnaz Rezaei, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: BeyondSight is a permanence-aware end-to-end driving framework that decouples actor existence from instantaneous observability by propagating persistent actor queries through prolonged occlusions. This keeps critical occluded agents in the prediction and planning pipeline rather than letting them disappear.

entry.title: MedRealMM: A Real-World Multimodal Benchmark for Chinese Online Medical Consultation

author.name: Runhan Shi and Quan Zhou and Yuqian Xu and Shuai Yang and Xin Wu and Zitong Zhou and Hui Liu and Bin Cha and Zheming Wang and Liya Li and Wei Wei and Haoyuan Hu and Jun Xu

entry.summary: MedRealMM is a large-scale multimodal benchmark built from de-identified real Chinese online patient-doctor consultations, using a clinical challenge-point extraction framework to isolate demanding moments including patient-uploaded images. It aims to better align medical LLM evaluation with authentic clinical practice.

entry.title: Scoped Verification for Reliable Long-Horizon Agentic Context Evolution under Distribution Shift

author.name: Dan C. Hsu, Luke Lu

entry.summary: GRACE maintains an LLM agent's persistent system-level instructions as a typed semantic graph and validates proposed updates within local typed neighborhoods before reconstructing them into textual instruction checkpoints. It aims to keep long-horizon agentic context evolution verifiable under distribution shift.

entry.title: TactiDex: A Real-World Tactile-Guided Benchmark for Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Suting Ni, Hanbing Zhang, Zhenyu Wei, Guo Chen, Chixuan Zhang, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: TactiDex is a real-world tactile-guided benchmark for dexterous manipulation that aligns whole-hand tactile signals with multi-granularity kinematic and object states, aiming to move human-to-robot transfer beyond kinematic mimicry toward contact-level human-likeness. It provides a dataset and standardized evaluation metrics.

entry.title: GenVid2Robot: From Video Generation to Robot Manipulation via Rigid-Geometric Consistency

author.name: Haohui Huang, Xi Yuan, Panpan Liao, Tao Teng, Chenguang Yang, Jing Guo, Yi Guo

entry.summary: GenVid2Robot converts generated video motion into executable robot trajectories via a rigid-geometric consistency framework that samples semantic anchors from the real first frame, tracks them through generated candidates, and verifies feasibility against first-frame RGB-D geometry. It bridges visually plausible but physically ungrounded generated video and real manipulation.

entry.title: WILDTRACE: Benchmarking Natural Evidence Trails in Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Zixin Chen, Peng Liu, Haobo Li, Rui Sheng, Jianhong Tu, Xiaodong Deng, Fei Huang, Kashun Shum, Dayiheng Liu, Huamin Qu

entry.summary: WILDTRACE is a long-context benchmark focused on source-internal evidence integration, where answering requires combining evidence naturally dispersed across distant passages rather than artificially planted needles or reverse-engineered multi-hop chains. It aims to test genuine long-document reasoning.

entry.title: Signed Symmetric Quantization for Few-Bit Integers

author.name: Ian Colbert, Eashan Dash, Pablo Monteagudo-Lago, Juan Amboage, Srinidhi N, Giuseppe Franco, Nicholas J. Fraser, Arun Ramachandran

entry.summary: Observes that signed integers have one extra negative value and shows standard symmetric quantizers waste it, forcing positive-outlier clipping that is a real error source at few-bit precision. It proposes a signed symmetric scheme retaining symmetric-format speed while reducing clipping.

entry.title: EHR-MPC: Inference-Time Control for Sepsis Treatment with Generative Patient Digital Twins

author.name: Joshua Pickard, Wei Qi, Na Li, Ann Woolley, Lisa Cosimi, Roy Kishony, Deborah Hung

entry.summary: EHR-MPC trains a generative EHR patient digital twin and uses model predictive control at inference to optimize sepsis treatment, decoupling dynamics learning from policy optimization for adaptability to changing clinical objectives. It is evaluated on a multicenter ICU cohort across eight hospitals.

entry.title: FlowDAgger: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptation of Generative Robot Policies in Latent Space

author.name: Michael Murray, Daphne Chen, Simran Bagaria, Dean Fortier, Tess Hellebrekers, Galen Mullins, Harshavardhan Gajarla, Oier Mees, Maya Cakmak, Andrey Kolobov

entry.summary: FlowDAgger adapts frozen flow-matching and diffusion robot policies from human interventions in latent space by inverting each expert action to the noise that would have produced it under the base policy. This enables sample- and compute-efficient correction without large data collection or online RL on hardware.

entry.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading

author.name: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Ruhan Wang, Junyao Yang, Zhichao Liu, Xiyang Wu, Anhao Li, Yue Yu, Ninghao Liu, Lichao Sun, Haotao Mi, LeoweiLiang

entry.summary: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench introduces 46 long-horizon terminal tasks across nine categories with dense subtask-level graded rewards, capturing intermediate progress that outcome-only benchmarks miss. It targets a more complete picture of agent capability on multi-hour tasks.

entry.title: Group Invariant Spectral Embedding

author.name: Yeari Vigder, Paulina Hoyos, David Thong, Joakim and\'en, Joe Kileel, and Amit Moscovich

entry.summary: This work incorporates group symmetries directly into affinity kernels for spectral embedding, proving convergence of graph Laplacians to differential operators on quotient spaces for data with Lie group invariances. It offers a principled way to make dimensionality reduction respect rotational or other structural symmetries.

entry.title: Event Stream based Multi-Modal Video Anomaly Detection: A Benchmark Dataset and Algorithms

author.name: Peipei Zhu, Yueqing Niu, Lin Zhu, Guanchong Niu, Yang Yu, Zheng Li

entry.summary: EVAD is an event-enhanced video anomaly detection framework that fuses conventional video with event-camera streams for robustness under poor lighting and fast motion, accompanied by a large visible-event benchmark of billions of events and hundreds of thousands of frames. It provides motion-salient cues complementary to visible-light video.

entry.title: Super-Generalist: Towards Comprehensive and Accurate Medical Image Understanding via Generalist-Specialist Synergy

author.name: Shaoteng Zhang, Weiwei Cao, Wanxing Chang, Yutong Xie, Kai Cao, Zaiyi Liu, Yu Shi, Tingbo Liang, Qi Zhang, Ling Zhang, Yong Xia, Jianpeng Zhang

entry.summary: Super-Generalist (SuG) unifies generalist vision-language learning with specialist objectives for medical imaging, adding spatially grounded, specialist-enhanced vision-language alignment to gain both broad generalization and fine-grained diagnostic capability. It targets reliable, spatially interpretable diagnosis across diseases and anatomies.

entry.title: Visual Inception: Compromising Long-term Planning in Agentic Recommenders via Multimodal Memory Poisoning

author.name: Jiachen Qian

entry.summary: Uncovers Visual Inception, a memory-poisoning attack where triggers hidden in user-uploaded images act as sleeper agents inside agentic recommender long-term memory. When later retrieved, poisoned memories hijack the agent planning chain toward adversary goals without prompt injection.

entry.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models via Interactions

author.name: Qingzhuo Wang, Ruiyang Qin, Zhenxin Qin, Wen Shen, Zhihua Wei

entry.summary: Proposes a unified interaction-based explanation of why knowledge distillation works in LLMs, decomposing outputs into nonlinear feature interactions. It finds distillation commonly sparsifies interactions, with students retaining fewer while suppressing others.

entry.title: Sticky Routing: Training MoE Models for Memory-Efficient Inference

author.name: Ali Kayyam

entry.summary: StickyMoE adds a differentiable routing-consistency loss during pretraining that penalizes abrupt expert switches between adjacent tokens, reducing costly weight swapping on edge devices. It requires no architecture change and one hyperparameter, letting experts and routing co-adapt.

entry.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices

author.name: Tao Lu, Haoyu Wang, Zonghui Wang, Keshen Xiang, Jiaheng Zhang, Wenzhi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a GPU inference method for LLMs at moderate unstructured sparsity (around 50 percent) using a three-layer matrix storage format that lets sparse tensor cores beat dense counterparts. It addresses the long-standing failure of sparse kernels to accelerate at practical sparsity levels.

entry.title: Inside the Skill Market: From Software Engineering Activities to Reusable Agent Skills

author.name: Jialun Cao, Xinru Yan, Songqiang Chen, Yaojie Lu, Zhongxin Liu, Shing-Chi Cheung

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study characterizes what software-engineering activities are being packaged into reusable agent skills across emerging skill marketplaces and their coverage of the development lifecycle. It provides the first systematic map of SE-specific reusable skills.

entry.title: Probing Diffusion Denoising Dynamics for Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Yasong Dai, Zeeshan Hayder, David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: D3CL adapts a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model's denoising dynamics for discriminative representation learning by treating noisy latents at different timesteps as contrastive views of the same image. It couples a contrastive objective with denoising reconstruction under parameter-efficient updates.

entry.title: OmniMapBench: Benchmarking Visual-Centric Reasoning on Diverse Map Documents

author.name: Yang Chen and Yunwen Li and Yufan Shen and Minghao Liu and Tianyu Zheng and Bin Fu and Qunshu Lin and Zhi Yu and Botian Shi

entry.summary: OmniMapBench is a benchmark of over 2,000 annotated question-answer pairs on 1,603 diverse map documents to test genuinely visual-centric reasoning, plus a Visual Dependency Index measuring accuracy drop when images are removed. It targets a gap where many document benchmarks are solvable from text alone.

entry.title: GeoTrace: Geometry-Aware Trajectory Token Compression for Video Large Language Models

author.name: Guohuan Xie, Mengqi Lei, Chuan Shi, Wei Bao, Yue Gao, Siqi Li

entry.summary: GeoTrace is a training-free spatiotemporal token-compression framework for video LLMs that decomposes video into sparse skeleton tokens and traceable residual event tokens via farthest-point anchoring and trajectory-constrained condensation. It reduces visual token counts while avoiding ambiguous fused features.

entry.title: L-MAD: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Debate Structures in Legal Reasoning

author.name: Tan-Minh Nguyen, Hoang-Trung Nguyen, Huu-Dong Nguyen, Dinh-Truong Do, Thi-Hai-Yen Vuong, Le-Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: L-MAD systematically evaluates multi-agent debate structures and aggregation methods for legal textual entailment, finding persona-assigned agents improve over single-agent baselines by up to eight percent. It reveals that more agents help but more discussion rounds cause an over-deliberation drift that reinforces mistakes.

entry.title: Event Burst Trigger: An Availability Backdoor Attack on Event-Based SNN Object Detection

author.name: Jaesun Baek, Chanwook Lee and Eun-Kyu Lee

entry.summary: Event Burst Trigger is an availability backdoor attack on spiking-neural-network event-based object detectors that injects triggers producing temporally concentrated event bursts, inflating spurious candidates and post-processing cost. It exposes an under-studied vulnerability in edge SNN detection.

entry.title: 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Low-Overlap Captures

author.name: Minhyuk Hwang, Sangmin Kim, Seunguk Do, Daneul Kim and Jaesik Park

entry.summary: StudioRecon reconstructs 4D human scenes from sparse, low-overlap cameras by decoupling background and humans, densifying background supervision with camera-controlled diffusion-synthesized novel views. It reduces artifacts in under-observed regions compared with prior low-overlap methods.

entry.title: Glob3R: Global Structure-from-Motion with 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Junyuan Deng, Heng Li, Kejie Qiu, Lingteng Qiu, Rui Peng, Weichao Shen, Weihao Yuan, Siyu Zhu, Zilong Dong, Ping Tan

entry.summary: Glob3R performs global structure-from-motion by explicitly optimizing feed-forward 3D foundation-model predictions, augmenting a frozen Pi3X backbone with a lightweight dense matching head to produce reliable multi-view feature tracks. It aims to reduce drift when scaling reconstruction to long or unordered image sets.

entry.title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making

author.name: Yanzhen Chen, Zihan Xu, Xiaocheng Zhang, Zhiting Fan, Weiqi Zhai, Hongxia Xu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: LongMedBench is a real-world EHR-based benchmark for long-horizon clinical decision-making, built from MIMIC-IV records into time-series event streams and long-context memory datasets to enable multi-session agent-environment interaction. It covers 335 patients with roughly 20 inpatient visits each.

entry.title: STEEL: Sparsity-Aware Fused Attention for Energy-Efficient Long-Sequence Inference on AMD's XDNA NPU

author.name: Victor J.B. Jung, Gagandeep Singh, Joseph Melber, Kristof Denolf, Francesco Conti, Luca Benini

entry.summary: STEEL is the first open-source FlashAttention implementation targeting AMD XDNA-like NPUs, introducing a dataflow formulation of prefill attention with sparsity awareness for energy-efficient long-sequence inference on laptop-class SoCs. It addresses privacy and reliability concerns of cloud offloading for on-device agentic workloads.

entry.title: Self-Guided Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs

author.name: Xinyu Zhu, Zhe Xu, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Kaushik Rangadurai, Hua Zhi, Frank Shyu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon, Yu Meng, Xi Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes self-guided test-time training for long-context LLMs, adapting parameters on the specific test context but selecting only relevant spans rather than the whole context or random spans, which would be prohibitively expensive or noisy. It addresses accuracy degradation as input length grows.

entry.title: Hydra++: Real-Time Hierarchical 3D Scene Graph Construction With Object-Level Shape Estimation

author.name: Hyungtae Lim and Nathan Hughes and Xihang Yu and Ruihan Xu and Yun Chang and Jingnan Shi and Rajat Talak and Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Hydra++ integrates learning-based category-agnostic object shape estimation into a real-time hierarchical 3D scene graph pipeline, adding a reprojection-mask consistency check to reject degenerate predictions from partial observations. It provides instance-specific shape detail beyond coarse point clouds or class-level CAD templates.

entry.title: Reward Transport: Property Control in Flow Matching via Noise-Space Alignment

author.name: Kehan Guo, Yili Shen, Yujun Zhou, Yue Huang, Chujie Gao, Shiyi Du, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Reward Transport treats the noise-to-data coupling in flow matching as an alignment interface, using optimal transport at training time to align a scalar noise coordinate with molecular rewards. Varying that coordinate at inference steers generation without an oracle or reward model.

entry.title: Adaptive Bayes exactly tracks information over intrinsic time

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: Derives an exact information-accounting identity for Bayesian and multiplicative-weights updates, decomposing regret into a per-round uncertainty payment and reduction in information distance to a comparator. The cumulative payment defines an intrinsic-time uncertainty clock.

entry.title: SafeExplorer: An Unbiased Policy Gradient for Reinforcement Learning with Recovery Interventions

author.name: Elham Daneshmand, Majid Khadiv, Glen Berseth and Hsiu-Chin Lin

entry.summary: SafeExplorer modifies PPO to give an unbiased policy gradient when a separate recovery policy intervenes on physical robots, addressing the bias from mixed-policy rollouts that ill-defined importance sampling cannot fix. The goal is to minimize falls during real-robot training rather than trade them against return.

entry.title: BlockServe: Block-Grained Continuous Batching for High-Throughput Diffusion LLM Serving

author.name: Yuanjie Zhu, Liangwei Yang, Ke Xu, Weizhi Zhang, Shanghao Li, Zihe Song, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: BlockServe is a continuous batching framework for serving diffusion LLMs that evicts completed requests at block boundaries and uses mixed-state execution to handle heterogeneous batch convergence rates. It reports up to 10x throughput gains over prior diffusion-LLM serving.

entry.title: Phone Segmentation and Recognition through Phonological Activation Mapping

author.name: Shikhar Bharadwaj, Kwanghee Choi, Stephen McIntosh, Chin-Jou Li, Eunjung Yeo, Daisuke Saito, Nobuaki Minematsu, Shinji Watanabe, Jian Zhu, David Harwath, David R. Mortensen

entry.summary: SPAM maps self-supervised speech-model representations to phonological feature activations and adds lightweight, gradient-free heads for joint phone segmentation and recognition. It works from under a minute of transcriptions and generalizes to unseen phones.

entry.title: Dec-MARVEL: Decentralized Multi-Agent Exploration without Communication under Budget Constraints

author.name: Janghyun Cho, Jimmy Chiun, Guillaume Sartoretti and Changjoo Nam

entry.summary: Dec-MARVEL is a decentralized, communication-free multi-UAV exploration framework where robots coordinate purely through incidental sightings of teammates within their field of view, under travel-budget constraints. A graph-attention policy trained with phase-conditioned critics selects return-feasible actions.

entry.title: REBASE: Reference-Background Subspace Elimination for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Mantha Sai Gopal, Jaison Saji Chacko, Harsh Nandwana, Sandesh Hegde, Debarshi Banerjee, Uma Mahesh

entry.summary: REBASE is a training-free in-context segmentation method that suppresses spurious background correspondences by identifying and eliminating a low-rank shared-background feature subspace between reference and query images. It improves prompt localization for foundation-model plus SAM pipelines.

entry.title: DETRAM: End-to-end DEtection, Tracking and Recovery of HumAn Meshes

author.name: Chunggi Lee, Seonwook Park, Wanhua Li, Umar Iqbal, and Hanspeter Pfister

entry.summary: DETRAM is a unified transformer framework that jointly detects, reconstructs, and tracks multiple human meshes across video frames using persistent identity-consistent query embeddings, without a separate detection module. It supports both automatic and user-prompted tracking under occlusion.

entry.title: Beyond Time Shifts: Adapting Omni-LLM as a Reference-Free Evaluator for Generative Audio-Visual Models

author.name: Yijie Qian, Juncheng Wang, Chao Xu, Huihan Wang, Yuxiang Feng, Yang Liu, Baigui Sun, Yong Liu, Shujun Wang

entry.summary: This work adapts an omni-modal LLM into a reference-free evaluator of audio-visual synchronization for generative models, addressing structural hallucinations and asymmetric cross-modal relations that break standard temporal-alignment metrics. It distills relative human-style judgments into absolute scalar scores.

entry.title: AgentKGV: Agentic LLM-RAG Framework with Two-Stage Training for the Fact Verification of Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Yumin Heo, Hyeon-gu Lee, Sumin Seo, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: AgentKGV is an agentic LLM-RAG framework for knowledge-graph fact verification with dynamic routing and iterative query rewriting, plus two-stage training via distillation SFT and trajectory-level GRPO. It targets accurate, cost-efficient verification at industrial scale.

entry.title: Quantum Circuits in Diffusion Models: A Fair-Comparison Study and a Mechanistic Analysis of Angle-Embedding Failures

author.name: Jaeuk Kim, Sanghoon Yoo

entry.summary: This study integrates variational quantum circuits into diffusion models via a squeeze-and-excitation scaffold and finds, under fair role-matched and parameter-matched classical controls, no statistically significant quantum advantage on MNIST and CIFAR-10. It also mechanistically analyzes why angle embeddings fail.

entry.title: VTaMo: Video-Text Alignment Model for Sign Language Translation

author.name: Junyi Hu, Zhewen He, Haomian Huang, Aoxiang Yang, Yi Fang

entry.summary: VTaMo is a gloss-free sign-language translation framework introducing explicit multi-granularity video-text alignment via entropy-regularized optimal transport, a learnable orthogonal global calibration, and position-aligned contrastive learning. It reports consistent gains across four sign-language benchmarks.

entry.title: Weaving Light and Time: Unified Harmonic-Geometric Representation Learning for Dense RGB-Event Parsing

author.name: Chenxu Peng, Chongtian zhou, Dicheng Liu, Bo-Wen Yin, Yimian Dai, Xialei Liu, Ming-Ming Cheng, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Evita is a unified backbone for dense RGB-event scene parsing that explicitly resolves geometric parallax and cross-spectral aliasing between dense intensity frames and sparse event spikes via a harmonic-geometric representation. It avoids the doubled cost of decoupled dual encoders.

entry.title: COAST: Context-Aware Differential Learning for Gene Expression Prediction in Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Keunho Byeon, Sunhong Park, Jeewoo Lim, Jin Tae Kwak

entry.summary: COAST predicts spatial gene expression from H&E histopathology images using context-aware differential learning that jointly models absolute expression and signed relative differences between spots via type-specific modulation and a transformer encoder. It explicitly leverages relative expression relationships that prior methods ignore.

entry.title: Interference and Retention in Continual Learning

author.name: Julius St\"ork

entry.summary: This paper reframes catastrophic forgetting in continual learning as direct interference energy between tasks, showing forgetting is structurally avoidable when task supports are disjoint but has an unavoidable floor under conflicting overlap. It derives an interference-gated allocation method and links the same geometry to model merging.

entry.title: REFORGE: A Method for Benchmarking LLMs' Reverse Engineering Capabilities in Decompiled Binary Function Naming

author.name: Nicolas Koller and Andreas u. Schmidt

entry.summary: REFORGE argues that fair evaluation of LLM binary reverse-engineering is bottlenecked by unreliable binary-to-source alignment under compiler optimization, not model capability. It provides a provenance-tracked pipeline to build trustworthy function-level ground truth for decompiled function naming.

entry.title: Interval Certifications for Multilayered Perceptrons via Lattice Traversal

author.name: Merkouris Papamichail and Konstantinos Varsos and Giorgos Flouris and Jo\~ao Marques-Silva

entry.summary: Reduces adversarial robustness certification for MLP classifiers to a lattice-traversal problem over axis-aligned interval regions, giving both sound and complete certifications. It offers a rigorous theoretical framing of certified robustness.

entry.title: Director: Accelerating Distributed MoE Serving via Online Proactive Expert Placement

author.name: Qianli Liu, Kaibin Guo, Zicong Hong, Peng Li, Fahao Chen, Haodong Wang, Jian Lin and Song Guo

entry.summary: Director is a distributed MoE serving system that proactively places experts online to minimize latency under rapidly changing request patterns, rather than relying on past activation history. It tackles expert-migration cost and NP-hard placement complexity.

entry.title: LieBN: Batch Normalization over Lie Groups

author.name: Ziheng Chen, Yue Song, Rui Wang, Xiao-Jun Wu, and Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: LieBN generalizes batch normalization to Lie groups using left- and right-invariant metrics that naturally exist on any Lie group, with theoretical guarantees on controlling Riemannian mean and variance. It provides normalization for manifold-valued deep networks.

entry.title: Vision Transformers Learn Gestalt-Like Figure-Ground Cues from Natural Images

author.name: Matthias Tangemann, Benjamin Lo, Zygmunt Pizlo, Kaleem Siddiqi, Dirk B. Walther, Sven Dickinson

entry.summary: Tests 25 Vision Transformers with linear probes and finds they learn Gestalt-like figure-ground cues such as surroundedness, convexity, and symmetry from natural images. It positions ViTs as tractable models for studying human figure-ground organization.

entry.title: CLAP: Direct VLM-to-VLA Adaptation via Language-Action Grounding

author.name: Yuri Ishitoya, Jeremy Siburian, Masashi Hamaya, Kuniaki Saito, Cristian C. Beltran-Hernandez, Mai Nishimura

entry.summary: CLAP directly adapts pretrained VLMs into vision-language-action models with minimal architectural change by prepending action sequences with a causal language-action prompt to avoid output-distribution mismatch. This offers a transparent path to studying how VLM capabilities transfer to control across scales.

entry.title: C-GAP: Class-Aware and Online Prompting Improves Vision-Language Models on Imbalanced Classes

author.name: Francis Fernandez, Arash Jahangiri, Salimeh Sekeh

entry.summary: C-GAP iteratively refines natural-language prompts fed to frozen open-vocabulary detectors to improve detection of rare or minority classes without retraining or new annotations. It targets safety-critical perception with small label spaces and class imbalance.

entry.title: Evolutionary Intelligence for Scientific Discovery: From Evolutionary Computation to Cumulative Discovery Systems

author.name: Chao Wang and Lingling Li and Fang Liu and Licheng Jiao

entry.summary: This survey introduces evolutionary intelligence as a framework linking evolutionary computation with cumulative, feedback-driven scientific discovery systems that retain experience across problems. It maps how population-based search can support autonomous open-ended exploration.

entry.title: ReGen: Hierarchical Multi-Prompt Representation Generation for Efficient Waveform Diffusion Models

author.name: Sang-Hoon Lee, Ha-Yeong Choi

entry.summary: ReGen is a hierarchical multi-prompt representation-generation framework for waveform diffusion that jointly estimates vector fields for representations and data in one model, plus a generalized flow-matching objective. It improves audio generation from highly compressed low-rate latents.

entry.title: What Pixels Are Enough? SEAMS: Sufficiency Saliency via MSE-Preservation Soft-Masks

author.name: Magdalena Tr\k{e}dowicz, {\L}ukasz Struski, Arkadiusz Lewicki, Karolina Pachota, Andrzej Grudzie\'n, Mateusz Jag{\l}a, Jacek Tabor

entry.summary: SEAMS is a sufficiency-based saliency method that directly optimizes a soft mask with a learnable budget to find the minimal image region preserving a frozen model's output, using a three-way image composite and requiring no distractor dataset or architecture-specific attribution. It applies to class probabilities, CLS embeddings, or token representations.

entry.title: Tactile and Vision Conditioned Contact-Centric Control for Whole-Arm Manipulation

author.name: Rishabh Madan, Angchen Xie, Samantha Saak, Andres Blanco, Dohyeok Lee, Sarah Grace Brown, Yunting Yan, Mark Zolotas, Jose Barreiros, Tapomayukh Bhattacharjee

entry.summary: TACTIC is a receding-horizon controller for whole-arm manipulation that distributes contact across multiple robot links using a contact-centric hybrid predictive model fusing RGB-D and distributed tactile signals. It addresses partial observation and physical inconsistency under distribution shift.

entry.title: Influence Diagnostics in High-dimensional M-estimation: Precise Asymptotics

author.name: Hugo Cui

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes the limiting distribution of leave-one-out influences for convex M-estimation under Gaussian design in the high-dimensional regime where sample size and dimension are comparable. It sharply describes how influential samples relate to the data geometry.

entry.title: Autoregressive latent diffusion for 3D molecule generation

author.name: Federico Ottomano, Gaopeng Ren, Yingzhen Li, Kim E. Jelfs, Alex M. Ganose

entry.summary: KRONOS is a latent autoregressive diffusion framework for 3D molecule generation that operates in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space, jointly modeling graph topology and geometry while supporting variable-length generation. A fill-in-the-middle-inspired mixed training strategy balances unconditional and context-conditioned generation.

entry.title: From Classification to Localization and Clinical Validation: Large-Scale Development of a Deep Learning System for Thoracic Disease Detection on Chest Radiographs in Thailand

author.name: Isarun Chamveha, Tretap Promwiset, Napat Wanchaitanawong, Trongtum Tongdee, Pairash Saiviroonporn, Warasinee Chaisangmongkon

entry.summary: This paper presents Inspectra CXR v5, a deep learning system combining a DenseNet-121 backbone with Attend-and-Compare modules and probabilistic class activation mapping for multi-label thoracic disease classification and weakly supervised lesion localization on chest radiographs. It emphasizes local adaptation to Thai populations and comprehensive clinical validation.

entry.title: Spectrally Deconfounded Gradient Boosting

author.name: Andrea Nava, Peter B\"uhlmann, Fabio Sigrist

entry.summary: This paper develops nonlinear spectral deconfounding for gradient boosting, replacing squared-error loss with a spectral loss that slows learning in confounding-aligned directions to mitigate hidden dense confounding. It shows deconfounding arises from the interaction of spectral shrinkage and regularization.

entry.title: Fully Trainable Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks and Lookup Table Networks

author.name: Wout Mommen, Lars Keuninckx, Matthias Hartmann, Werner Van Leekwijck, Piet Wambacq

entry.summary: This paper introduces a method to jointly optimize both connections and gate/lookup-table functions in deep differentiable logic gate networks and lookup table networks, using a probability distribution over candidate connections per input pin. Connection-optimized networks outperform fixed-connection baselines on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST while using far fewer gates.

entry.title: Eluna: An Agentic LLM System for Automating Warehouse Operations with Reasoning and Task Execution

author.name: Ning Liu, Kalle Kujanp\"a\"a, Zhaoxuan Zhu, P Aditya Sreekar, Kaiwen Liu, Chuanneng Sun, Jorge Marchena Menendez, Matthew Bales, Tianyu Yang, Shahnawaz Alam, Rose Yu, Baoyuan Liu, Kristina Klinkner, Shervin Malmasi

entry.summary: Eluna is a production-deployed agentic LLM system that encodes warehouse standard operating procedures as directed acyclic graphs with progressive disclosure and delegates independent tasks to parallel sub-agents with persistent code execution. It uses asymmetric episodic distillation to meet latency and accuracy needs.

entry.title: NL-PAC: Specification Ambiguity and Certified Minimax Risk Floors in LLM-Mediated Supervision

author.name: Berkay Anahtarci

entry.summary: NL-PAC formalizes learning under ambiguous natural-language specifications, showing that when multiple readings are admissible but supervision is target-blind, additional labels reduce sampling error but cannot resolve identification. It derives certified minimax risk floors for LLM-mediated supervision.

entry.title: MultiView-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for World-Centric Multi-View Integration in VLMs

author.name: Hantao Zhang, Jinru Sui, Ed Li, Dirk Bergemann, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: MultiView-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark evaluating whether VLMs can integrate observations across viewpoints into a coherent world-centric 3D mental model, decoupling object positions from transient perspectives. Frontier VLMs show consistent failures on this allocentric integration.

entry.title: Neuro-Agentic Control: A Deep Learning-based LLM-Powered Agentic AI Framework for Controlling Security Controls

author.name: Saroj Gopali, Bipin Chhetri, Deepika Giri, Sima Siami-Namini and Akbar Siami Namin

entry.summary: This framework couples an LLM planner with a time-series foundation model and a counterfactual physics-injection step to enable physics-grounded autonomous defense of industrial IoT security controls. The physics simulation aims to mitigate the safety risks of LLM hallucination in closed-loop control.

entry.title: A Personalized Computational Framework for Assessing the Sufficiency of Partially Observed Data in Healthcare AI models

author.name: Qingchu Jin, Felistas Mazhude, Jamie B. Rabb, Robert S. Kramer, Douglas B. Sawyer, Raimond L. Winslow

entry.summary: This work introduces full-feature-capacity and Feature Sufficiency Analysis to determine whether a subset of available clinical features is enough for a healthcare AI model to reach its full-feature prediction performance. It provides a personalized framework for reasoning about partially observed patient data.

entry.title: Basic Research, Lethal Effects: Military AI Research Funding as Enlistment

author.name: David Gray Widder, Sireesh Gururaja, Lucy Suchman

entry.summary: A critical policy analysis of how U.S. Department of Defense grant solicitations from 2007 to 2023 enlist academic AI researchers into warfighting agendas even under a basic-research framing. It scrutinizes the porous boundary between basic and applied military AI funding.

entry.title: Mixture of Probes: Learning from Privileged Modalities in Multimodal LLMs Through Probing

author.name: Dominick Reilly and Qiyu Wu and Hiromi Wakaki and Srijan Das and Yuki Mistufuji

entry.summary: Mixture of Probes lets multimodal LLMs learn from privileged modalities available only at training time by disentangling modality-specific and modality-general signals through probing. It preserves modality-dependent structure while transferring complementary supervision.

entry.title: TSRouter: Dynamic Modality-Model Selection for Time Series Reasoning

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Tao Feng, Dehai Min, Lu Cheng, Ge Liu, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: TSRouter dynamically selects the best modality and model for time-series reasoning, exploiting that LLMs preserve numerical detail while VLMs capture global visual patterns. It models interactions among tasks, queries, modalities, and models to route each query cost-effectively.

entry.title: Training, Reading, and Editing Legible Transformers

author.name: Mark Oskin

entry.summary: Explores building transformers from legible, bounded operators that read as fuzzy set operations, identifying a failure mode where a crispness penalty collapses detectors into dead constants. It introduces a per-channel variance floor and a learned per-unit fraction to recover both legibility and quality.

entry.title: The Patchwork Problem in LLM-Generated Code

author.name: Viraaji Mothukuri, Reza M. Parizi

entry.summary: Identifies the patchwork problem where LLM-generated code is locally valid but globally incoherent, referencing undeclared configs, nonexistent packages, or missing auth guards that CI rarely catches. It formalizes structural coherence as consistency invariants over graph representations of repository artifacts.

entry.title: A Formalization of the Mean-Field Derivation of the Vlasov Equation: AI-Assisted Lean Formalization as a Strategy Game

author.name: Joseph K. Miller

entry.summary: Formalizes a research-level mean-field derivation of the nonlinear Vlasov equation in Lean 4 by a mathematician directing an AI system, framing the effort as a formalization game won when the proof compiles axiom-clean with no gaps. It also introduces a reuse criterion for absorbing the development into general libraries.

entry.title: Model Agnostic Graph Prompt Learning for Crystal Property Prediction

author.name: Shrimon Mukherjee, Kishalay Das, Partha Basuchowdhuri, Pawan Goyal, Niloy Ganguly

entry.summary: The paper proposes multilevel node- and graph-level soft prompt learning to inject latent features into graph neural networks for crystal property prediction without hand-engineering domain descriptors. It aims to reduce reliance on domain expertise and model size.

entry.title: Toward Active Object Detection for UAVs in the Wild: A Large-Scale Dataset, Benchmark and Method

author.name: Tianpeng Liu, Xinhua Jiang, Li Liu, Qinmu Shen, Siwei Tang, Zhen Liu, Yongxiang Liu

entry.summary: EvoLP is a self-evolving latency predictor for edge devices that improves accuracy during the model-compression process, avoiding expensive on-device measurement. It reportedly outperforms prior predictors across three devices and multiple model variants.

entry.title: Adaptive Latent Trajectory Anchoring for Action Segmentation Dataset Condensation

author.name: Artheme Gauthier-Villar, Guodong Ding, Angela Yao

entry.summary: This paper reframes action-segmentation dataset condensation as deterministic latent mapping using denoising diffusion implicit models, representing action segments as trajectories anchored by sparse latent points with adaptive budget allocation. It replaces expensive VAE-based iterative inversion.

entry.title: Subtoken Vision Transformer for Fine-grained Recognition

author.name: Jie Zhu, Ivy Zhang, Minchul Kim, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: SubViT selectively tokenizes discriminative image patches into multiple subtokens while keeping the standard token sequence for global context, allocating extra capacity to regions that matter for fine-grained recognition. A two-stage training strategy avoids extra inference-time attention extraction.

entry.title: EXHOLD: Experience-Aware Real-Time Hold Control for Large-Scale Ride-Hailing Matching at DiDi

author.name: Xu Liu, Kai Wan, Zihao Lu

entry.summary: EXHOLD is a deployable two-stage framework for ride-hailing hold control at DiDi that separates experience-aware assessment of driver-order pairs into interpretable tiers from hold-time execution. It aims to replace brittle heuristic thresholding under non-stationary traffic.

entry.title: Equivariant Filter for High Performance Image Tracking using an Event Camera

author.name: Angus Apps, Yixiao Ge, Timothy L. Molloy, Robert Mahony

entry.summary: This paper presents an equivariant filter for high-performance planar image tracking using an event camera, exploiting SE(2) symmetry and an asynchronous event-blob tracker to estimate affine translation and rotation. It leverages group structure for principled state estimation from event streams.

entry.title: Vascular Geometry Characterization for AI-Based Endovascular Navigation

author.name: Han-Ru Wu, Harry Robertshaw, Lisa Dwyer-Joyce, Thomas C Booth, Alejandro Granados

entry.summary: This study characterizes vascular geometry metrics associated with endovascular navigation difficulty and builds an automated pipeline for quantitative vascular feature extraction from CT angiograms of 61 patients. It aims to enable complexity grading for training and evaluating RL-based navigation.

entry.title: Control Laguerre Tessellation: Semi-discrete Optimal Transport Over Control Systems

author.name: Ripon C. Sarker, Abhishek Halder

entry.summary: This paper develops Control Laguerre Tessellation, a control-theoretic generalization of Laguerre tessellations for semi-discrete optimal transport where the ground cost is the optimal control cost of moving agents. Under a twist condition, the optimal transport map is a tessellation, illustrated for minimum-energy and minimum-time linear agents.

entry.title: Generative Communications: Overview, Technologies, and Trends

author.name: Wenjun Zhang, Zhiyong Chen, Tong Wu, Guo Lu, Li Song, Feng Yang, and Meixia Tao

entry.summary: This article introduces generative communications as a 6G paradigm where large AI models drive semantic understanding and content generation so transmitters send minimal information and receivers synthesize output from shared generative priors. It reframes communication as controlled generation rather than bit-accurate reproduction.

entry.title: Super-Tuning: From Activation-Aware Pruning to Sparse Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ivan Ilin, Philip Zmushko, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: Super repurposes pruning saliency signals (Wanda-style activation-weighted magnitude) to select a sparse trainable support for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and Supra hybridizes this sparse update with LoRA under a matched parameter budget. Arithmetic experiments on Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3-8B show top accuracy for the best variants.

entry.title: Risk-Aware General-Utility Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Pedro P. Santos, F\'abio Vital, Alberto Sardinha, Francisco S. Melo

entry.summary: This paper studies risk-aware general-utility Markov decision processes, where objectives depend on state-visitation frequencies, focusing on the entropic risk measure to trade off expected performance against risk aversion. It proposes an MCTS-based online planning approach to solve them.

entry.title: Shortcut Trajectory Planning for Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guanquan Wang, Yoshimasa Tsuruoka

entry.summary: Shortcut Trajectory Planning is an offline model-based RL framework that uses shortcut models as efficient one-step or few-step trajectory generators, trained in a single stage with step-size conditioning to avoid costly teacher-student distillation. It selects plans using a feasibility-aware corrected critic.

entry.title: Similarity search generalisation in contrastive learning with InfoNCE loss

author.name: Nick Whiteley

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows the InfoNCE population risk with k negatives is O(1/k) close to an expected cross-entropy quantifying deviation between softmax similarity search on unseen data and an idealized search using the positive-sample generator. It complements mutual-information and alignment-uniformity interpretations and introduces a continuity bound for generalization.

entry.title: Active rejection enables reliable generalization of universal machine-learning interatomic potentials

author.name: Mingxiang Luo, Xinnan Mao, Lu Wang, Lei Bai, Feng Ding, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes Adaptive Multi-Teacher Routing to build high-fidelity training data for universal machine-learning interatomic potentials by reformulating label construction as a structure-wise decision under uncertainty. Using a small set of real r2SCAN labels, it calibrates multiple pretrained teachers and combines descriptors, teacher identity, and disagreement to route each structure to a reliable source.

entry.title: HALO: Hybrid Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Language Models

author.name: Micah Zhang

entry.summary: HALO adds adaptive latent refinement on top of a frozen pretrained LM, applying a coarse refinement stage plus selective second-stage refinement only on tokens chosen by scoring and halting. It reports best average performance among compared methods on MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond.

entry.title: STEAM: Stable Self-Training with Elastic Matching and Adaptive Purification

author.name: Shaoxiang Wang, Kejia Zhang, Haiwei Pan, Lan Zhang

entry.summary: STEAM is an end-to-end unsupervised cross-view geo-localization framework matching drone and satellite images via stable spatial-aware modules, elastic matching, and adaptive pseudo-label purification. It avoids costly annotation and mitigates noisy pseudo-label accumulation.

entry.title: PRecG: Legal Precedent Retrieval with Graph Neural Networks and Rhetorical Role Segmentation

author.name: Devanshu Verma, Vasudha Bhatnagar, Vikas Kumar, Balaji Ganesan

entry.summary: PRecG retrieves legal precedents by hierarchically learning judgment representations with graph neural networks and rhetorical-role segmentation, capturing how legal entities shift meaning by their rhetorical role. It moves beyond treating legal documents as monolithic text.

entry.title: Implicit-Behavior Coordination from Unlabeled Sub-Task Demonstrations for Rearrangement Tasks

author.name: Ahmed Shokry, Usama Ahmed Siddiquie, Sicong Pan, Maren Bennewitz

entry.summary: This work formulates long-horizon robotic rearrangement as implicit-behavior coordination learned from unlabeled mixed-behavior demonstrations, avoiding predefined skills, labels, or switching logic. Behaviors are coordinated through value-guided action selection and evaluated in Habitat.

entry.title: 6 months to live for open models

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: This policy-focused post argues that open-weight AI models face an unprecedented regulatory threat, pointing to reported White House discussions of an executive order that could restrict Chinese-origin models and government uses. The author frames this as the most serious real-world test yet of open-source AI viability and ties it to recent model licensing negotiations.

entry.title: GraphSeg: Segmented 3D Representations via Graph Edge Addition and Contraction

author.name: Haozhan Tang, Tianyi Zhang, Oliver Kroemer, Matthew Johnson-Roberson, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: GraphSeg produces consistent 3D object segmentations from sparse 2D images without depth by building dual correspondence graphs and using graph edge addition and contraction. It addresses over-segmentation and cross-view inconsistency of 2D models like SAM in 3D robotics settings.

entry.title: Ground-Truthing AI Energy Consumption: Validating CodeCarbon Against External Measurements

author.name: Raphael Fischer

entry.summary: Validates software-based AI energy estimators like CodeCarbon against external ground-truth power measurements across hundreds of experiments, quantifying where static and dynamic estimation assumptions break down. It matters for credible carbon accounting in ML.

entry.title: SplatCtrl: Perception-Action Coupling via Gaussian Scene Representations and Reactive Robot Control

author.name: Siddarth Jain, Ho Jin Choi

entry.summary: SplatCtrl couples real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting scene reconstruction from RGB-D with reactive robot control, deriving continuous signed distance functions from isotropic Gaussians for differentiable collision estimates. It enables collision-free arm control in dynamic, previously unseen environments.

entry.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Partially Observed Actions

author.name: Gautam Dasarathy, Vineet Gattani, Lalit Jain

entry.summary: Studies stochastic linear bandits where only a random subset of each action vector coordinates is observed, showing sublinear regret is generally impossible but achievable when actions have low intrinsic dimension. The TOFU-POV algorithm estimates the latent subspace from masked actions.

entry.title: Integrating Large Language Models and Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Image Classification

author.name: Camila Piscioneri Magalh\~aes and Lucas Pascotti Valem

entry.summary: This work integrates LLM-derived textual descriptions with graph convolutional networks to improve graph construction for semi-supervised image classification, moving beyond similarity graphs from visual features alone. LLM knowledge augments the structural representation of visual data.

entry.title: TSR-Ego: Temporally Guided Stereo Refinement Framework for Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Md Mushfiqur Azam, John Quarles, Kevin Desai

entry.summary: TSR-Ego is a temporally guided stereo refinement framework for egocentric 3D human pose estimation from head-mounted fisheye cameras, enriching stereo features with causal temporal convolution and projection-guided sampling. It improves robustness when current-frame stereo cues are occluded or ambiguous.

entry.title: HiHR: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification

author.name: Qiwei Yang and Pingping Zhang

entry.summary: HiHR is a hierarchical hyperbolic representation framework for aerial-ground person re-identification that fuses multi-granularity vision-text features and builds a hierarchical feature structure in hyperbolic space to preserve view-specific cues. It avoids the pitfalls of direct cross-view feature alignment.

entry.title: YeTI: You Only Need Two Noisy Images for Real-World sRGB Noise Generation

author.name: Jaekyun Ko, Byung Wan Lim, Soomin Lee, Dongjin Kim, Tae Hyun Kim

entry.summary: YeTI is a framework for synthesizing realistic sRGB sensor noise using only two noisy observations of the same scene, avoiding the need for clean ground truth or camera metadata. It disentangles scene structure from noise via a reconstruction autoencoder and models the noise distribution with a one-step conditional diffusion transformer, supporting scalable denoiser training.

entry.title: Robot Trajectron V3: A Probabilistic Shared Control Framework for SE(3) Manipulation

author.name: Pinhao Song, Zhongxi Li, Ze Fu, Federico Ulloa Rios, Renaud Detry

entry.summary: Robot Trajectron V3 is a probabilistic shared-control framework for SE(3) grasping that formulates teleoperation as Bayesian inference, learning a transformer-based prior over user intent from point clouds and candidate grasps and combining it with real-time commands. It reduces cognitive load for high-DoF manipulation over low-bandwidth interfaces.

entry.title: Dynamic Inverse Rendering for Enhanced Material-Lighting Decomposition

author.name: Raza Yunus, Benjamin Ummenhofer, Jan Eric Lenssen, Eddy Ilg

entry.summary: This work resolves the material-lighting ambiguity in inverse rendering by reconstructing rigidly moving objects, which provide diverse light-surface interactions that constrain the decomposition. It marries object tracking and reconstruction with inverse rendering for general rigid motion.

entry.title: PhysV2A: Reachability-Gated and Semantic-Mask-Constrained Feasibility Completion for Video-to-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Haohui Huang, Junda Duan, Tao Teng, and Chenguang Yang

entry.summary: PhysV2A converts embodiment-agnostic video-derived 6D object motion into robot-executable trajectories via reachability-gated, semantic-mask-constrained feasibility completion, treating grasp feasibility as trajectory-conditioned rather than local. It couples each grasp candidate rigidly with recovered object motion for hierarchical feasible selection.

entry.title: Action-Factored Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Scalable Quantum Device Tuning

author.name: Edwin De Nicolo, Rahul Marchand, Cornelius Carlsson, Pranav Vaidhyanathan and Natalia Ares

entry.summary: QADAPT is a cooperative multi-agent RL framework for scalable quantum-dot device tuning that uses an online-learned factored action representation to decouple agents and reduce interference from parameter cross-talk. It achieves zero-shot generalization to unseen device sizes with roughly constant learning cost.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Vision-Language Adaptation with Continuous Metadata Conditioning for Animal Re-Identification

author.name: Anil Osman Tur and Tonje Knutsen Sordalen and Kim Tallaksen Halvorsen and Cigdem Beyan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how Bayesian causal discovery behaves under latent confounding in linear Gaussian models, deriving a critical correlation threshold above which the score favors a spurious edge between two confounded variables. It shows this threshold decreases with sample size, so more data increases the risk of confidently inferring the wrong structure.

entry.title: Robustifying Vision-Language Models via Test-Time Prompt Adaptation

author.name: Xingyu Zhu, Huanshen Wu, Shuo Wang, Beier Zhu, Jiannan Ge, Jiaheng Zhang, Long Chen

entry.summary: RITA is a robust test-time prompt-adaptation framework for vision-language models that shifts from sample-level confidence heuristics to leveraging the distributional structure of augmented views, based on the observation that adversarial distortion is structurally brittle while semantic integrity persists across augmentations. It aims to preserve CLIP's zero-shot robustness under adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: SolarChain-Eval: A Physics-Constrained Benchmark for Trustworthy Economic Agents in Decentralized Energy Markets

author.name: Shilin Ou, Yifan Xu, Luyao Zhang

entry.summary: SolarChain-Eval is a physics-constrained benchmark that casts decentralized energy-market governance as a Gymnasium MDP to evaluate autonomous economic agents across utility, physical safety, fairness, and auditability. It probes whether agents exploit invalid physical data or create artificial liquidity.

entry.title: iLENS: Interpretable LLM-Guided Mixture-of-Experts for Neuroimaging Survival Analysis

author.name: Farica Zhuang, Seong Woo Han, Zixuan Wen, Shu Yang, Yize Zhao, Li Shen

entry.summary: iLENS uses an LLM to synthesize structured neuroimaging measures and unstructured text to guide mixture-of-experts routing for Alzheimer conversion survival prediction. It aims to add interpretability and language reasoning to otherwise static risk models.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Evolutionary Generation of Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization Algorithms

author.name: Georgios Laskaris, Reuben Brasher, Niki van Stein, Elena Raponi, Thomas B\"ack, Florian Neukart

entry.summary: Extends the LLaMEA framework to multi-objective Bayesian optimization, using LLMs as mutation and crossover operators within evolutionary strategies to generate full algorithm implementations, with integrated hyperparameter tuning. Roughly 900 generated algorithms are benchmarked against a strong baseline.

entry.title: Nonconvex Composite Functional Constraints via First-Order Augmented Lagrangian Methods under Local Regularity

author.name: Linglingzhi Zhu, Jiajin Li

entry.summary: Analyzes nonasymptotic convergence of first-order augmented Lagrangian methods for nonconvex composite functional-constrained optimization, using a smoothed prox-linear approach under local regularity. It provides a finite-time mechanism converting truncated minimax stationarity into KKT guarantees.

entry.title: Optimal Top-$k$ Identification from Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Motti Goldberger, Nils Rudi

entry.summary: Studies fixed-confidence top-k identification from noisy pairwise comparisons, aiming for asymptotically optimal expected sample complexity matching the information-theoretic lower bound. It advances pure-exploration bandit theory for ranking-style problems.

entry.title: SCATE: Learning to Supervise Coding Agents for Cost-Effective Test Generation

author.name: Sijia Gu, Noor Nashid, Ali Mesbah

entry.summary: StereoSplat+ reconstructs render-ready 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from a single stereo pair using a feed-forward network enhanced with diffusion-assisted progressive inference to fill occlusions and missing geometry. It targets on-device robotics and AR where multi-view capture is unavailable.

entry.title: AlphaZero in Sparsely Rewarded Games: Limits and Auxiliary Supervision

author.name: Brent Kong, Tejas Ram, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: Examines AlphaZero limits in sparsely rewarded games, comparing vanilla, multi-frame, and auxiliary-loss variants in Connect Four and Chomp, and finds strong play does not guarantee optimal play. Oracle-derived auxiliary policy supervision helps preserve exact optimal trajectories.

entry.title: Residual Physics-Informed Neural Networks for High-Fidelity BLDC Motor Modeling

author.name: Haitham El-Hussieny

entry.summary: This paper presents a physics-informed residual network that learns a continuous-time surrogate of full six-state BLDC motor dynamics, predicting angle, velocity, currents, and temperature while satisfying electromechanical and thermal ODEs. Curriculum-scheduled physics penalties enable fast training.

entry.title: Complexity-Guided Component-wise Initialization for Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Konstantin Garbers, Nicholas Oh

entry.summary: The authors analyze recurring spectral patterns across eleven GPT-2-style checkpoints and test whether these patterns can be reused as an initialization signal for pretraining. They construct initialization schemes mimicking component-wise magnitudes and spectral profiles of trained models.

entry.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting under Distribution Shifts: A Synthetic Evaluation

author.name: Konrad \"Ozdemir, Julia Gastinger, Lukas Kirchdorfer, Heiner Stuckenschmidt

entry.summary: This paper studies temporal knowledge graph forecasting robustness under controlled distribution shifts using a synthetic generator encoding recurrence, homophily, and periodicity. Evaluating seven architectures, it finds robustness is highly signal-dependent.

entry.title: CogniConsole: Externalizing Inference-Time Control as a Formal Abstraction for Reliable LLM Interactions

author.name: Vanessa Figueiredo and Wilter Franceschi

entry.summary: CogniConsole argues LLM reliability depends heavily on inference-time control, externalizing task framing and context selection into a structured interface. Controlled probes with 489 trials show more structural scaffolding systematically lowers output variance and failure rates at fixed model.

entry.title: GATS: Graph-Augmented Tree Search with Layered World Models for Efficient Agent Planning

author.name: Maureese Williams and Dymitr Nowicki

entry.summary: GATS combines UCB1-based tree search with a three-layer world model (symbolic matching, learned execution statistics, and LLM fallback) to eliminate LLM calls during agent planning inference. It reports higher success rates than LATS and ReAct on synthetic planning tasks.

entry.title: Learning-enabled Parameter Synthesis for Nonlinear Systems from Signal Temporal Logic

author.name: Alex Beaudin, Hanna Krasowski, Eric Palanques-Tost, Calin Belta, Murat Arack

entry.summary: Proposes learning-enabled parameter synthesis for nonlinear systems that provably satisfy continuous-time Signal Temporal Logic specifications under uncertain initial conditions, combining gradient-based optimization with set-based reachability verification. It scales to up to 18 parameter dimensions.

entry.title: A Coreset Selection Framework with Ensemble Aggregation for Image Classification

author.name: Pedro Rocha Dantas and Lucas Pascotti Valem

entry.summary: This framework combines score-stratified coreset selection with ensemble aggregation over multiple training runs to select representative image-classification training subsets. It samples across score intervals and pools predictions to reduce run-to-run variance.

entry.title: Augmenting Fundamental Analysis with Large Language Models: A RAG-Based System for Generating Investor Briefs

author.name: Bartosz Zi\'o{\l}ko and Kacper Dobrzeniewski

entry.summary: This study uses an LLM in a retrieval-augmented setup to generate automatic investor briefs from company reports, SEC EDGAR filings, and macroeconomic data, evaluated by nine individual investors over four weeks across nine companies. It examines LLM support for fundamental financial analysis.

entry.title: Empirical Pedestrian Safety Assessment in a Mobile Robot Using a Predictive Social Force Model

author.name: Alireza Jafari and Yun-Hao Tsai and Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces predictive social force models (PSFM and PTSFM) that integrate predicted social force vectors over a finite horizon for mobile-robot navigation among pedestrians, and evaluates them experimentally with volunteers in facing scenarios. It assesses both objective safety and subjective comfort.

entry.title: LionVote: Per-Layer Learning Rate Adaptation for Lion

author.name: Kris Atallah (New York University, New York, USA)

entry.summary: LionVote is a per-layer learning-rate mechanism for the Lion optimizer that diagnoses cross-layer-type scale disparities and adapts rates using gradient-direction stability and momentum-health signals with a validation tiebreaker. It reports modest accuracy gains on ViT-Tiny/CIFAR-100.

entry.title: Rethinking Monocular Depth Embedding for Generalized Stereo Matching

author.name: Libo Lin, Shuangli Du, Minghua Zhao, Zhenzhen You, Shun Lv, Yiguang Liu

entry.summary: This paper rethinks how monocular depth priors are embedded into stereo matching to improve generalization, reducing branch coupling to avoid shortcut learning and using soft rather than hard constraints to tolerate monocular depth errors. It targets textureless and occluded regions where stereo methods struggle.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Digital-Twin Coordination for Heterogeneous LLM Embodied Agents over Computing Power Networks

author.name: Nuocheng Yang and Sihua Wang and Zihan Chen and Tony Q. S. Quek and Changchuan Yin

entry.summary: This paper proposes communication-efficient digital-twin coordination for teams of heterogeneous LLM embodied agents over computing-power networks, replacing bandwidth-heavy multi-round natural-language dialogue that scales poorly with team size. It targets coordination quality and action delay under limited network resources.

entry.title: DKCD: Domain Knowledge-Enhanced Causal Discovery from Unstructured Data

author.name: Xin Li, Jin Li, Shoujin Wang, Kun Yu and Fang Chen

entry.summary: DKCD enhances causal discovery from unstructured data by injecting domain knowledge to better identify latent factors and produce domain-grounded factor annotations, reducing error propagation into causal graphs. It targets high-expertise domains like healthcare, finance, and education.

entry.title: Diversifying to Verify: When Task-Equivalent Programs Differ in Verifiability

author.name: Shirley Yu and Ruben Martins

entry.summary: Diversify2Verify is a staged LLM pipeline for Why3 that infers representation-specific contracts and generates diverse recursive and imperative implementations, since task-equivalent programs can differ in automated verifiability. On a new 73-task benchmark with 292 variants, verification improves from 96 to 154 artifacts after repair passes.

entry.title: Practical Source Code Recovery from Binary Functions Using Anchor-Based Retrieval and LLM Reasoning

author.name: Charles Edward Gagnon, Steven H. H. Ding, Philippe Charland, Benjamin C. M. Fung

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline for recovering source code from stripped binary functions by combining reverse engineering, anchor-based retrieval from a source database, and LLM re-ranking, rather than generating decompiled pseudocode. It extracts anchors via Ghidra, retrieves candidate files through an inverted index, and re-ranks with an LLM using disassembly and metadata.

entry.title: Bi-Manual Joint Camera Calibration and Scene Representation

author.name: Haozhan Tang, Tianyi Zhang, Matthew Johnson-Roberson, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: Bi-JCR enables marker-free joint calibration of multiple cameras across bimanual robot manipulators by leveraging 3D foundation models for dense multi-view correspondence. It simultaneously estimates camera extrinsics and a shared scene representation.

entry.title: HERO: A Heterogeneity-Aware Benchmark Library for Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Thinh T. H. Nguyen, Le-Tuan Nguyen, Minh-Duong Nguyen, Nhi Trinh, Anh Tran Nam Nguyet, Dung D. Le, Kok-Seng Wong

entry.summary: HERO is a benchmark library for federated continual learning that disentangles task split, client data split, and client task sequence, with parameters controlling data skew and task-order mismatch. It provides comparable evaluation across FCL methods on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

entry.title: GReFEM: Multimodal LLMs as Zero-Shot Semantic Assistants for Physics-Guided 3D Mesh Refinement

author.name: Kartik Bali, Mahish K. Guru, Christian J Cyron, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: GReFEM investigates whether off-the-shelf multimodal LLMs can act as zero-shot semantic proxies for physics-guided finite element mesh refinement, grounding refinement regions from geometric and physical understanding. It explores replacing iterative solvers or supervised surrogates.

entry.title: AgenticFocus: Object-Preserving Mixed Reality Synthesis from Human FPV Video for Dexterous Humanoid Learning

author.name: Iaroslav Kolomiets, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Jeffrin Sam, Dmitrii Iarchuk, Yara Mahmoud, Daniia Zinniatullina, Mikhail Konenkov and Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AgenticFocus converts ordinary first-person human videos into robot-trainable demonstrations by restoring occluded object geometry, reconstructing full-hand motion, and retargeting it to a humanoid embodiment. It yields smoother wrist motion and lower trajectory error than cross-embodiment baselines.

entry.title: Secure-by-Disguise: A Systematic Evaluation of Image Disguising for Confidential Medical Image Modeling

author.name: Jason Rojas, Jiajie He, Yash Patel, Yuechun Gu, Zeyun Yu, Keke Chen

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates image-disguising privacy methods (DisguisedNets, NeuraCrypt) for confidential cloud-based medical image modeling across classification and segmentation, assessing utility, efficiency, and reconstruction-attack robustness. It finds performance varies strongly by task.

entry.title: Adaptive MPPI with Online Disturbance Covariance Estimation: Provable Stability Tightening via Spatial Smoothing

author.name: Hyung-Jin Yoon, Hunmin Kim

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive Model Predictive Path Integral control with an online cell-wise recursive estimator for unknown spatially varying disturbance covariance, using spatial diffusion for smoothing. It proves a finite-horizon error bound and stability tightening via a dissipative diffusion operator.

entry.title: Quantum-Enhanced Synthetic Data Generation Using Quantum Circuit Born Machines for Imbalanced Tabular Learning

author.name: Tanapol Nuatho, Narisorn Sangnakara, Prapong Prechaprapranwong, Rajchawit Sarochawikasit

entry.summary: This paper uses a Quantum Circuit Born Machine to generate synthetic data for imbalanced tabular learning, exploiting superposition and entanglement to model complex distributions after PCA-based dimensionality reduction. It tests on Iris and Telco churn datasets.

entry.title: AnythingReality: Robust Online Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Open-Vocabulary VR Scene Exploration

author.name: Timofei Kozlov, Dmitrii Maliukov, Andrey Marchenko, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AnythingReality integrates online 3D Gaussian splatting, ORB-SLAM3 pose estimation, and speech-driven vision-language interaction for real-time VR exploration of noisy real-world reconstructions. It reports notable PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS gains over prior online splatting methods.

entry.title: REMIND: RE-Identification with Memory for INDoor Navigation

author.name: Pablo Diaz-Pereda, Alejandro Rodriguez-Ramos, David Perez-Saura, Pascual Campoy

entry.summary: REMIND is an online tracker for long-term re-identification of generic indoor objects from monocular RGB, handling long temporal gaps, viewpoint changes, and illumination shifts without camera pose or depth. It adds persistent memory and global identity consistency lacking in prior trackers.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Small VLMs on Multilingual Visual MCQ

author.name: Spiros Baxevanakis, Peng-Jian Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies whether test-time scaling transfers to small open vision-language models on a multilingual visual multiple-choice benchmark, comparing self-consistency, describe-then-reason with PRM-guided beam search, and post-hoc selectors on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3.5-4B. It finds that run conditions like answer parseability and decoding budget matter more than the search machinery.

entry.title: Multi-Layer Gaussian Splatting for Immersive Anatomy Visualization

author.name: Constantin Kleinbeck, Hannah Schieber, Klaus Engel, Ralf Gutjahr, Daniel Roth

entry.summary: Proposes a layered Gaussian Splatting representation of CT volumes to enable efficient, real-time immersive anatomy visualization on compute-constrained VR headsets. It targets medical education and surgical planning where full path tracing is too expensive.

entry.title: Hybrid Foveated Path Tracing with Peripheral Gaussians for Immersive Anatomy

author.name: Constantin Kleinbeck, Luisa Theelke, Hannah Schieber, Ulrich Eck, R\"udiger von Eisenhart-Rothe, Daniel Roth

entry.summary: Combines streamed foveated volumetric path tracing at the gaze center with a lightweight Gaussian Splatting approximation in the periphery for interactive, high-quality immersive anatomy rendering. It aims to balance visual fidelity and interactivity in VR.

entry.title: Decoupled Illumination Priors for Spatially Controllable Multi-View Indoor Scene Relighting

author.name: Chenjian Gao, Linning Xu, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: Lume-Palette performs spatially controllable multi-view indoor relighting by decoupling illumination distillation from a diffusion prior and explicit illumination casting from coarse 3D geometry. It targets photorealism, precise light placement, and multi-view consistency.

entry.title: Pattern-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Handling Missing Data

author.name: Minett Tran, Taehee Jeong

entry.summary: Proposes pattern-aware graph neural networks that explicitly encode missingness patterns alongside observed values, testing four encoding strategies across seven UCI datasets. It reports substantial gains over baselines that ignore informative missingness.

entry.title: Federated Low-Rank Koopman Learning for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection in IoT Systems

author.name: Tung-Anh Nguyen, Van-Phuc Bui, Anh Tuyen Le, Kim Hue Ta, Minh Thuy Le, J.Andrew Zhang, and Xiaojing Huang

entry.summary: FedKAD is a resource-efficient federated Koopman anomaly-detection framework for distributed IoT multivariate time series, learning normal dynamics via lightweight sliding-window Koopman representations instead of large neural models. Federated training is formulated as low-rank learning to save bandwidth and compute.

entry.title: Power Flow Feasibility Assessment Using Variational Graph Autoencoders

author.name: Ferran Bohigas-Daranas and Hamid Latif-Martinez and Eduardo Prieto-Araujo and Pere Barlet-Ros and Oriol Gomis-Bellmunt

entry.summary: This short paper applies a variational graph autoencoder to detect whether power-flow solutions from AI-driven solvers are feasible, validated on the IEEE 118-bus case. It targets an overlooked reliability aspect of learned power-flow methods.

entry.title: All you need is SAMPAT

author.name: Jayadeva and Madhur Aswani

entry.summary: SAMPAT is a three-layer neural architecture that provably approximates any smooth function while yielding a closed-form algebraic-analytic expression for full interpretability. It reports competitive performance on synthetic and benchmark datasets.

entry.title: Semantic Hardness Is Not Visual Hardness: Sign-Aware Hard Negative Mining for Sign Language Retrieval

author.name: Junmyeong Lee, Chan Hur, ChangSu Choi, Sukmin Cho, Fitsum Gaim, Eui Jun Hwang, Hoyun Song, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: This paper improves fine-grained sign language retrieval by introducing Sign-Aware Hard Negative Mining, which selects hard negatives based on visual confusability in the sign embedding space rather than text similarity. It argues semantic hardness differs from visual hardness and validates on PHOENIX-2014T.

entry.title: Towards Detecting Inconsistencies in End-to-end Generated TODs

author.name: Tiziano Labruna, Giovanni Bonetta, Bernardo Magnini

entry.summary: This paper detects inconsistencies in end-to-end generated task-oriented dialogues by conceptualizing them as a constraint satisfaction problem, where dialogue segments are variables and constraints capture properties like adherence to a knowledge base. It targets hallucinations such as suggesting non-existent entities.

entry.title: CtrlVTON: Controllable Virtual Try-On via Visual-Instance-Prompt Segmentation

author.name: Seungyong Lee, Hyun Jun Jang, Sangoh Kim, and Sungjoon Park

entry.summary: CtrlVTON adds user control over how garments are worn (fit, style, placement) in virtual try-on by recasting it as image editing with segmentation-mask conditioning, and introduces VIP-SAM for instance-level garment segmentation from a flatlay image. It distinguishes instance-level from category-level segmentation.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Scalable and Transferable Node Centrality Approximation

author.name: Samra Sana, Giorgio Mantica, Saul Imbrici

entry.summary: This paper uses graph neural networks to approximate betweenness and closeness centrality as a node-ranking problem, evaluating transferability across topologies with Kendall's tau. It reports strong rank correlations, including tau=0.938 for a large betweenness model trained on 5,000-node graphs.

entry.title: Fictional Worldbuilding: Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration with Hierarchical Context Compression and Iterative Review

author.name: Jingbo Chen, He Wang, Wei Yuan, Yuqiao Lai, Zhenyan Lu

entry.summary: AutoWorldBuilder is a multi-agent LLM system for constructing coherent fictional worlds, addressing context explosion, creativity-consistency tension, and quality assurance via a structured concept network with conflict detection, a DAG-based batch scheduler, and a four-layer context compression achieving about 90% token reduction. It targets game design and literary creation.

entry.title: Multimodal Scenario Similarity Search for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tam\'as Matuszka, Andr\'as Tam\'asy, Bal\'azs Szol\'ar

entry.summary: This paper presents a multimodal framework for autonomous-driving scenario retrieval that unifies visual and trajectory-based representations, comparing an explicit surrounding-agent motion matcher (Exo-Trajectory) with a contrastively learned transformer (ScenarioFormer). It clarifies the relative strengths of visual versus motion descriptions for finding similar scenarios.

entry.title: TextileNet: Towards Zero-shot Text-style Segmentation of Manuscripts

author.name: Anguelos Nicolaou, Antonella Ambrosio, Desiree Di Donato, Georg Vogeler

entry.summary: TextileNet is a fully convolutional multi-task network trained only on synthetic data to produce dense pixel-level texture embeddings, transferred zero-shot to historical manuscript script-style discrimination. The authors also establish a human baseline via a paleographic visual quiz spanning lay participants to expert paleographers.

entry.title: Creativity, honesty and designed forgetting emerge in small hyperbolic language models

author.name: Kwan Soo Shin and In Seok Kang and Yunkyung Min

entry.summary: This paper studies three small hyperbolic-substrate language models (146M-3B) as companion agents, training a 146M behavioral auditor that detects compliance gaps human raters cannot agree on and a linear readout that flags companion-induced sycophancy. It frames creativity, honesty, and designed forgetting as emergent, auditable companion traits.

entry.title: Programming-by-Example for Batch-Editing Collision Meshes in 3D Software

author.name: Gengyang Xu, Dongwei Xiao, Hengcheng Zhu, Yiteng Peng, Wei Meng, Shuai Wang, and Shing-Chi Cheung

entry.summary: Formulates batch-editing of collision meshes in 3D software as a programming-by-example problem and uses neuro-symbolic program synthesis to generalize an edit intent across many heterogeneous meshes. It reduces tedious manual collision-mesh editing.

entry.title: FairSelect: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Level and Intersectional Algorithmic Fairness
